items.title: بسبب هند رجب.. نجم السلة الأمريكي إيرفينغ يهاجم "إي إس بي إن"
items.summary: وجّه نجم السلة الأمريكي كايري إيرفينغ انتقادات إلى شبكة "إي إس بي إن" بعد تغريم لاعب كرة القدم عزيز الشاعر لكتابته اسم الطفلة الفلسطينية هند رجب أسفل عينيه خلال مباراة.
items.body_text:
بسبب هند رجب.. نجم السلة الأمريكي إيرفينغ يهاجم "إي إس بي إن"
صعّد نجم كرة السلة الأمريكي كايري إيرفينغ موقفه الداعم للاعب فريق "هيوستن تكسانز" عزيز الشاعر، فبعد إعلانه استعداده لدفع الغرامة المفروضة عليه لكتابته اسم الطفلة الفلسطينية هند رجب أسفل عينيه خلال مباراة، وجّه انتقادات إلى شبكة "إي إس بي إن" (ESPN) الرياضية بسبب طريقة تناولها القضية.
ورد إيرفينغ على منشور للشبكة عبر منصة "إكس"، قائلا: "اسمها هند رجب، وكانت أشجع من كل واحد منكم في إي إس بي إن"، في تغريدة حصدت قرابة 5 ملايين مشاهدة حتى كتابة التقرير.
وجاء انتقاد إيرفينغ بعدما نشرت الشبكة تقريرا عن عرضه دفع الغرامة المالية المفروضة على الشاعر من دون ذكر اسم هند رجب، وهو ما أشار إليه إيرفينغ في رده على المنشور.
غرامة بسبب تكريم هند رجب
وفرضت رابطة دوري كرة القدم الأمريكية "إن إف إل" (NFL)، الأربعاء، غرامة قدرها 11 ألفا و941 دولارا على الشاعر، بسبب ما اعتبرته مخالفة لقواعد معدات وملابس اللاعبين، خلال مباراة فريقه أمام "بافالو بيلز" الأسبوع الماضي.
وكان الشاعر، البالغ من العمر 29 عاما، قد كتب اسم هند رجب على المنطقة أسفل عينيه، وهي مساحة يستخدمها لاعبو كرة القدم الأمريكية عادة لوضع الطلاء أو الملصقات للحد من انعكاس الضوء.
قصص مقترحة
list of 2 items
وبعد انتشار خبر الغرامة، أعلن إيرفينغ استعداده لتحمل قيمتها، وكتب عبر منصة "إكس": "سأتكفل بغرامته"، قبل أن يعود ويوجّه انتقاده إلى "إي إس بي إن" بسبب طريقة تناولها القضية.
ولم يتوقف موقف إيرفينغ عند التكفل بالغرامة؛ إذ أعاد تسليط الضوء على اسم هند رجب، محولا منشوره إلى محور جديد للنقاش حول حضور القضية الفلسطينية في المشهد الرياضي والإعلامي الأمريكي.
إشادة على المنصات
وحظي موقف إيرفينغ بتفاعل واسع على مواقع التواصل، حيث أشاد ناشطون ومدونون بإقدامه على استخدام شهرته الرياضية للحديث عن قصة هند رجب ودعم الشاعر.
وقال الناشط كول هاند لونغ هورن إنه يقف إلى جانب إيرفينغ والشاعر، وإلى جانب "جميع الأرواح البشرية التي يدافعون عنها".
كما علّقت الكاتبة والناشطة الأمريكية سمر دهمش على موقف إيرفينغ، معتبرة أن تغريدته أعادت اسم هند رجب إلى الواجهة، وكتبت أن الطفلة الفلسطينية واجهت ظروفا قاسية بشجاعة، منتقدة في الوقت نفسه طريقة تناول مؤسسة إعلامية كبرى للقضية.
واستعاد ناشطون ومدونون تفاصيل قصة هند رجب، مشيرين إلى أنها كانت في السادسة من عمرها عندما علقت داخل سيارة في غزة، وتحدثت هاتفيا مع فرق الإسعاف أثناء محاولات الوصول إليها.
وفي تعليقات أخرى، وصف مؤيدون إيرفينغ بأنه من أبرز لاعبي دوري كرة السلة الأمريكي للمحترفين الذين يتحدثون علنا عن القضية الفلسطينية، وأشادوا باستعداده لدفع الغرامة.
وكتب أحد المعلقين: "أنت أسطورة يا بطل فلسطين حرة"، بينما وصفه آخرون بأنه "صوت لمن لا صوت لهم"، معتبرين أن شهرته الرياضية تمنحه مساحة واسعة للتعبير عن مواقفه.
كما تضمنت بعض التعليقات مواقف سياسية حادة تجاه إسرائيل، وربطت بين قصة هند رجب والحرب على غزة.
مواقف سابقة لعزيز الشاعر
ولا تُعَد هذه المرة الأولى التي يواجه فيها عزيز الشاعر عقوبة على خلفية تعبيره عن موقف مرتبط بالحرب على غزة.
ففي يناير/كانون الثاني الماضي، خلال الموسم السابق من دوري كرة القدم الأمريكية، عاقبته رابطة "إن إف إل" بعدما ظهر وهو يرتدي شريطا على أنفه يحمل عبارة "أوقفوا الإبادة الجماعية"، في إشارة إلى الحرب الإسرائيلية على قطاع غزة.
وبين الغرامة الأخيرة وموقف إيرفينغ منها، عاد اسم هند رجب إلى واجهة النقاش الرياضي الأمريكي، بعدما تحول تكريم طفلة فلسطينية خلال مباراة إلى قضية تجاوزت حدود الملعب لتصل إلى الإعلام ومنصات التواصل.
يشار إلى أنه في 29 يناير/كانون الثاني 2024، وأثناء محاولة عائلة هند النزوح من منطقة تل الهوا جنوب غربي مدينة غزة، أطلقت قوات الاحتلال الإسرائيلي النار على السيارة التي كانت تقلّهم، مما أدى إلى مقتل أفراد العائلة، في حين نجت هند مؤقتا وبقيت عالقة داخل السيارة.
وفي أثناء محاصرة المركبة، أجرت هند اتصالا هاتفيا مع جمعية الهلال الأحمر الفلسطيني طالبة المساعدة، في وقت سعت فيه طواقم الإسعاف إلى الوصول إليها وسط أوضاع ميدانية بالغة الخطورة. وفي 10 فبراير/شباط 2024، وبعد انسحاب القوات الإسرائيلية من المنطقة، عُثر على جثمان هند إلى جانب جثامين أفراد عائلتها، إضافة إلى المسعفين اللذين توجها لإنقاذها، واللذين قُتلا أثناء أداء واجبهما الإنساني.

items.title: Iran expels Swedish diplomat after Stockholm ousts its embassy staffer
items.summary: Iran on Thursday ordered a Swedish diplomat to leave the country within 48 hours in response to Sweden's expulsion of an official at the Iranian embassy in Stockholm, while rejecting Sweden's accusations against Tehran as "baseless."
items.body_text:
By continuing to browse our site you agree to our use of cookies, revised Privacy Policy and Terms of Use. You can change your cookie settings through your browser.

The city view of Tehran. /VCG
        Iran on Thursday ordered a Swedish diplomat to leave the country within 48 hours in response to Sweden's expulsion of an official at the Iranian embassy in Stockholm, while rejecting Sweden's accusations against Tehran as "baseless."
Iran's Foreign Ministry said in a statement that Alireza Yousefi, director general for Western Europe at the ministry, summoned the Swedish ambassador to Iran on Thursday morning and lodged a strong protest against Sweden's "destructive" policies, particularly its "inappropriate rhetoric about Iran and hosting of anti-Iran terrorist groups and individuals."
During the meeting, the Swedish ambassador was informed that a Swedish diplomat had been ordered to leave Iran within 48 hours "due to reasons that were explained to the ambassador," the statement said.
Sweden's Foreign Ministry said on Wednesday that it had summoned Iran's ambassador and asked an official at the Iranian embassy to leave the country over activities "not compatible with the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations."
Swedish Justice Minister Gunnar Strommer later told state broadcaster SVT that the decision was made over Iran's alleged activities against "Jewish and Israeli interests" in Sweden.
Iran's Foreign Ministry rejected Sweden's claims, saying Stockholm had "in an unjustified move that is in violation of international law, compelled a diplomat serving at Iran's embassy in Stockholm to leave the country without any justified reason."
It added that Sweden's action was taken under Israel's influence and constitutes an attempt to disrupt the normal operations of the Iranian embassy in Stockholm.
The ministry said Iran would adopt necessary measures to protect its national rights and interests, including through reciprocal actions.
                Source(s): Xinhua News Agency

items.summary: Chinese Defense Minister Dong Jun held talks with visiting Lao Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Defense Khamlieng Outhakaysone in Beijing on Monday.
items.body_text:
By continuing to browse our site you agree to our use of cookies, revised Privacy Policy and Terms of Use. You can change your cookie settings through your browser.

Chinese Defense Minister Dong Jun held talks with visiting Lao Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Defense Khamlieng Outhakaysone in Beijing on Monday.
Dong said the Chinese military is ready to work with the Lao military to further strengthen high-level exchanges, enhance the quality and efficiency of practical cooperation in various fields, provide strong support for building an all-weather China-Laos community with a shared future in the new era, and safeguard regional stability.
Khamlieng Outhakaysone said the Lao side is willing to strengthen high-level communication and exchanges at various levels between the two militaries and promote practical cooperation across various fields to achieve more outcomes.
This year marks the 65th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between China and Laos.
Since September 7, the Chinese and Lao militaries have been conducting a joint military exercise in Vientiane, Laos, codenamed "Peace Train-2026," focusing on humanitarian assistance and medical services. The exercise is scheduled to run through late September, making it the sixth joint exercise of its kind between the two militaries since 2017.

items.title: South Africa's Ramaphosa urges BRICS to defend multilateralism
items.summary: Ramaphosa said South Africa advocated a predictable global system based on international law, with the UN Charter at its center, adding that an order founded on the sovereign equality of states, territorial integrity and political independence would benefit all nations, large and small.
items.body_text:
By continuing to browse our site you agree to our use of cookies, revised Privacy Policy and Terms of Use. You can change your cookie settings through your browser.
                            
                            I agree
                        
                    
                        Africa
                    
                    
    16:03, 13-Sep-2026
                    
                
                CGTN
                    
                    Africa;
                
            Cyril Ramaphosa, South Africa's president, arrives for a meeting with Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, Brazil's president, not pictured, at Planalto Palace in Brasilia, Brazil, on Monday, March 9, 2026. /CFP
        South African President Cyril Ramaphosa on Saturday called on BRICS countries to strengthen multilateralism and push for global governance reform, saying the voices of Africa and the Global South must be fully reflected in shaping the future international order.
Ramaphosa made the remarks at a session during the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, India, according to a statement released by the South African Presidency.
He said the authority of the United Nations (UN) and the foundations of multilateralism were under threat as multilateral institutions and rules were being "ignored and subverted."
Ramaphosa said South Africa advocated a predictable global system based on international law, with the UN Charter at its center, adding that an order founded on the sovereign equality of states, territorial integrity and political independence would benefit all nations, large and small.
BRICS should remain a united voice for reform, demonstrate the practical results of multilateral cooperation and help shape a fairer, more accountable and development-oriented global governance system, he said.
"We must strengthen multilateralism through reform and action," Ramaphosa said. "And we must ensure that the voices of Africa and the Global South are fully reflected in shaping the future international order."

items.title: Japan's PM Takaichi reshuffles cabinet, taps first JIP member
items.summary: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi reshuffled her cabinet on Thursday, retaining most key ministers while bringing in a newcomer from the Japan Innovation Party (JIP), the junior coalition partner of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP).
items.body_text:

Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and members of her reshuffled Cabinet arrive at the prime ministerâs office in Tokyo on September 17, 2026. /VCG
        Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi reshuffled her cabinet on Thursday, retaining most key ministers while bringing in a newcomer from the Japan Innovation Party (JIP), the junior coalition partner of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP).
It is Takaichi's first cabinet reshuffle since she took office last October.
According to the new lineup, Chief Cabinet Secretary Minoru Kihara, Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi, Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi and Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama all remained in their respective posts.
Among those entering the cabinet for the first time, House of Representatives members Kazuo Yana and Yoshihiro Seki had previously been disciplined by the LDP over a high-profile political slush fund scandal. They were named agriculture minister and education minister, respectively. This marked the first time since the scandal came to light that lawmakers disciplined by the party over the affair had received cabinet positions.
Hiroshi Nakatsuka, formerly secretary general of the JIP, was appointed minister in charge of regulatory reform, making him the first JIP member to serve as a cabinet minister. The move marked a shift from the LDP and JIP cooperating outside the cabinet to cooperation within the cabinet.
Shigeaki Koga, a former official at Japan's Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry, said that on foreign and security policies, the JIP is even more hawkish than Takaichi and could potentially encourage the prime minister to pursue more hawkish policies.
Another focus of the reshuffle is the absence of former Internal Affairs and Communications Minister Yoshimasa Hayashi from the new cabinet. Hayashi was Takaichi's rival in last year's LDP presidential election.
Analysts said the personnel changes indicate, on the one hand, that the Takaichi administration will press ahead with its established military buildup, proactive fiscal policy, and diplomatic agenda.
The Takaichi government is set to revise Japan's three key security documents by the end of this year, potentially including plans to acquire large numbers of unmanned systems and move toward mass production of hypersonic missiles.
On the other hand, Takaichi's latest cabinet reshuffle is also aimed at consolidating her administration's power base and paving the way for her to secure another term as LDP president in next autumn's party leadership race.

        The 2026 Arab Media Summit, held in Dubai from September 15 to 17, attracted 250 media organizations from 23 countries, bringing together senior government officials, heads of media institutions, prominent figures and content creators.
China Media Group (CMG) participated in the summit as the sole invited Chinese media outlet.
Focusing on media transformation and the creative economy, the three-day summit featured over 175 panel discussions covering topics such as content production, globalization narratives and the impact of artificial intelligence on journalism. Through eight thematic forums, it explores how the Arab media can enhance its competitiveness by pooling ideas, experiences and practices, while fostering new opportunities for cooperation.

        As the sole invited Chinese media organization, CMG delegates engaged with participants from multiple countries and gave interviews to local media outlets.
Mohammed Al Hammadi, chairman of the UAE Journalists Association, is interviewed by CMG in Dubai, UAE, September 16, 2026. /CMG
        In an interview with CMG, Mohammed Al Hammadi, chairman of the UAE Journalists Association, stated that China's influence in the Arab region is steadily growing.
CMG's participation in the Arab Media Summit essentially represents interaction with Arab media. Both sides need communication and an understanding of each other's audiences, enabling interactive exchanges between China and the Arab world while helping the Arab world better understand China.

Chinese Vice President Han Zheng addresses the welcome banquet of the 13th Beijing Xiangshan Forum in Beijing, China, September 15, 2026. /Xinhua
        Chinese Vice President Han Zheng on Tuesday addressed the welcome banquet of the 13th Beijing Xiangshan Forum, which was attended by official representatives from nearly 100 countries, regions and international organizations.
Han said despite the complex challenges facing the world today, the trend of the times featuring peace, development, cooperation and win-win results is irresistible, and the general trend toward world multipolarity and economic globalization is irreversible.
The peoples of all countries have an ever-stronger aspiration for development and security, and their call for international fairness and justice is growing louder, he said.
Han stressed the need to uphold the purposes and principles of the UN Charter, uphold true multilateralism, resolve differences and disputes through dialogue and consultation, put people first, and ensure that technology benefits humanity.
As a responsible major country and the largest developing country, China always views its own development within the context of human development, and contributes its share to world peace, stability, development and prosperity through Chinese modernization, Han said.
He noted that over the 20 years since its founding, the Beijing Xiangshan Forum has played an important role in building consensus on security, promoting defense cooperation and safeguarding regional peace and stability.
He expressed the hope that participating guests would engage in in-depth exchanges during the forum to make new contributions to advancing international security cooperation and safeguarding world peace and stability.

items.title: U.S. failure to appoint Australian ambassador "diplomatic insult": former deputy PM
items.summary: Former Australian Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer has accused the U.S. of hitting Australia with a "diplomatic insult."
items.body_text:
CANBERRA, Jan. 3 (Xinhua) -- Former Australian Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer has accused the U.S. of hitting Australia with a "diplomatic insult."
Fischer, who served as Deputy Prime Minister from 1996 to 1999 under Australia's longest-serving Prime Minister John Howard, on Wednesday said the U.S. administration's failure to appoint an ambassador to Canberra for 18 months indicated Australia was now of "low priority."
John Berry, the former U.S. Ambassador to Australia, resigned in September 2016, leaving the post vacant ever since.
"This is now bordering on a diplomatic insult," Fischer told Fairfax Media on Wednesday. "We've been downgraded, despite all the nice noises. We are a low priority.
Fischer identified U.S. President Donald Trump's opposition to a refugee deal negotiated between his predecessor Barack Obama and Australian Prime Minister Malcolm Turnbull as a likely reason for the current administration's failure to appoint an ambassador.
It has long been speculated that Admiral Harry Harris, head of the U.S. Pacific Command, is the likely next ambassador but there has been no confirmation from the White House.
Simon Jackman, head of the United States Studies Centre at the University of Sydney, disagreed with Fischer, saying the delay showed the Trump administration was taking the appointment "extremely seriously."

items.title: South Africa freedom day memorial gathering reveals its pursuit of dignity and inclusive governance in post apartheid era
items.body_text:
IN-DEPTH / IN-DEPTH
                        South Africa freedom day memorial gathering reveals its pursuit of dignity and inclusive governance in post apartheid era
                        Politics finds its rhythm
                        
                     Editor's Note: 
In an era of profound global shifts and increasingly complex regional dynamics, a proper understanding of the world must be rooted in "grounded experience" and localized insights. Global Times English edition, in collaboration with the Academy of International and Regional Communication Studies, Communication University of China, is proud to launch "Local Insights," an English-language column dedicated to original, field-based observations.
We invite Chinese scholars and professionals who are studying, conducting exchanges, or working outside China, as well as international students and friends living and studying in China who are familiar with the social contexts of their home countries or third countries, to begin from first-hand field experience and engage with social, cultural, and contemporary issues beyond China. In the fifth article of this column, drawing on her onâtheâground experience as a Chinese exchange scholar, the author observes a South Africa Freedom Day memorial gathering, revealing how local politics unfolds through collective singing, dancing, and grassroots participation, while also reflecting on the gap between political liberation and economic justice.
As a PhD student, I am currently on an exchange program at Nelson Mandela University in South Africa, with support from the China Scholarship Council. Since arriving here, I have developed a habit of stepping beyond campus whenever possible. Community meetings, municipal events and public gatherings have become a vital way for me to engage with local life. This time, a local friend recommended that I attend a memorial event in Kariega, organized by the Congress of South African Trade Unions (COSATU) in honor of its former president, Phumzile John Gomomo. Beyond that, I had little sense of what kind of gathering I was about to enter.
It was on the way that I noticed the streets were unusually vibrant. Groups of people were dressed in colorful attire, with bright Xhosa headscarves and garments bearing political symbols. My friend then reminded me that it was April 27, which is Freedom Day in South Africa. On this day in 1994, South Africa held its first non-racial election, formally ending apartheid and inaugurating democratic rule. Over the past three decades, Freedom Day commemorates political liberation, while also inviting recurring reflection on whether the promise of freedom has been fully realized. In that sense, Freedom Day marks an important moment for observing contemporary South African politics and social sentiment.
The aerial view of Johannesburg, South Africa Photo: VCG
From street to hall: Entering Freedom Day
The event was scheduled to begin at 10 am, and we arrived shortly before the hour. Yet there were not many people present. Banners of COSATU, the South African Communist Party (SACP), and the African National Congress (ANC) had already been displayed inside the hall, quietly framing the political context of the gathering. Although my understanding was still limited, I could already sense that their presence mattered. COSATU, SACP and ANC represent key forces in South Africa's political landscape, historically linked through the "Tripartite Alliance" formed during the anti-apartheid struggle and sustained in various forms since 1994. I could see that this was not simply a local gathering, but one embedded within a much longer political tradition.
What struck me first was how different the atmosphere was from what I had expected of a political gathering. There was no sense of urgency or visible tension. items.title: China to introduce new train timetable from July 1, including high-speed train service between Beijing and Urumqi
items.body_text:
China to introduce new train timetable from July 1, including high-speed train service between Beijing and Urumqi
                        
                        
                    Passengers are pictured at the Beijing Tongzhou Railway Station in the Beijing Municipal Administrative Center in Beijing, capital of China, May 29, 2026. From 2016 to 2026, the Beijing Municipal Administrative Center marks a decade of planning and development. Over the past ten years, it has undergone a remarkable transformation into a vibrant modern area. Photo: Xinhua
China's national railway network will implement a new train-running timetable starting July 1, which will strengthen connectivity between the country's northwestern provinces and the central, southern, and southwestern regions, while also introducing high-speed train service for the first time between Urumqi, Northwest China's Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, and Beijing, the China State Railway Group announced on Wednesday.
Tickets under the new timetable went on sale on Wednesday.
The upgraded network is expected to further enhance railway transportation capacity and operational efficiency. Under the new timetable, China's national railways will operate 12,174 scheduled passenger trains, marking an increase of 106 trains compared with the current schedule.
For example, the railway authorities have arranged 58 high-speed trains from Xi'an in Northwest China's Shaanxi to destinations including Nanyang of Central China's Henan Province, Hankou of Central China's Hubei Province and Chongqing city in Southwest China.
Wan Yaqiong, director of the ticket sales workshop at Xi'an Station under China Railway Xi'an Group, said that the new timetable will introduce direct services from Xi'an to Hankou, with the fastest round-trip travel time controlled within seven hours, according to a report by the China Central Television (CCTV) News on Wednesday.
Additionally, high-speed trains will operate from Yan'an city in Shaanxi to Shaoshan city in Central China's Hunan, establishing a direct high-speed rail link between the two major "red tourism" destinations - historical sites with a modern revolutionary legacy, the CCTV News report noted.
After the timetable adjustment, high-speed trains will run for the first time between Urumqi station and Beijing West station. At the same time, the T-series trains operating between Urumqi and Chongqing West will be upgraded to Z-series direct express trains, shortening the travel time between the two places by more than two hours.
The railway authorities will increase the number of high-speed services during morning and evening rush hours on certain high-speed rail lines in the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region, the Yangtze River Delta, and the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, providing greater convenience for commuters.
Global Times

items.title: Chinese expert criticizes Filipino FM's claim that Japan-Philippines delimitation 'nothing to do' with China, warns move serves ulterior purposes beyond bilateral talks
items.body_text:
Chinese expert criticizes Filipino FMâs claim that Japan-Philippines delimitation ânothing to doâ with China, warns move serves ulterior purposes beyond bilateral talks
                        
                        
                    Philippines' Foreign Minister Maria Theresa Lazaro delivers a speech at the Nikkei Forum at a hotel in Tokyo on June 10, 2026. Photo: VCG
In response to the Philippine foreign minister's claim that its boundary discussions with Japan "have nothing to do" with China, a Chinese expert on Thursday said the soâcalled Japan-Philippines maritime delimitation talks concern an area east of China's Taiwan island and contradict international law and the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea. The expert noted the move carries ulterior purposes beyond bilateral discussions.
Philippine Secretary of Foreign Affairs Maria Theresa Lazaro said that establishing clear maritime boundaries between the Philippines and Japan is of vital importance to the country's national defense in an interview on Wednesday.
China has criticized such negotiations, while Lazaro claimed the discussion "has nothing to do with them" and "just between the Philippines and Japan." She added, "We should continue with our delimitation talks," even if China keeps objecting or increases pressure, Nikkei Asia reported.
Lazaro also expressed so-called concern over increasing activities by Chinese vessels in waters close to the Taiwan island, per the outlet.
Ding Duo, Director of the Research Center for International and Regional Issues at the National Institute for South China Sea Studies, told the Global Times on Thursday that Lazaro's words constitute three violations.
First, it violated the international law, in particular the Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties, which stipulated, in simple words, that "bilateral treaty does not create obligations or rights for a third State." If the Philippines and Japan reach any agreement regardless of China interests, that constitute a violation, Ding said.
Second, such discussions ran counter to the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, which stipulated equity in maritime boundary delimitation. Based on this principle, given that the delimitation involves China's interests, and the final decision must not bypass China, Ding added.
The expert further noted that third, in a situation that three parties interests are involved, the acts of Philippines and Japan violated the "obligation of restraint" and "principle of good faith" in international law.
Japan and the Philippines have been hyping so-called maritime delimitation issue recently, concerning an area east of China's Taiwan island. Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. agreed to start formal talks on EEZ boundaries and the continental shelf when the president visited Tokyo on a state visit in May, per reports.
In response, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said on May 29 that according to China's domestic law and international law including UNCLOS, China has exclusive economic zone and continental shelf in this area. Japan and the Philippines' so-called maritime delimitation talks constitute a severe violation of China's maritime rights and interests, UNCLOS and other international law and basic norms governing international relations. China strongly deplores and firmly opposes that and has lodged serious protests with both countries.
The so-called delimitation talks are completely illegal, null and void, and will have no effect on China's claims to rights in the area east of the Taiwan island or exercise of China's lawful rights. China urges Japan and the Philippines to immediately stop any violation of China's maritime rights and interests and take concrete actions to uphold regional peace and stability.
Ding also noted that in addition to diplomatic methods to break the Japan-Philippines collusion, China can also conduct normal maritime law enforcement, patrol

items.title: 学习手记 | “环境就是民生”
items.summary: 6月5日是世界环境日，也是我国环境保护法确立的环境日。 22年前的这一天，在时任浙江省委书记习近平部署推动下，以农村人居环境整治为重点的“千万工程”启动。 当时，习近平同志担任浙江省委书记刚半年多，工作千头万绪。他何以将农村人居环境整治作为重点工作？ 在基层调研时，习近平同志发现，在浙江经济快速发展的同时，广大农村却面临“成长的烦恼”，村庄面貌不如人意。 全省3.4万个村庄中，人居环境较好的仅4000个。有人形容：“走过一村又一村，村村都是垃圾村。”还有农民这样描述：“起早贪黑赚钞票，垃圾堆里数钞票，躺在医院花钞票。”可以说，人居环境整治是当时浙江农村群众的一个迫切期盼。 “千万工程”聚焦乡亲们走什么村道、怎么处理畜禽粪便等小问题，却直接关系农民获得感、幸福感，是实打实的民生大事。 老百姓的生活环境如何，习近平同志念兹在兹： 上世纪70年代，在陕北冯家坪公社赵家河大队驻点时，他撸起袖管，一石一瓦盖起村里第一个男女分开的厕所； 到正定工作，不仅大力推进“人拉猪吃”的“连茅圈”改造工作，还拿着大扫帚走上街头搞卫生，推动成立全县第一支专职卫生清洁队； 任福州市委书记，亲自为建造垃圾处理场选址

items.title: 刘国中在安徽调研时强调 全力以赴夺取夏粮丰收 全面打牢秋粮生产基础
items.summary: 新华社合肥6月5日电 中共中央政治局委员、国务院副总理刘国中3日至5日到安徽调研“三夏”农业生产工作。他强调，要深入学习贯彻习近平总书记关于国家粮食安全的重要论述，按照党中央、国务院部署，扛稳政治责任，毫不放松抓好夏收夏种夏管，全力以赴夺取夏粮丰收，全面打牢秋粮生产基础，确保完成全年粮食生产目标任务。 刘国中先后来到宿州市、淮南市、六安市，深入小麦机收和夏播现场、农机跨区作业服务点、农事服务中心、粮食仓储中心、地方农科院等，实地察看夏收夏种、农机作业服务保障、粮食烘干收储等工作，详细了解农作物新品种选育、大面积单产提升、农资保供稳价、高标准农田建设等情况。 刘国中强调，“三夏”工作抓得好不好，事关全年粮食生产目标任务能否顺利实现。当前正值“三夏”农业生产关键时期，要抓住有利天气抢晴收获，组织好农机跨区作业，强化服务保障和安全管理，确保夏收高效进行。要抓实抓牢机收减损、烘干晾晒等各项措施，最大程度减少粮食损失。要精心做好夏粮收购工作，引导各类企业积极入市，保障粮食市场平稳运行。要压茬推进夏播，加强农资供应和农事服务，强化技术集成及推广应用，落实落细合理密植、精量播种等大面积单产提升措施，

items.title: 韩正会见中美高级别二轨对话美方代表团
items.summary: 新华社北京6月5日电 6月5日，国家副主席韩正在北京会见中美高级别二轨对话美方代表团。 韩正表示，中美关系是当今世界最重要的双边关系之一。当前，中美关系处于关键历史节点。中美相互尊重、和平共处、合作共赢，不仅有利于两国，也有利于世界和平与发展。希望中美高级别二轨对话能不断汇聚两国有识之士的真知灼见，增进美国各界对中国的了解和理解，共同推动中美关系稳定、健康、可持续发展。 美方表示，美中高级别二轨对话有助于双方更好理解对方，为两国关系发展提供更多有益思路。中国经济发展令人钦佩，双方应加强贸易、投资等领域对话合作。

items.title: 全国人大常委会启动节约能源法执法检查
items.summary: 新华社北京6月5日电 为推动节约能源法全面有效实施，促进更高水平、更高质量做好节能工作，全国人大常委会5日启动节约能源法执法检查。 节约能源法自1998年1月1日实施，并于2007年、2016年、2018年进行了修改。 记者5日从全国人大常委会节约能源法执法检查组第一次全体会议上了解到，为全面深入了解法律实施情况，此次执法检查采取实地检查与委托检查相结合的方式，检查组将赴天津、江苏、湖南、广东、广西、四川等省（区、市）开展实地检查，并委托北京、河北、山西、吉林、上海、重庆等省（市）人大常委会对本行政区域内节约能源法实施情况进行检查。检查组将采取实地检查、听取汇报、组织座谈、典型调研、专题研究、抽查暗访等多种方式，全面准确了解法律实施情况，对带有普遍性的问题深入调查研究。 检查组将重点检查8方面内容：落实节能管理制度情况，推进重点领域节能工作情况，重点用能单位节能管理情况，推动节能技术进步情况，实施节能激励措施情况，与法律配套的行政法规、部门规章以及地方性法规的制定情况，法律实施中存在的其他问题，对节约能源法修改的意见和建议。

items.summary: 在树下院落、乡间凉亭，一场场热气腾腾的“凉亭夜话”，正悄然改变着河南省三门峡市卢氏县基层治理的面貌。从群众自发到如今党委引领下的制度化实践，“凉亭夜话”不仅成为群众表达心声的平台，也构建起基层治理的创新模式，让“小议事”撬动“大治理”。 “凉亭夜话”源于卢氏县木桐乡群众的自发行动。农闲时，村民围坐凉亭、树下，或为化解纠纷说和相劝，或为某一项目献计献策。卢氏县党委因势利导，对此进行规范化、制度化，并在全县推广。 “凉亭夜话”以开放空间为议事场景，每月至少组织一次群众议事会，激发群众参与热情。同时，明确“五议三不议”原则，划定议事边界。通过建立民情收集机制，形成“民情清单”“议事清单”，配套“四公”议事制度和闭环工作机制，加强督促督办。 2024年，“凉亭夜话”决议落实率高达92%，持续激发干部群众谋发展、干事业、促振兴的内生动力。木桐乡年投资59亿元的钼矿项目落地，创办了创业技能培训中心，打造了“灵神粉条”网红品牌，办起了位于豫陕交界地带的烤鱼店，各项产业红红火火，名列全县“十快乡镇”。全县农村党支部领办专业合作社170余家，涌现出一批集体经济收入超百万元的村。（记者 崔志坚 通讯员 刘

items.title: 北京发布14项举措保障新就业群体权益
items.summary: 本报北京6月4日电 （记者王洲）6月3日，北京市司法局、市市场监管局、市总工会联合发布14项具体举措，构建政策协同、法律服务和维权保障三位一体的制度框架保障新就业群体权益。在公共法律服务方面，北京市司法局组织市、区两级公共法律服务中心、乡镇（街道）工作站为新就业形态劳动者提供法律咨询、法律查询服务以及律师、公证、司法鉴定等法律便利服务，村（居）法律顾问也将常住新就业形态劳动者纳入服务范围；设立“城市蜂鸟”法律援助项目，为在交通事故中不负主要责任、无法认定法律援助条件的网约配送员提供公益法律服务。 同时，北京市市场监管部门将发挥网约配送行业党委作用，及时收集、反映、协调解决网约配送员的问题困难和集中诉求，协同开展“清朗网络平台算法典型问题治理”专项行动，推动平台企业落实算法安全主体责任。市总工会将规范召开企业职工代表大会，落实劳动者四项重大权益保障，开通工会法律服务绿色通道，常态化开展工会特色交通安全、职业健康专项教育。 《 人民日报 》（ 2025年06月05日 14 版）

items.title: 北京出台举措优化入境旅游服务

items.title: “阿大葱油饼”焕新记（干部状态新观察·走进一线探作风）
items.summary: “阿大葱油饼”店铺前排起长队。 受访者供图"> “阿大葱油饼”店铺前排起长队。受访者供图 下午两点，午餐时间已过，上海市静安区石门二路上，“吴根存阿大葱油饼”的招牌下还排着长长的队伍。 “阿大”吴根存在上海颇有名气。他做了30多年的葱油饼，一度是上海街头小吃中的“顶流”。直到3年前老店歇业，“阿大葱油饼”才渐渐淡出人们的视线。 年近七旬的“阿大”坐到店门口休息，厨房里忙碌的，是他的儿子吴志勇。 “想把老爸树起来的品牌再做起来，把葱油饼的手艺传承下去。”摘下帽子、口罩，脱掉围裙，吴志勇满头大汗。曾是外企员工的他，有这个念头已经许久。在上海市区多处考察后，今年4月，一家人选中了石门二路这家门面“老店新开”。 “‘阿大葱油饼’回来了！”随着刚出炉的葱油饼照片、视频在网上热传，新店门前迅速热闹了起来。顾客络绎不绝，店里只得贴出提示：每人限购5只。 生意红火令人欣喜，可没成想，紧接着就收到不少投诉。 4月底，周边商户、居民接连反映：店里的油烟乱排，影响正常经营、生活；马路上排队的顾客有时太多，堵住人行道，阻碍交通。 “街道干部来找我时，我是有点蒙的。”吴志勇说，葱油饼要好吃，需要烤和炸，自然产生

items.title: 优化口岸营商环境没有最好，只有更好（快评）
items.summary: 出台高效举措、优化服务体验、强化硬件设施、搭建高效平台……近年来，海关等职能部门和地方政府密切合作，推出一系列精准有力的政策措施，为激发经营主体活力和助力外贸高质量发展注入强劲动能。 口岸营商环境直接关系到国际贸易的便利程度。优化口岸营商环境，意味着在简化流程、提高效率、降低成本上下功夫。无论是通关时间的缩短，还是报关手续的简化，都显著降低了企业的运营成本，加快了货物的流转速度。 优化口岸营商环境没有最好，只有更好。随着全球贸易格局不断变化，口岸营商环境的优化仍将是一个持续的过程。各地各部门应持续提升政策供给质量，更大程度释放政策效应，推动口岸营商环境向着更加高效、透明、公平、便利的方向发展，有力助推贸易强国建设。 《 人民日报 》（ 2025年06月05日 08 版）

items.title: 将适老化理念融入“诗与远方”（专家点评）
items.summary: 自驾出行、列车出游和旅居康养成为越来越多老年人的选择。 银发旅游蓬勃发展，推动了旅游产业升级。无论是城镇还是乡村，都在努力完善旅游基础设施和公共文化服务。为了更好满足老年游客的需求，还应开发更多适合老年人的旅游线路和产品，并加强博物馆、美术馆、酒店等场所的适老化改造。从硬件到服务，全社会应共同发力，将适老化理念融入方方面面，助力老有所游、老有所乐。 值得关注的是，老年人也可能因信息不对称而遭遇消费陷阱，还可能因为行程安排不当而水土不服。文化和旅游部门要联合市场监管等部门，从社交平台的旅游广告和招徕资质审查开始，重点规范交通、餐饮、住宿、购物、自费项目、医疗保障和应急救援等服务标准，加强对强买强卖、诱导消费、价格歧视等行为的综合监管和专项执法，让老年人畅享“诗与远方”。 （作者为中国旅游研究院院长） 《 人民日报 》（ 2025年06月05日 04 版）

items.title: 习近平总书记关切事｜我们的名字叫“长江”——三个沿江村庄的变迁故事

items.summary: 6月4日上午，国家主席习近平在北京中南海会见白俄罗斯总统卢卡申科。 新华社记者 黄敬文摄"> 6月4日上午，国家主席习近平在北京中南海会见白俄罗斯总统卢卡申科。 新华社记者 黄敬文摄 新华社北京6月4日电 6月4日上午，国家主席习近平在中南海会见白俄罗斯总统卢卡申科。 习近平再次祝贺卢卡申科当选连任总统。习近平指出，中国和白俄罗斯是真朋友、好伙伴。双方一直以诚相待、以信相交。两国传统友好历久弥坚，政治互信牢不可破，各领域合作全面推进。中方始终从战略高度和长远角度看待和发展中白关系，愿同白方一道，推动两国关系和互利合作行稳致远。双方要进一步加强在联合国、上海合作组织等多边框架内协调和配合，共同反对霸权霸道霸凌，捍卫国际公平正义。 卢卡申科表示，这是我第15次访问中国，每一次都真切感受到中方的深情厚谊。白方感谢中方长期以来大力支持和帮助，对中国高度信任，将坚定不移发展对华关系，积极推进对华合作。在国际事务中，中国坚定维护多边主义，反对单边主义和制裁施压，为世界树立了榜样。白方深表钦佩，愿与中方共同捍卫国际公平正义。 王毅参加会见。 《 人民日报 》（ 2025年06月05日 01 版）

items.title: 习近平向韩国当选总统李在明致贺电
items.summary: 新华社北京6月4日电 6月4日，国家主席习近平致电李在明，祝贺他当选韩国总统。 习近平指出，中韩互为重要近邻和合作伙伴。建交33年来，双方超越意识形态和社会制度差异，携手并进、相互成就，实现两国关系平稳健康发展，不仅增进了两国人民福祉，也为促进地区和平稳定和发展繁荣作出积极贡献。 习近平强调，我高度重视中韩关系发展。当前，世界百年变局加速演进，国际和地区形势中的不确定因素增多。作为全球和地区重要国家，中方愿同韩方一道，坚守建交初心，坚定睦邻友好方向，坚持互利共赢目标，共同推动中韩战略合作伙伴关系不断向前发展，更好造福两国人民。 《 人民日报 》（ 2025年06月05日 01 版）

items.title: 公证档案管理办法修订 推进公证电子档案信息化建设
items.summary: 记者6月4日从司法部获悉，司法部、国家档案局近日印发新修订的《公证档案管理办法》，进一步推进公证电子档案信息化建设，优化公证档案保管期限，完善公证档案利用规则等。 公证档案是记录公证活动过程的基本载体，是国家档案的重要组成部分，是公证执业监督和质量管理的主要依据。办法完善公证档案管理部门职责任务，明确国务院司法行政机关负责制定全国统一的公证档案工作制度，并与国家档案主管部门对全国公证档案工作进行监督、指导和检查。 在推进公证档案电子化与文书材料归档数字化转型方面，办法设专章明确公证档案信息化建设的整体性要求和原则性规定，规定公证电子档案与传统载体公证档案具有同等效力，倡导推进公证档案数字化，并对已经数字化的档案备查提出要求。让静态数据转化为服务动能，更好促进减证便民。 此外，办法依据新修订的档案法及其实施条例，规定大幅缩短公证档案保管期限，将永久、60年和20年的保管期限，相应调整为永久、30年和10年，并制作《公证档案保管期限表》，以附件形式附后。办法明确公证档案保管责任，规定公证机构可以将公证档案的保管期限通过书面告知、办公场所公示等方式告知当事人。规范公证档案销毁条件和程序，明确

items.title: 法治力量护航民营经济高质量发展（代表之声）
items.summary: 《中华人民共和国民营经济促进法》颁布施行，令民营企业界广为振奋。这部法律的出台，承载着民营经济人士多年的期盼，回应了经营实践中的痛点、难点问题，必将开启民营经济发展的崭新篇章。 改革开放40多年来，民营经济从小到大、从弱到强，不断发展壮大。我父辈那样老一代民营企业家视法治建设为企业发展根基，呼吁加强法治保障，对民营经济领域法治建设有着深切期盼。上世纪90年代，许多民营企业家为制定乡镇企业法建言献策。从当年的乡镇企业法，到如今的民营经济促进法，映照了我国从推进农村工业化到构建高水平社会主义市场经济体制的深刻变革。 作为一名来自民营企业的全国人大代表，我有幸参与了民营经济促进法的立法过程。去年在草案征求意见阶段提交了意见，今年全国两会期间又提交了相关代表建议，并列席十四届全国人大常委会第十五次会议，见证了新法的审议和表决。让我印象特别深刻的是，立法过程中，立法机关充分听取民营企业家的意见，相关部门负责同志也专程到我们的驻地，就法律条款进行详细解读和沟通，充分体现了党和国家对民营经济的重视、对民营企业诉求的尊重。 党的十八大以来，党中央出台一系列重大举措，促进民营经济持续、健康、高质量发展。

items.title: “阿大葱油饼”焕新记（干部状态新观察·走进一线探作风）

items.title: “填一表、跑一次” 辽宁沈阳推出“公民信息连锁变更一件事”
items.summary: 平日里，你有过变更身份信息多次跑的经历吗？如何让更改身份信息快速又准确，来看看沈阳推出的“公民信息连锁变更一件事”。 2024年10月17日，沈阳市“公民信息连锁变更一件事”正式上线。沈阳居民在申请变更姓名、出生日期、民族、性别、居民身份证号码等基本信息时，可以在线下基层派出所或线上的沈阳政务服务网，通过填写一张表单，提交一次变更申请，进行业务办理。审批通过后，公安内部立即启动跨层级、跨警种联动，外部与社保、医保、公积金等部门跨部门联动，开展“串并联”审批。全部完成后，同步发放新的身份证、驾驶证、机动车登记证、机动车行驶证、保安员证、爆破作业人员许可证、社会保障卡，同步变更医保和公积金账户等信息，证照全部邮寄到家。截至目前，全市已经办理相关业务160余件。 沈阳市民邵某是“公民信息连锁变更一件事”的首位体验者，通过沈阳政务服务网“公民信息连锁变更一件事”板块申请变更姓名后，邵某的身份证、驾驶证、机动车行驶证、机动车登记证书，医保、公积金和姓名同步更改，一次申请全部办理完成。 据介绍，“公民信息连锁变更一件事”改革的实施离不开办事流程优化以及多部门数据共享与协同合作。沈阳市营商环境建设局

items.title: Ticket to Trouble: Scalping Row Disrupts Shanghai Comedy Show
items.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019041/Ticket to Trouble: Scalping Row Disrupts Shanghai Comedy Show
items.summary: Police placed three ticket scalpers in custody, and three others received administrative penalties after attendees who had purchased tickets through unofficial channels were denied entry to the venue.
items.body_text:
Ticket to Trouble: Scalping Row Disrupts Shanghai Comedy Show
An incident at a Shanghai stand-up show in which customers who bought tickets through unofficial channels were denied entry because of the venue’s ticket identity-verification requirements has sparked public debate over China’s ticket scalping market.
The topic has surged to Chinese microblogging platform Weibo’s trending list, receiving over 57 million views as of Friday. Many argued that making exceptions for scalped-ticket holders is unfair to legitimate buyers and could further fuel the practice.
The show, held Sept. 11 at the city’s Majestic Theatre, was headlined by Fu Hang, a comedian known for his high-energy performances and distinctive delivery. To combat ticket scalping, show organizer Standby had implemented a system requiring attendees to present their ID cards and undergo real-name checks upon entry.
The scene quickly became chaotic, as ticketholders whose ID cards did not match the identity information provided at the time of purchase were not allowed entry. Videos of the incident circulating online showed a large crowd gathered outside the theater, demanding entry, and delaying the show’s start time. Because of the disorder, all ticket holders were eventually allowed in, and Fu extended his performance for 20 minutes to make up for the delay.
Chinese law prohibits ticket scalping for profit, which can result in administrative penalties, including detention and fees. In 2023, the Ministry of Culture and Tourism and the Ministry of Public Security jointly issued a notice requiring shows with a capacity over 5,000 to adopt real-name ticket purchases and admission.
Ulala Li, a Shanghai resident and comedy fan who bought her ticket through an official channel, told Sixth Tone she felt overlooked by Standby. “Shouldn’t the audience members who entered the venue properly and were left waiting for 20 minutes have received an apology and compensation?” she said.
“I think there’s a legitimate place for a secondary market. But when there are too many professional scalpers, they can seriously disrupt the healthy functioning of the market,” she added.
Tickets for Fu’s show were priced between 280 and 580 yuan ($42 to $86). According to domestic media, one attendee told Fu that he had paid 3,500 yuan for a scalped ticket — roughly seven times its original price.
Event organizer Standby said on Sept. 12 that it would cover documented losses caused by the delayed performance, including cancellation, train and flight ticket change fees, and additional accommodation expenses.
A day later, Shanghai police announced that three scalpers who bought 104 tickets to the show and resold them at higher prices had been placed under criminal coercive measures. The three reportedly made more than 18,000 yuan in illegal profits.
Three others also received administrative penalties for reselling eight tickets they had purchased through official channels, making more than 570 yuan in profit, the police added.
An audience member was also punished for starting a widely spread rumor online that “80% of the show’s tickets were sold through scalpers.”
Internet celebrity and stand-up comedy commentator Luo Yonghao criticized Standby’s actions in a popular Weibo post on Saturday, saying that “ticket scalpers can never be completely eliminated.” He suggested introducing regulated secondary ticketing platforms to legalize ticket resales and called for legislation on the issue.
Editor: Marianne Gunnarsson.
(Header image: Visuals from Xiaohongshu, reedited by Sixth Tone)

items.title: How I Brought China’s Vibe-Coding Revolution to Rural America
items.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019015/How I Brought China’s Vibe-Coding Revolution to Rural America
items.summary: U.S. startup founder Ken Chester entered China’s first rural hackathon in a remote village in Fujian province. Then, he took the idea back to Michigan.
items.body_text:
How I Brought China’s Vibe-Coding Revolution to Rural America
As the car chugged up a dark, winding mountain road in eastern China’s Fujian province, I began to worry that I had made a huge mistake.
I had come to this remote mountainside to explore China’s push to harness the rise of artificial intelligence to drive growth in the countryside — a campaign I believed could offer some interesting lessons for the rest of the world.
A few days earlier, at a tech event in Shanghai, a contact had mentioned that a village in Fujian was about to host the country’s first “rural hackathon.” The idea immediately intrigued me. I had attended several hackathons in Silicon Valley over the years, but these events were typically sleepless, caffeine-fuelled contests where expert coders would team up to hammer out hundreds of lines of code over a few days.
To many in the Bay Area, the idea of holding a hackathon outside of a major tech industry hub — let alone in a tiny village — would have seemed like an outlandish proposition. Non-coders tended to be viewed as afterthoughts at best, or dead weight at worst.
But China seemed to be taking a different approach, leaning into the potential for new AI tools to lower the barriers to creating and running online businesses. Curious to learn more, I’d booked a ticket for the event — and jumped on a train from Shanghai.
But Longtan Village turned out to be even more remote than I’d imagined. Getting there involved taking a sleek high-speed train to neighboring Zhejiang province, then a much slower “green train” to the city of Ningde in Fujian, followed by an hourlong car ride up a snaking mountain track.
They weren’t really planning to host a hackathon here, were they?
My doubts eased somewhat once I arrived at the village. A brightly lit hall stood out like a beacon in the darkness, where a couple of young volunteers were welcoming latecomers with care packages, farmer’s hats, and directions to a hotel offering free accommodation, where I’d be sharing a room with another participant I hadn’t yet met.
As the only foreigner joining the event, I was first asked whether I could speak Chinese. I acknowledged a shaky command of the language, collected my things, and trudged off through the dark to find my room, as I nervously wondered how I would pitch a startup entirely in Mandarin.
But I was excited to get an up-close look at China’s vibe-coding revolution. As someone with family in rural Michigan, I have long had a keen sense for how accelerating technological change has deepened class and regional inequalities — and tried to find ways to bridge those divides.
Since college, I have tried to use my experience in the tech industry to drive social change, working on a range of projects to empower local communities. My trip to China was part of that effort, as I hoped to gain new ideas from the dynamic tech scene here.
Longtan, it turned out, offered an interesting case study. The village was no ordinary Chinese farming community — it was more like a social experiment, driven by a combination of government policy and youthful idealism.
Over the past few years, Longtan has seen a growing influx of young people looking to escape the intense pressure of life in China’s major cities. The local authorities have encouraged the inflow, seeing it as a way to revive the local economy after decades of urban migration.
The new residents moved into renovated buildings alongside the original villagers, and set up a non-hierarchical online cooperative known as the DAO to manage their affairs. They made a living by painting, running hotels and cafés, or as digital nomads.

items.title: Marriage Proposal at Beijing Concert Hits Sour Note With Fans
items.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019036/Marriage Proposal at Beijing Concert Hits Sour Note With Fans
items.summary: The couple’s romantic gesture drew angry shouts and security intervention. A viral video of the incident later prompted a reported police complaint.
items.body_text:
Marriage Proposal at Beijing Concert Hits Sour Note With Fans
Against the backdrop of tens of thousands of fans singing “Southern Girl” by popular Chinese folk singer Zhao Lei, a man in the audience drops to one knee, a woman in a wedding dress rises to her feet, and the two begin hurling wedding candies into the crowd.
But soon the audience turns, and instead of congratulating the happy couple, they start shouting, “Sit down” and “That’s enough,” drowning out Zhao’s singing and requiring several security guards to intervene.
The scene, which occurred at Zhao’s Sept. 12 concert at Beijing’s National Stadium, soon was heavily criticized after being posted on Douyin, the Chinese version of TikTok. Related topics on microblogging platform Weibo have been viewed over 130 million times as of Thursday.
Proposals at concerts are common in China, but pushback has grown in recent years. A 2025 survey of over 800 young Chinese by online tech news platform youth36kr found that over one-third of respondents ranked wedding proposals at concerts as “unwelcome” and “disruptive.”
Concert ticket prices are also climbing, making some feel that on-site disturbances come at a personal cost to their experience. Data from October 2024 showed that average concert ticket prices were nearly 525 yuan, up from roughly 485 yuan the previous year. In May 2025, average ticket prices climbed to nearly 750 yuan.
Many argued the couple had overstepped the bounds of acceptable public behavior. One online comment read, “I came for the concert, not your proposal.” Another user posted, “I paid to watch a performance, not to be the backdrop for your little sideshow.”
The discussion intensified on Monday when the video’s original poster, surnamed Xie, told domestic media that a user claiming to be the fiancé featured in the video had messaged him demanding he delete it. Xie said the user apologized for disrupting the concert but said the video infringed on the couple’s portrait rights, that they had filed a police report, and that they would pursue legal action if it was not removed.
Zheng Xiaoqiang, a senior partner at Beijing Tiantai Law Firm, told Sixth Tone that privacy claims usually fail in large public venues such as the concert arena where the incident took place. “They chose to actively draw attention (to themselves) in a public setting with tens of thousands of people present,” Zheng said.
However, he said that close-ups, repeated edits, or mocking captions of the incident reposted online may cross into portrait rights infringement. He added that the minor disruption to audience members is rarely compensable in court.
Other recent concert marriage proposals have similarly sparked controversy in China. In 2023, at a Beijing concert for the popular Taiwanese rock band Mayday, a couple in wedding attire took photos in front of the stage, sparking jeers that drowned out the music. Many said they disrespected both the audience and the performers.
Wang Yao, a concertgoer who proposed to her partner at pop singer Zhang Jie’s 2025 Beijing concert, told Sixth Tone that audiences differ depending on the music genre. Folk fans tend to value immersive musical experiences, while pop fans are more tolerant of interruption, she said.
Those who witnessed her own proposal sent her their videos, which Wang then posted on social media, earning hundreds of thousands of likes. “The proposal was brief, and people mostly cheered and wished us well,” she said.
“A concert proposal can be a touching surprise, but it ultimately shouldn’t disturb other audience members,” she added.
A university student from Wuhan, capital of the central Hubei province, surnamed Chen, told Sixth Tone she and her friends oppose marriage proposals during concerts, but used to support them. “As consumers, our sense of agency and public order has grown,” she said. “Singers and fans put a lot of effort into performances, and proposers piggyback on that at no cost. That’s selfish and insincere.”

items.title: Bangladesh and Pakistan hit by Gulf energy disruptions
items.summary: Energy disruptions are hitting Bangladesh and Pakistan as LNG shortages, rising fuel costs, and limited supplies ripple across South Asia Read Full Article at RT.com
items.body_text:
Bangladesh and Pakistan hit by Gulf energy disruptions
Bangladesh’s export factories are cutting production and Pakistan has rolled out fuel subsidies as disruptions to Gulf energy supplies drive shortages and higher costs across South Asia.
The pressure follows disruptions to oil and gas shipments through the Strait of Hormuz after the US-Israeli attacks on Iran. Fighting between Saudi Arabia and the Iranian-backed Houthis has also threatened trade through the Red Sea, another key route for Gulf energy supplies.
Bangladesh has been particularly exposed. The country relies heavily on imported LNG for electricity, and disruptions to supplies from Qatar have forced Dhaka to seek more expensive cargoes on the spot market. The gas and power shortages have triggered blackouts and factory shutdowns.
Asian spot prices for liquefied natural gas (LNG) have climbed close to $30 per million British thermal units from around $10 before the conflict.
The pressure is now hitting Bangladesh’s garment industry, its biggest export sector. A survey by the Bangladesh Knitwear Manufacturers and Exporters Association found that 55% of factories have seen buyers cancel or reduce orders because of gas and power shortages since late August, while 78% partially halted production.
Production delays are also raising costs. One garment producer spent $50,000 to air-freight jackets to a French buyer after delays, Reuters reported. Factories have turned to diesel to keep operations running, and industrial growth and production are slowing, Power Minister Iqbal Hasan Mahmud said this week.
Pakistan is also facing mounting pressure from expensive fuel. Its power sector could require up to 400 million cubic feet of gas a day through winter, while only two LNG cargoes have been confirmed for September.
Islamabad introduced a nationwide relief program this week offering eligible motorcycle, rickshaw, and small-car owners a subsidy of about $0.36 per liter of fuel within capped quotas.
And in a throwback to restrictions that were imposed in April, markets now have to close by 9 PM, marriage halls by 10 PM, and restaurants by 11 PM local time. Islamabad also banned official dinners, except for foreign visitors and delegations, and the purchase of new government vehicles.
Supply risks remain elevated. Only four commodity vessels crossed the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday, compared with a ten-day average of around 16, although three LNG vessels reappeared outside the strait.

Gates used vaccine funding to pressure governments – Merkel
Bill Gates turned the vast financial resources of his foundation into political leverage, using its wealth to pressure governments to spend more on vaccination, former German Chancellor Angela Merkel has said.
In the Meckel & Matthes podcast released by Handelsblatt earlier this month, Merkel warned that uncontrolled corporate power could leave governments doing “what the corporations order.” She said she first saw the danger not with the rise of artificial intelligence, but when Gates set up his foundation, which had more money “than the development budgets of major industrialized countries.”
An unelected billionaire had effectively put himself on a political footing with elected leaders, according to Merkel.
“He was suddenly received at least as warmly by some heads of state in the world as I was,” Merkel recalled. “And then he also had the power – by virtue of his money – to exert moral pressure.” If governments failed to provide enough funding for the international vaccine alliance, “we were immediately in a bad light,” she said.
Gates would then tell African leaders that “Merkel had been stingy this year,” she recalled. “And with that, he had gained considerable power.”
The vaccine alliance Merkel referred to is Gavi, a public-private partnership involving governments, the World Health Organization, UNICEF, the World Bank and private donors. The Gates Foundation was a founding partner, providing $750 million in seed funding, and has since contributed billions of dollars to the organization. Germany became a major Gavi donor during her chancellorship, pledging €600 million for 2016-2020 and another €600 million for 2021-2025.
The former chancellor said the foundation had focused heavily on a handful of areas, including vaccination. When she asked Gates about putting more money into education, he told her that the results there were harder to measure because teachers, countries and students differed.
That left governments with difficult choices over limited development budgets, Merkel said. They still had to fund education while Gates pressed them to put money into vaccination and diseases such as malaria. “That’s the kind of constraint you get caught in,” she said.
During the Covid-19 pandemic, the Gates Foundation worked closely with major global health organizations and collected extensive funding for worldwide health and vaccine initiatives.
The foundation, originally known as the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, was renamed the Gates Foundation after Melinda French Gates stepped down as co-chair in 2024, three years after the couple divorced. Their marriage had reportedly been strained in part by Bill Gates’ ties to convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.
Days after Merkel’s remarks, Gates said his foundation had dropped its goal of eradicating measles worldwide, citing growing reluctance to get vaccinated in wealthy countries. “At one point, the foundation wanted to eradicate measles, but the vaccine hesitancy in rich countries has meant that’s not on our list of goals,” he told Reuters, calling it “kind of tragic.”

items.title: Lindsey Graham sanctions bill ‘a grand disservice’ to US – Moscow (VIDEO)
items.summary: New Russian energy sanctions could raise US fuel prices and complicate diplomacy with Moscow, the Russian Embassy has warned Read Full Article at RT.com
items.body_text:
Lindsey Graham sanctions bill ‘a grand disservice’ to US – Moscow (VIDEO)
The “Russophobic” new sanctions bill empowering US President Donald Trump to impose steep tariffs on buyers of Russian energy will lead to ever-higher prices at the pumps for Americans, the Russian Embassy in Washington has warned.
The legislation was championed by the late Senator Lindsey Graham, a Russia hawk and staunch Ukraine supporter who pushed for “crushing sanctions” on Moscow before his unexpected death this summer. Named ‘The Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026’ in his honor, the bill allows the president to impose tariffs of up to 100% on goods from major buyers of Russian oil and gas, potentially including China and India, and additional sanctions on Russia and Iran. It cleared the House on Wednesday, removing the final congressional hurdle before reaching Trump, who has said he plans to sign it.
The Russian Embassy in Washington on Friday warned the legislation will likely backfire on American consumers, particularly as Middle Eastern energy supplies are already disrupted by the US war on Iran.
“Russophobic instinct underlying the late Senator Graham’s bill… makes a grand disservice to the current Administration’s efforts to Make America Great Again,” the embassy wrote on X. “Destabilizing energy markets by blocking Russian oil and gas trade as Mideast supply is dramatically cut is an invitation to ever-higher prices at the pump close to midterm November elections.”
The embassy also warned that targeting major buyers of Russian energy could deepen tensions between Washington on one side and Moscow and Beijing on the other. It argued that the legislation runs counter to the Trump administration’s diplomatic efforts with Moscow and that simultaneously confronting Russia and China would create a geopolitical “lose-lose” situation for Washington.
Russophobic instinct underlying the late Senator Graham’s bill approved by the House on September 16th (and earlier by the Senate) makes a grand disservice to the current Administration’s efforts to Make America Great Again.
Destabilizing energy markets by blocking Russian oil… pic.twitter.com/TQR4fFxD5C
US gasoline prices are already under pressure from the Middle East energy crisis. US gasoline averages $4.43-$4.44 a gallon, over $1.10 more than a year ago, while diesel has hit a record $6.40 nationwide, jumping 77 cents in the first half of September alone.
Disruptions to tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, a critical route for Gulf oil exports, have constrained supplies, while instability around the Red Sea and Bab el-Mandeb Strait due to Iran-allied Yemeni Houthi advances has threatened another major shipping route. Crude prices have climbed above $100 a barrel, raising concerns about further increases at the pump if disruptions persist.
China and India, the largest buyers of Russian energy, have opposed the bill and defended their purchases. Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun said on Thursday that Beijing rejects Washington’s “long-arm jurisdiction” as lacking a basis in international law. India has warned that tariffs over Russian oil purchases could affect US-India ties and vowed to “take all necessary measures to protect its trade and economic interests.”
Moscow has long denounced Western energy sanctions as illegal and self-defeating, arguing that they redirect Russian exports while forcing Western countries toward more expensive supplies. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov warned this week that additional US sanctions would make reaching a settlement of the Ukraine conflict more difficult.

items.title: Wine Production in Crimea Drops 25% Amid Fuel Shortages and Supply Line Attacks
items.summary: Industry experts told Kommersant that the production slump was due to Ukraine ramping up its attacks on the peninsula this summer.
items.body_text:
Wine production in annexed Crimea fell by one-quarter in the first eight months of 2026 due to fuel shortages and logistical bottlenecks triggered by intensifying Ukrainian attacks, the newspaper Kommersant reported Friday.
Data from Russia’s Federal Alcohol Market Regulation Service show Crimean still wine output dropped 24.7% year-on-year between January and August, while sparkling wine production fell 38%. In Russia, still wine output fell nearly 15% and sparkling wine dropped 14.5% over the same period.
Crimea, which Moscow annexed from Ukraine in 2014, is a major regional supplier, accounting for 20% of all still wine and 10% of sparkling wine sold in Russia.
Industry experts told Kommersant that the production slump was due to Ukraine ramping up its attacks on the peninsula this summer, triggering an acute fuel shortage and disrupting shipping between Crimea and the Russian mainland.
Transporting essential production materials — including glass bottles, corks and packaging — has become increasingly expensive and hazardous, the experts said. Rolling power outages caused by strikes on energy infrastructure have further strained winemaking operations.
At the same time, fewer tourists have been traveling to Crimea due to deadly Ukrainian attacks, leading to a decrease in people making wine purchases while on vacation there.
Despite the current drop in output, winemakers anticipate a recovery later this year, buoyed by forecasts of a strong grape harvest expected to be the best in a decade.

items.title: Nestlé Weighing All Options After Kremlin Takes Control of Its Russian Business
items.summary: President Vladimir Putin signed a decree Thursday placing the company’s Russian assets under temporary administration.
items.body_text:
Nestlé said Friday that it was weighing all options to protect its rights after the Kremlin decided to take control of the Swiss food maker's Russian business, the latest move against a Western company since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
The Nescafé and KitKat maker said it took note of the decision, announced in a presidential decree on Thursday, and was assessing the situation.
"Nestlé is committed to taking all necessary steps to protect its rights and ensure continuity of business operations in the interests of all stakeholders, particularly its employees," the company said in a statement.
It declined to comment further on what action it was considering.
Nestlé shares were down 1.5% in early trading in Zurich.
Russia has tightened control over foreign-owned assets since the 2022 invasion of Ukraine. A 2023 decree signed by President Vladimir Putin gives Moscow the power to place assets from countries it deems "unfriendly" under temporary administration.
Moscow has also used the law to raise cash through forced sales, exit taxes and discounts, while rewarding Kremlin-loyal insiders.
Nestlé has six factories in Russia producing coffee, pet care and infant formula products. It generated sales of about 2 billion Swiss francs ($2.4 billion) in Russia in 2021, the last year it released figures, and has about 7,000 employees there.
The sales figure corresponds to about 2% of Nestlé's total sales, although analysts estimate the contribution has declined after the company scaled back activities in the country.
Nestlé has suspended the vast majority of sales, non-essential imports and exports, advertising and capital investment, said Bank Vontobel analyst Jean-Philippe Bertschy, who estimates Russia now contributes around 1% of group sales.
"While negative for sentiment and raising the prospect of an asset impairment or unfavourable disposal, we expect a marginal financial impact, given Russia's limited contribution to group sales," he said.
French supermarket group Auchan was also targeted by Thursday's decree, with its Russian assets transferred to the temporary management of L.E.V. Management.
Auchan, which operates 230 stores and an online business in Russia where it employs about 30,000 people, declined to comment.
The newspaper Kommersant has previously reported that a company known as KS Logistika asked Putin to place Nestlé's assets under temporary administration.
In previous cases, temporary administration has often preceded state expropriation, with assets later transferred to Kremlin-linked individuals or companies.
Other Western companies have sold Russian assets or handed them to local managers to comply with sanctions or in response to threats from Moscow to seize foreign-owned assets.
Nestlé has justified continued operations in Russia by arguing that, as a food producer, it supplies essential goods.
Moscow took control of French dairy company Danone's Russian business and beer company Carlsberg's stake in a local brewer in 2023.
Danone was removed from the list of assets under temporary Russian state management in March 2024 amid reports that a Russian businessman known for his pro-war credentials planned to buy the business at a steep discount.
In December 2024, Carlsberg sold its shares in Baltika Breweries in a management buyout.
Kepler Cheuvreux analyst Jon Cox said such experiences did not bode well for Nestlé.
"Ultimately, Nestlé may end up losing those assets — around 2% of its sales and cash tied up in Russia — for the foreseeable future, and any compensation is unlikely to be an offset," he said.

items.title: Where Can Russian Athletes Compete After the IOC’s Provisional Ban Lift?
items.summary: The Moscow Times has compiled a list detailing where and how Russian athletes can currently compete on the international stage.
items.body_text:
Russia’s return to international sports competition was already well underway long before the International Olympic Committee (IOC) provisionally lifted its ban on the Russian and Belarusian Olympic Committees this July.
The shift began in September 2025, when the International Paralympic Committee voted against maintaining its ban on Russian and Belarusian athletes, paving the way for them to compete at the 2026 Milano-Cortina Paralympic Games, where Russian competitors won eight gold medals.
By December, the IOC recommended that international federations lift their bans on Russian and Belarusian youth athletes.
However, some individual governing bodies acted even earlier. The International Judo Federation became the first to restore full participation rights to senior Russian athletes in November of last year. World Taekwondo followed this January by approving the full return of both junior and senior athletes from Russia and Belarus.
Since then, eight additional Olympic sports federations have restored full participation rights to Russian athletes and teams, allowing the use of the Russian flag, national anthem and team uniforms.
Below is a list compiled by The Moscow Times detailing where and how Russian athletes can currently compete on the international stage:
Federations that allow full senior and youth participation
Archery: On August 14, World Archery reinstated Russian athletes, allowing them to compete under their national flag and bringing their status in line with Belarusian athletes, who were reinstated in May.
Aquatics: The World Aquatics Bureau lifted its ban on senior Russian and Belarusian athletes on April 13, 2026, two months after it lifted its ban on Junior athletes.
In its statement, World Aquatics President Husain Al Musallam said, “Over the last three years, World Aquatics and the AQIU have successfully helped ensure that conflict can be kept outside the sporting competition venues. We are determined to ensure that pools and open water remain places where athletes from all nations can come together in peaceful competition.”
Boxing: On July 30, World Boxing announced that it was restoring full participation rights to all Russian athletes.
"The Executive Committee accepted that Russian athletes would now take part in World Boxing competitions like boxers from any other national federation. However, World Boxing will strictly monitor the behaviour of Russian delegations during events as well as compliance with anti-doping protocols," the statement read.
World Boxing previously lifted its restrictions on Belarusian athletes on May 12.
Equestrian: The International Equestrian Federation (FEI) will lift restrictions on Russian riders and officials starting Oct. 5 and once again allow international competitions to be held in Russia, the governing body has said.
FEI had already approved a return to competition for junior athletes from Russia and Belarus on May 19, 2026, but did not change its stance that senior athletes should compete with neutral status at that time.
Fencing: The International Fencing Federation (FIE) reinstated Russian and Belarusian athletes on June 2, 2026.
“The decision reflects the FIE’s commitment to the fundamental principles of the Olympic Charter, including non-discrimination, equal treatment and the universality of sport, as well as the objectives and principles set out in the FIE Statutes,” FIE’s statement read.
On July 28, Russian fencer Pavel Graudyn won gold in the Men's individual sabre at the World Fencing Championships in Hong Kong, marking Russia's first gold at a major championship since the International Fencing Federation lifted its restrictions.
Field Hockey: On Sept. 17, the Russian Field Hockey Federation announced that it had received a letter from the International Hockey Federation (FIH) lifting all restrictions against its athletes and national teams.

items.title: Russian officials trying to move assets abroad and open foreign bank accounts amid mobilization rumors, Bloomberg reports
items.summary: Amid rumors of a new mobilization, senior Russian officials have spent recent months trying to open accounts at foreign banks and move their assets abroad, Bloomberg reported, citing documents it had obtained.
items.body_text:
Russian officials trying to move assets abroad and open foreign bank accounts amid mobilization rumors, Bloomberg reports
Amid rumors of a new mobilization, senior Russian officials have spent recent months trying to open accounts at foreign banks and move their assets abroad, Bloomberg reported, citing documents it had obtained.
According to Bloomberg, draft office employees are doing the same, and advising friends and relatives to leave Russia.
Bloomberg’s report offered no further details.
Speculation that Russia could announce a new mobilization after elections to the State Duma, the lower house of Russia’s parliament, has circulated for several weeks, echoed by Meduza sources, Western media, and Ukrainian officials. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has said that Russian authorities are allegedly planning to mobilize up to 300,000 people this fall.
Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov has said Ukrainian officials are trying to “ideologically stir up the situation” in Russia with their statements about a possible mobilization. Commenting on the rumors, Vladimir Putin has said that “there is no scenario today that would require a mobilization,” and has called the reports “utter nonsense” and an “information attack” on Russia.

items.title: Russian man swims from Kaliningrad to Lithuania seeking asylum, gets sent back to Russia
items.summary: Lithuania’s border service detained a Russian citizen who swam across the Neman River seeking political asylum and sent him back to Russia, according to a report by the Lithuanian news outlet Lrytas.
items.body_text:
Russian man swims from Kaliningrad to Lithuania seeking asylum, gets sent back to Russia
Lithuania’s border service detained a Russian citizen who swam across the Neman River seeking political asylum and sent him back to Russia, according to a report by the Lithuanian news outlet Lrytas.
The State Border Guard Service (VSAT) told the news outlet BNC the man was taken into custody on September 17 on the bank of the Neman River at around 1:50 p.m. Lrytas reported he is 60 years old; BNC put his age at 68.
During questioning, the man told Internal Affairs Ministry and border service officials that he was being persecuted in Russia over “activity on social media.” Lithuanian authorities, including the State Security Department, decided that same day to return him to the Kaliningrad region via the Panemunė checkpoint.
“There was no information indicating he faced any danger, held any special status, or might be admitted to the European Union, and he does not fall into a vulnerable category. It was decided not to let this person in,” a VSAT representative said.

items.title: ‘Nestlé is committed to taking all necessary steps to protect its rights’: Nestlé and Auchan respond to Putin’s decree placing their Russian assets under temporary management
items.summary: Nestle said it has “taken note” the Russian president’s decree introducing “temporary external administration” at Nestlé Russia.
items.body_text:
‘Nestlé is committed to taking all necessary steps to protect its rights’: Nestlé and Auchan respond to Putin’s decree placing their Russian assets under temporary management
Nestle said it has “taken note” the Russian president’s decree introducing “temporary external administration” at Nestlé Russia.
“The company is assessing the situation and its options. Nestlé is committed to taking all necessary steps to protect its rights and ensure continuity of business operations in the interests of all stakeholders, particularly its employees,” the company said in a statement.
Auchan’s Russian subsidiary, Auchan LLC, is continuing to operate as usual following Putin’s decree. The company said it “sent a request for clarification” about the decree but did not specify to whom.
“Once we receive the relevant information, we will be able to provide more detailed comment. As of today, the company and all its outlets continue operating as usual, without any changes,” company representatives told the Russian business news outlet RBC.
Putin signed the decree on the evening of September 17, placing the Russian subsidiaries of France’s Auchan and Switzerland’s Nestle under temporary management by “L.E.V. Management.” The same decree also placed shares of “Le Monlid,” the Russian division of France’s Leroy Merlin, under temporary management.
“L.E.V. Management” was registered in Moscow in October 2024, with Andrei Krayushkin listed as its general director. The independent Russian news outlet Novaya Gazeta Europe reported that his full name and date of birth match those of Interior Ministry Major General Andrei Krayushkin, the former first deputy head of the migration department.

NEW DELHI: In a significant blow to the Mamata Banerjee-led faction of the Trinamool Congress (TMC), the party's candidate for the upcoming Nandigram assembly bypoll, Sanchita Dey Pradhan, withdrew her nomination on Friday.Pradhanâs sudden departure from the race came after she met West Bengal chief minister and senior BJP leader Suvendu Adhikari in Kolkata. Her withdrawal also came just a day ahead of the deadline for withdrawing nominations. A photograph purportedly showing Adhikari and Pradhan together went viral on social media, the authenticity of which could not be confirmed.
The October 6 bypoll was necessitated after Adhikari vacated the Nandigram seat to retain BhowaniporeâMamata Banerjee's traditional bastionâwhere he had defeated the then chief minister in the West Bengal assembly elections held in April.That election marked the end of the TMC's 15-year rule, and the BJP formed its maiden government in West Bengal.
Mamata extends support to Congress
Addressing a press conference, Mamata Banerjee announced that her party would support the Congress candidate in Nandigram.Opposition leaders, including Congress' Rahul Gandhi, had called her up to express solidarity, she added."We are extending our support to Congress in Nandigram and in Assam. We are doing this for the greater interest of the nation...
Rahul Gandhi rang me up yesterday, Arvind Kejriwal also expressed solidarity; we will all fight together against BJP," the former chief minister said.She also strongly criticised the Election Commission over its decision to freeze the TMC's original "flowers and grass" symbol on Thursday. Following the split in the party, the poll panel on Friday assigned the name "Mamata All India Trinamool Congress" with the "football player" symbol to Mamata Banerjee's faction, while recognising the rebel camp led by Arup Roy as the "Democratic Trinamool Congress" with the "envelope" symbol.
The political turmoil follows massive internal rebellion after the TMC's assembly election loss, with over 60 of its 80 MLAs revolting against the leadership. In the Lok Sabha, 20 of the party's 27 MPs recently merged with the Nationalist Citizens Party of India to extend support to the BJP-led NDA government at the Centre.
Karan Manral is a journalist at the Times of India. He covers politics, social issues, and international affairs, exploring stories that affect peopleâs everyday lives. He also writes explainers to make these stories easier for readers to follow.

items.title: ‘PNS Hunain violated maritime norms’: India rejects Pak's claims over naval collision
items.body_text:
India rejects Pakistanâs claims after INS Kolkata collision with PNS Hunain
NEW DELHI: India on Friday rejected Pakistanâs allegations over the collision between Indian Navy warship INS Kolkata and Pakistan Navy vessel PNS Hunain in the Arabian Sea, accusing Islamabad of trying to âhide the truthâ and saying the Pakistani vessel violated a 1991 bilateral agreement and international maritime regulations.MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said Pakistan's response to India's diplomatic protest was expected and rejected the allegations against India."Recent events involving Pakistan and India have taken place. I would like to clarify a few things before you. We have seen Pakistan's response to the protest lodged by us. As always, it is an evasive reply or an attempt to hide the truth, which was expected from them. We completely reject the allegations made against us. I would like to place some facts before you and reiterate them. INS Kolkata was on a routine deployment in the Western Arabian Sea when a Pakistani naval ship, PNS Hunain, behaved in an unacceptable and unprofessional manner at sea, resulting in a collision. The dangerous overtaking maneuver by PNS Hunain was a grave violation of Article 10 of the Agreement on Advance Notice on Military Exercises, Maneuvers, and Troop Movements between India and Pakistan of April 1991.
This article explicitly states that naval units in the sea should not come within three nautical miles of each other..."
Jaiswal said the Pakistani vessel's manoeuvre also violated international maritime rules governing the prevention of collisions at sea."We have seen Pakistan's response to the protest we had lodged. It is the usual prevarication that we expected. We reject the allegations and insinuations contained therein. Let me reiterate the facts of the matter for you. INS Kolkata was on a routine deployment in the Western Arabian Sea when Pakistani naval ship Hunain conducted itself in an unacceptable and unprofessional manner at sea that resulted in a collision. The dangerous overtaking maneuver by PNS Hunain was in gross violation of Article 10 of the Agreement Between India and Pakistan on Advance Notice on Military Exercises, Maneuvers and Troop Movements of 1991, which clearly specifies that naval units at sea are not to be within three nautical miles of each other. In addition, the Pakistani ship also infringed the International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea. The Pakistani side has once again been advised about the need for all military units to observe due care and respect the provisions of the relevant agreements between the two sides in order to prevent any repeat of such incidents. The incident did not cause any major damage to INS Kolkata, and she remains at sea..."
What happened in the Arabian Sea
The collision took place on September 15 in the North Arabian Sea. India has said INS Kolkata was on routine deployment in international waters when PNS Hunain carried out a dangerous overtaking manoeuvre that resulted in the collision.Pakistan, however, has disputed India's account and accused the Indian warship of carrying out aggressive manoeuvres near its naval vessel. Islamabad has also claimed that the incident occurred within Pakistan's exclusive economic zone during its SEASPARK-26 naval exercise.
Both countries have lodged diplomatic protests following the incident.Under Article 10 of the 1991 agreement between India and Pakistan, naval units at sea are required to maintain a separation of at least three nautical miles.India has maintained that PNS Hunain came close to INS Kolkata at high speed before the collision, describing the manoeuvre as a violation of the bilateral agreement as well as the International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea.India also said the incident did not cause major damage to INS Kolkata and that the warship remains at sea. Reports said PNS Hunain suffered damage and subsequently returned to port.
