By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief
The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) and the Federal Ministry of Finance have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) on Monetary-Fiscal Policy Coordination to strengthen their partnership in the pursuit of stronger macroeconomic management, lasting economic stability and sustainable prosperity for all Nigerians.
The Governor of the CBN, Mr Olayemi Cardoso, signed on behalf of his bank, while the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Mr Taiwo Oyedele, signed on behalf of his ministry.
Speaking at the event at the CBN headquarters, in Abuja, yesterday, Mr Cardoso said the deal represented a shared commitment to deepen collaboration between the two parties in the interest of the nation’s economy and the Nigerian public.
His words, “Fiscal and monetary policies remain two important and complementary instruments for the management of a modern economy. While fiscal policy influences economic activity through government expenditure, taxation and borrowing decisions, monetary policy promotes price stability and financial system soundness through the management of liquidity, interest rates and monetary conditions. When these policies work in harmony, their combined impact is far greater than their individual efforts.”
The CBN boss emphasised that the MOU did not mean the creation of a new relationship between the two institutions, as, according to him, the bank and the ministry have worked together for decades in addressing critical macroeconomic issues, including inflation management, debt sustainability, budget financing, exchange rate stability, economic reform programmes and responses to domestic and global shocks.
The difference the MOU makes
Mr Cardoso said that although both authorities have been working together, the MOU was necessary, as it provides a clear framework for the type of consultation and information sharing between the two parties and that the relationship would no longer be left to mere individual discretions of office holders.
He said, “This memorandum provides a structured framework for regular consultation, information exchange and policy coordination. It will strengthen collaboration in critical areas such as government cash management, debt issuance planning, liquidity forecasting, macroeconomic analysis and periodic policy consultations, thereby enhancing policy coherence and the effectiveness of economic management.
“It transforms a relationship built on practice into one anchored by clear processes and enduring institutional commitment. By establishing predictable mechanisms for engagement, the framework will improve the quality of decision-making, reduce uncertainty and strengthen our capacity to respond effectively to emerging economic challenges.
“The timing of this agreement is particularly noteworthy as the Central Bank of Nigeria advances its transition towards an inflation-targeting framework. Across the world, the success of inflation targeting is known to rest not only on the effectiveness of monetary policy but also on the existence of a supportive fiscal environment.
“The Memorandum will also provide the foundation for developing the operational framework that will guide its implementation. Through regular dialogue, information sharing and coordinated policy assessments, both institutions will be better positioned to align their actions, minimise policy trade-offs and pursue shared national objectives.
“The ultimate goal is clear: to build a more stable, resilient and productive economy capable of delivering broad-based prosperity for present and future generations of Nigerians.”
In his remarks, Mr Oyedele stressed the need for the two authorities to closely work together while maintaining their respective autonomies, as both work in the interests of the same economy.

items.body_text:
PESHAWAR: Five cops were among 16 martyred in an explosion at Kohat Police Lines, according to officials.
Footage aired on television showed citizens gathered next to a building with a collapsed wall, digging through rubble and helping the injured.
The attack was claimed by the Hafiz Gul Bahadur-led Ittehadul Mujahideen.
Speaking to Dawn, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Inspector General (IG) Zulfiqar Hameed confirmed the death toll, adding that more than 50 people were injured.
He told Dawn that a vehicle-borne suicide bomber initially struck the building’s gate. He said that some headed towards the Counter Terrorism Department building, where they were neutralised, while around three went to the Special Branch building.
An initial handout from IG Hameed said the explosion occurred at a mosque at Kohat Police Lines. It added that initial reports suggested an explosive-laden vehicle was rammed into the building.
In a later statement, he said that a suicide bomber detonated himself near the Special Branch building, adding that an exchange of fire was underway with Fitna al Khawarij terrorists.
“The operation will continue until the complete elimination of Fitna-ul-Khawarij,” the IG was quoted as saying, adding that the police’s morale remained high.
Fitna al Khawarij is a term the state uses for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan.
At around 3:30pm, police said the clearance operation was “in its final stages”.
The statement detailed that seven terrorists had attempted to infiltrate Police Lines after the explosion.
“So far, six terrorists, including a suicide bomber, have been killed,” the statement said.
Separately, KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi sought a detailed report on the incident, saying the targeting of innocent citizens was “deeply regrettable and unacceptable,” as per a statement issued by his office.
He directed authorities to ensure immediate treatment for the injured. “The nation’s morale cannot be dampened by cowardly acts of terrorism,” he was quoted as saying.
In 2010, 20 people, mostly the relatives of policemen, were killed and more than 90 injured in a remote-controlled bomb blast inside a police colony located just behind the Kohat Police Lines.
Condemnations pour in
President Asif Ali Zardari, condemning the incident, vowed that the complete elimination of foreign-sponsored terrorists was “essential for national security”.
President Zardari wished the injured a swift recovery.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif sought a report on the blast from the concerned authorities. He also directed authorities to expedite relief operations, Radio Pakistan reported.
KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi also condemned the blast, praying for the recovery of the injured.
“The entire nation stands with the security forces to eradicate terrorism,” he said in a statement.
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said in his condemnation that terrorists’ “cowardly acts cannot weaken the nation’s resolve”.
A statement posted on his ministry’s X account said Naqvi expressed grief over the loss of lives in the attack and extended condolence to the bereaved.
“The nation is standing with the families of the martyrs in this moment of grief,” he was quoted as saying.
This is a developing story that is being updated as the situation evolves. Initial reports in the media can sometimes be inaccurate. We will strive to ensure timeliness and accuracy by relying on credible sources, such as concerned, qualified authorities and our staff reporters.

items.body_text:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday issued directives to include motorcycles, rickshaws and Qingqis that were registered after Jan 1, 2006 in the govt’s recently announced fuel scheme.
“All motorcycles, rickshaws, and Qingqis registered after Jan 1, 2006, will be eligible for registration in the Prime Minister Fuel Relief Scheme,” the Prime Minister’s Office said in a post on the social media platform X.
“Now, those who drive 20-year-old motorcycles, rickshaws, and Qingqis will also be able to benefit from the Prime Minister’s Fuel Relief Scheme,” it said.
PM Shehbaz Sharif had on Sep 13 announced a “relief scheme” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices.
Under the scheme, owners of motorcycles, rickshaws, Qingqis, three-wheelers and vehicles with engines of up to 800cc will receive a Rs100 per litre relief on petrol.
Motorcycles, rickshaws and Qingqis, as well as other two- and three-wheeler users, are eligible for relief on 20 litres of petrol per month. Owners of small cars with engines up to 800cc will receive the Rs100 per litre relief on 30 litres of petrol every month.
Renewed hostilities in the Middle East, which have resulted in disruption of major oil supply routes, have caused fuel prices to rise in the past two months.
In addition to the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz due to the US-Iran war, trade via Bab al-Mandab — which has become a vital route for Saudi oil exports in recent months — is also facing a rising threat from Houthi rebels.
The subsidy scheme faced snags on Thursday, the first day of its nationwide rollout, as many petrol pumps declined to honour the digital app, claiming they lacked the system needed to provide petrol at Rs100 per litre less.
A day prior, the Pakistan Petroleum Dealers Association (PPDA) expressed concerns that its members were unaware of the subsidy disbursement mechanism and feared they would have to run from pillar to post to recover the amount.
Amid the fuel crisis, the federal government on Thursday also reintroduced austerity measures, including setting 9pm as the closing time for markets and reducing fuel provision for official vehicles by 50 per cent for a period of three months.

items.body_text:
LAHORE: The Lahore High Court (LHC) on Friday extended the suspension of a Pakistan Medical and Dental Council (PMDC) directive for Afghan medical students to return to the neighbouring country after the lawyers representing the body and a varsity sought more time to submit their replies.
The PMDC issued a notification on September 1, directing Afghan medical students enrolled in Pakistani colleges to return to Afghanistan. The notification also barred medical and dental colleges from granting admission or placement to Afghan students for the current academic session.
Subsequently, a set of petitions against the directive was filed by 13 Afghan students enrolled at different institutions in Lahore, including King Edward Medical University, Shaikh Khalifa Bin Zayed Al Nahyan Medical and Dental College and the Services Institute of Medical Sciences, on September 10.
At the last hearing on Sept 11, LHC’s Justice Khalid Ishaq had sought replies from the respondents, including the PMDC, the health ministry and the vice chancellors of the medical varsities and colleges in question.
But the lawyers for the PMDC and the University of Health Sciences, appeared before the court on Friday, and sought more time to furnish their written replies.
The judge allowed their requests and adjourned the hearing for a date to be fixed later.
During the hearing, Justice Ishaq also heard a plea filed by five Afghan medical graduates on Thursday.
The petitioners said they completed a five-year MBBS programme in the 2021-2026 session under the HEC-administered Allama Iqbal Scholarship, but the PMDC had left their registration applications undecided for months.
The five petitioners argued in their plea that without PMDC registration, they could not enrol in the mandatory year-long house job required to practice medicine, which effectively stalled their careers despite having fulfilled their academic requirements. They contended that PMDC’s own 2025 regulations granted graduating students a right to a house job placement at their affiliated teaching hospital, and that the council’s governing 2022 Act did not empower it to order deportations.
The plea was clubbed with those filed on Sept 10.
Specifically regarding this petition, Justice Ishaq asked the counsel for the petitioners, Advocate Asad Jamal, to satisfy the court as to how his clients could seek a year-long house job as a right, keeping in view Pakistan’s current foreign policy.
He also asked the lawyer why did graduates wanted to continue their stay despite completing their MBBS programme.
Advocate Jamal responded that the graduates had a legitimate expectation for a house job after the completion of their programme.
Justice Ishaq the directed the counsel to convince the court on the maintainability of the pleas filed by the graduates, keeping in view Pakistan’s current foreign policy.
A large number of Afghan medical students were also at the court to attend the hearing.
Deportation drive
Millions of Afghans have poured into Pakistan over the past several decades, fleeing successive wars, as well as hundreds of thousands who arrived after the return of the Taliban government in 2021.
A deportation drive first launched in 2023 was renewed in April last year when the government rescinded hundreds of thousands of residence permits for Afghans, warning them of arrests if they did not leave.
Last year alone, over a million Afghan nationals were deported by Pakistan, a Senate Standing Committee on Kashmir Affairs, Gilgit-Baltistan and States and Frontier Regions (SAFRON) was informed.
Pakistan deported a total of 1,155,221 Afghan nationals in 2025, top officials of the Ministry of Interior and Chief Commissionerate for Afghan Refugees told the meeting.
The repatriated Afghans included 163,429 proof of registration card holders, 74,943 Afghan citizen card holders, 509,671 undocumented individuals and 407,178 voluntary returnees.

items.title: Greta Gerwig explains why she cast Meryl Streep as Aslan in 'Narnia' reboot
items.summary: Streep, 77, will voice the iconic Lion in the upcoming 'Narnia' rebootGreta Gerwig had a very specific voice in mind when casting Aslan for her upcoming Narnia movie. In an interview with Empire published Thursday, September 17, the award-winning filmmaker explained why Meryl...
items.body_text:
Published September 18, 2026
Greta Gerwig had a very specific voice in mind when casting Aslan for her upcoming Narnia movie.
In an interview with Empire published Thursday, September 17, the award-winning filmmaker explained why Meryl Streep was the rare actor who fit everything she wanted for the iconic lion in Narnia: The Magician’s Nephew.
“I wanted someone who was profound but not pretentious, who had gravitas but not morose self-seriousness,” Gerwig, 43, said. “Someone who could communicate depth and pathos as well as joy and delight.”
Age was another important factor for Gerwig. She wanted an actor who could bring wisdom to Aslan while still capturing the character’s sense of wonder, and 77-year-old Streep ticked all the boxes.
“I wanted someone who was older than 70, so there was a wisdom of experience, but who also had the capacity of fresh wonder, like a child,” Gerwig explained. “And also to be one of the greatest actors to ever do it. That list is not a long one.”
Streep will lend her voice to Aslan in the Netflix adaptation, which hits Imax on Feb. 12, 2027, before arriving on Netflix April 2.
The character was previously voiced by Liam Neeson and serves as Narnia’s true king, appearing throughout C.S. Lewis’ seven-book series.

Published September 18, 2026
WNBA is back with a bang after a short break, and we witnessed Angel Reese shining on court with all guns blazing after lifting fifth title at FIBA Women’s World Cup in Berlin.
Angel Reese and Rhyne Howard put up a strong show in the Dream’s blowout win over the Sun that held Connecticut to a season low of 59 points.
The Atlanta Dream defeated the Connecticut Sun 103-59 at Gateway Centre Arena on Thursday, September 17.
Howard, who finished with 10 points, eight assists, four steals and one key 3-pointer.
With this 3-pointer, Howard became the league’s only player who scored more than 100 3-pointers in a single season.
“We had a good, hard talk at halftime. We’re still fighting for something come playoffs, and so we’re making sure that we handle our business and that we don’t leave anything up to anybody else,” said Rhyne Howard.
Speaking of her record, she added, “I’m breaking a 3-pointer record every year, so I expect nothing less. Shooters are going to shoot, so I’m going to keep doing that.”
“There are going to be plenty more 3-point records with my name on them,” the confident Howard asserted.
Reese became the first player in WNBA history to score 30 points in just 25 minutes.
She posted 11 of 14 shots, including one 3-pointer, and had three assists and two blocks.
Reese, in a postgame on-court interview, described her performance and said, “I was joking in the locker room that I was very well-rested and ready to play.
“Right now, it’s important to make sure we’re setting the tone and leaving a taste in everybody’s mouth about what the playoffs are going to look like.”
For context, it was Reese’s 30th double-double of the season, and her 12th game with 20 plus points.

items.title: At least 16 martyred, 57 injured in Kohat mosque bomb blast
items.body_text:
At least 16 martyred, 57 injured in Kohat mosque bomb blast
- By Laiq Ur Rehman -
- Sep 18, 2026
KOHAT: At least 16 people have been martyred and 57 others injured in a bomb blast at a mosque in Kohat, police sources confirmed, ARY News reported citing security sources.
Following the explosion, security forces and police cordoned off the surrounding area and launched a search operation. Security squads rushed to the scene immediately upon receiving reports of the blast.
Security sources stated that investigation teams are actively gathering information to determine the exact nature and cause of the explosion.
Earlier, an explosion was reported at the Old Police Line in Kohat, confirmed police spokesperson on Friday.
Following the blast, police teams have reached the site, while routes leading to the old police lines have been closed as a precaution.
Police officials said the Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) office is also located within the old police lines.
Rescue teams reached the site shortly after the incident and launched relief and rescue operations, according to Rescue 1122. According to police spokesperson, at least 20 injured have been moved to the hospital.
The rescue service said 35 officials are working at the blast site.
Earlier this year, in February, a Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP) was among five people killed and three others were injured when unidentified gunmen attacked a police vehicle on Shakardara Road in Kohat.
According to police officials, the incident occurred while a police team was transporting two accused persons in a police mobile. Armed assailants opened fire on the vehicle, triggering a heavy exchange of gunfire.
Those killed in the attack include DSP Lachi Asad Mehmood, Investigation Inspector Anar Gul Khan, and a police constable. The two accused in police custody, identified as Yousuf Khan and Samiullah, were also killed during the attack.
Three Frontier Corps (FC) personnel were injured and shifted to the District Headquarters (DHQ) Hospital for medical treatment.
Following the incident, security forces cordoned off the area and launched a search operation. Additional police contingents were also dispatched to the scene, and security was placed on high alert amid fear and panic in the area.

items.title: Spanish police operation clears migrants from Ceuta
items.body_text:
Spanish police operation clears migrants from Ceuta
- By Reuters -
- Sep 18, 2026
MADRID – Thousands of migrants living on the beaches of North African city of Ceuta in Spain were forcibly driven away by riot police on Friday. Police have moved the migrants to makeshift shelters and processing facilities at the port in Ceuta.
Approximately 150 riot police descended on the beach, forcing dozens of migrants living in roadside shelters to leave. Police fired warning shots with rubber bullets and used batons to break through barricades during moments of palpable tension.
What Occurred During the Operation?
Friday’s operation was tense from the start as tactical units approached the beachfront encampment. Although most residents left without resistance, there was sporadic pushback during other instances when police attempted to clear the beachheads.
Authorities fenced off the access points to the beaches, where authorities guided small groups onto organized shuttles heading for the port compound in Ceuta. Officials say the operation was brought about by the dire public health and safety situations caused by the years-long illegal camping.
What Will Happen to Migrants now?
Once at the port complex, migrants are being documented, screened, and processed by officials. European border agents and Spanish humanitarian organizations are present to receive migrants’ asylum applications and help them settle into the makeshift shelter.

Anthropic expands Into biology with new lab for AI drug research
- By Web Desk -
- Sep 18, 2026
San Francisco, CA – Artificial intelligence pioneer Anthropic has officially moved from the purely digital realm into the tangible biological world. On 18 September 2026, the company announced that it has established a physical wet lab in the San Francisco Bay Area to conduct real-world biological experiments and expand its drug AI pipeline.
Moving from Simulation to Reality Beyond Visualisation – Using Lab Robots and Wet Lab Experiments Though the facility will make use of only laboratory automation, it will not be solely software-based; it will directly run physical biology experiments under the close guidance of its AI model Claude.
[ Computational Models (Claude Science) ] [ Model Hardware Standard Protocol Interface ] [ Automated Wet Lab Robotics (Bay Area Facility) ] [ Empirical Biological Feedback ] Away from Computer Simulations, Back to Lab Robots and Biological Validation Rather than solely choosing to simulate experiments in advance, this laboratory will make use of physical automation dictated by Claude.
This will be based on the Model Hardware Standard protocol, which was officially launched in August 2026 and which enables lab robots to execute biological procedures under the direction of a large language model.
[ Computational Models (Claude Science) ] [ Model Hardware Standard Protocol Interface ] [ Automated Wet Lab Robotics (Bay Area Facility) ] [ Empirical Biological Feedback ] Rather than purely automating, the company emphasizes the important role of researchers and human experimenters in its safety architecture.
“We believe in the power of tight feedback loops, and there’s no substitute for having our own experiences alongside researchers in the trenches trying to develop drugs.”
– Eric Kaouderer-Abrams, Head of Life Sciences at Anthropic Taking on Neglected Diseases Rather than following the traditional biotech product paradigm, the company’s initial drug discovery operations will focus on preclinical research into neglected and orphan diseases, which have historically been an “off-limits” space for drug companies due to price considerations.

items.body_text:
Most Asian stocks track Wall St rally, yen drops after BoJ rate hike
Hong Kong – Asian stocks mostly rose on Friday in line with a rally on Wall Street as a drop in oil prices eased inflation concerns, while the yen dropped against the dollar even after the Bank of Japan hiked interest rates to a three-decade high.
The Federal Reserve’s lift in borrowing costs this week provided some relief to traders concerned that policymakers were not moving quick enough to address a spike in inflation that could deal a blow to the world’s top economy.
That has been helped by news that Saudi Arabia was moving to restore within days about half of crude shipments disrupted by the stoppage of its East-West pipeline to the Red Sea.
The conduit, even more important since the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz by Iran, was shut last week after being targeted by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis.
Crude prices, which had soared around a fifth in September, have fallen around five percent from recent highs, with West Texas Intermediate dipping below $100 for the first time since last Friday. WTI was down more than one percent Friday and Brent lost two percent.
The surge in oil this month has been among the main catalysts for rising inflation since the United States and Israel began their war on Iran at the end of February.
And the latest fall-off provided some much-needed support to stocks.
Seoul, Tokyo, Hong Kong, Shanghai, Taipei, Mumbai and Bangkok all advanced, although there were losses in Singapore, Wellington, Jakarta and Manila. Sydney was barely moved.
London, Paris and Frankfurt dipped.
The latest moves in oil and the Fed’s action reassured investors and kept the 10-year US Treasury bond yield — a key indicator of borrowing costs throughout the world’s biggest economy — back below five percent.
Japan’s Nikkei was also helped by a drop in the yen against the dollar that came in the wake of the BoJ’s well-telegraphed decision to lift rates to their highest level since 1995.
Pressure has increased on officials to further tighten monetary policy as a spike in oil prices caused by the Middle East crisis — which shows little sign of ending anytime soon — is expected to keep putting a floor under inflation.
“Given that underlying CPI inflation has been approaching two percent and financial conditions have been accommodative, the bank will continue to raise the policy interest rate,” the BoJ said on its website.
But the yen slipped to more than 157 to the greenback, compared with around 156 earlier.
Stephen Innes at Quintex Intel suggested traders were jolted by the fact that the hike was not unanimous, passing by a 7-2 majority.
“For a market looking for evidence that the BoJ could shorten the distance between hikes, those dissents mattered,” he wrote.
“Traders were looking for signs that the Bank could move faster from here, yet two members were already arguing that even today’s move had come too soon.”
Focus will now turn to Governor Kazuo Ueda’s news conference due later in the day.
“Attention should fall on the forward swaps curve and the Bank’s guidance around the pace and urgency of further tightening,” wrote Chris Weston at Pepperstone.
“The market will be looking for confirmation that further normalisation remains firmly on the table, while assessing whether the Bank sees any urgency to move again.”

items.body_text:
KBR and AKT sign engineering deal for Iraq’s West Qurna gas capture project
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – KBR and AKT have signed a contract to complete the comprehensive engineering design for Iraq’s West Qurna Gas Capture Project, which advances Basrah Gas Company’s efforts to collect associated gas and minimize flaring in southern oilfields.
KBR will offer engineering expertise for the design work in partnership with AKT, since the project is part of Basrah Gas Company’s (BGC) larger gas collection initiative.
The project aims to collect associated gas generated with crude oil from West Qurna, which would otherwise be burnt, enabling more of the resource to be processed and consumed domestically.
Expanding gas capture is critical to Iraq’s attempts to prevent flaring, enhance local gas supplies, and make better use of its energy resources, especially as the country seeks to reduce its dependency on imported gas and fuel for power production.
The West Qurna development is one of many gas projects now underway in southern Iraq, where some of the country’s major oilfields are located and significant amounts of associated gas are generated.
KBR said that the deal strengthens its role in gas monetization and energy infrastructure projects in Iraq and the broader Middle East.
The companies did not disclose the contract’s amount or the timeframe for completing the detailed engineering design.

items.title: Egypt bans social media accounts for under-13s and mandates “safe mode” for ages 13-15
items.summary: Egyptian authorities declared a major digital crackdown on Thursday, barring children under the age of 13 from holding independent social media accounts and slapping strict mandatory restrictions on users under 15. In a joint decree issued by the Supreme Council for Media Regulation (SCMR) and the National Telecommunications Regulatory Authority (NTRA), social media platforms operate … The post Egypt bans social media accounts for under-13s and mandates “safe mode” for ages 13-15 appeared first
items.body_text:
Egyptian authorities declared a major digital crackdown on Thursday, barring children under the age of 13 from holding independent social media accounts and slapping strict mandatory restrictions on users under 15.
In a joint decree issued by the Supreme Council for Media Regulation (SCMR) and the National Telecommunications Regulatory Authority (NTRA), social media platforms operate under a tough new mandate designed to shield children and young teenagers from digital risks. Under the newly unveiled regulations, platforms are strictly forbidden from allowing children under 13 to create or activate independent personal accounts.
For young teens aged 13 to under 15, personal accounts will still be permitted—but with a heavy catch. Platforms must automatically and mandatorily activate “Safe Mode” on these accounts, and the setting cannot be unilaterally disabled by the underage user as long as they remain in that age bracket.
To ensure the rules are not easily skirted, the decree compels tech platforms to deploy effective age-verification protocols and actively prevent users from manipulating age boundaries. Companies must audit existing accounts and take immediate action against any profile confirmed or suspected to belong to a user under 15. However, a formal appeals process must be provided to correct any legitimate age-verification errors.
Officials frame the sweeping measures as a direct response to directives from President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi aimed at safeguarding youth from the dangers of social media misuse and forging a safer online ecosystem.
Underscoring the broader vision, Khaled Abdel Aziz, Chairman of the SCMR, emphasized that digital child safety has become “a shared responsibility between the state, the family, society, and digital platforms.” He insisted that the objective is not to strip technology away from children, but rather to guarantee its safe, responsible, and age-appropriate use.
Echoing this stance, NTRA Chief Executive Mohamed Shamroukh explained that the framework operates on the principle of “age- and risk-proportionate protection,” delivering varying tiers of security based on a user’s developmental age and exposure to online hazards.
Tech firms have been put on a strict clock: platforms must bring their operations into full compliance within three months of the decree taking effect, and must submit a comprehensive operational blueprint and technical timeline detailing their execution strategy within the next 30 days.

Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi warned Thursday that persistent schemes to destabilize the state remain an ongoing threat, declaring that the unrest witnessed between 2011 and 2013 “has not ended” and that underlying plots “have not stopped.”
Speaking during an address at the Egyptian Military Academy, President Sisi emphasized that while methods may evolve, the push to dismantle the state persists, underscoring public awareness as the nation’s primary defense against continuous challenges.
Reflecting on regional volatility, Sisi noted that while several neighboring nations suffered catastrophic destabilization during that period, Egypt miraculously survived.
He described the nation’s survival as a divine blessing, asserting that events across the region were systematically orchestrated and planned, imposing a heavy responsibility on Egypt to safeguard its stability—particularly given its finite national resources.
The President stressed that protecting the state is a collective civic duty rather than a mandate tied to any single authority or leadership figure. Framing national preservation around the institution of the presidency, he cautioned, distorts the true purpose of state resilience, which rests on the joint responsibility of the government, institutions, and the Egyptian public.

items.body_text:
The Egyptian Meteorological Authority announced a noticeable shift in the weather across Egypt, as the country experiences a gradual drop in temperatures ranging between 3 to 5 degrees Celsius in most areas, starting Friday, and continuing through next Tuesday.
This drop comes after a heatwave that swept the country over the past few days, bringing temperatures back to seasonal averages for this time of year.
Moderate to warm and humid weather will prevail in the early morning, turning hot and humid during the day across the north of the country down to Greater Cairo and North Upper Egypt, while remaining extremely hot in South Upper Egypt.
Maximum temperatures in Greater Cairo and the Nile Delta are expected to reach around 33°C on Friday, dropping to 32°C on Saturday and Sunday, while in South Upper Egypt, temperatures will decrease from 43°C down to 39°C by the beginning of next week.
Meteorologists warned of dense morning fog forming at times between 4:00 AM and 8:00 AM on roads to and from northern Egypt, Greater Cairo, the Canal Cities, and Central Sinai.
There are also chances of light to occasionally moderate rain over parts of the northern coasts and the northern Nile Delta. Winds will pick up across most areas at speeds between 30 and 40 km/h, helping to cool the atmosphere, with a chance of kicking up sand and dust in parts of the Western Desert.

Farming permit gridlock at Lake Nasser reignites demands for Nubian right of return          
        Five months ago, a group of young men from the Nubian village of Daboud tried to apply for permits at the Lake Nasser Development Authority to grow watermelons along the lake’s shore.
They were told to return in August or early September, when applications are typically open. But when they did, they were told there were no permits available, even though other farmers were working in the area.
The group then went to the Egyptian Border Guard Corps, but were unable to meet the official they were seeking. During that time, they saw other people entering and leaving with permits for various activities, said one of the young men, who spoke to Mada Masr on condition of anonymity. “We sat there for three hours until the place cleared out and we were [the only ones] left,” he said.
Three days later, the young men took things into their own hands. They published a video online on September 4, calling for a Nubian mass mobilization conference the following week to discuss their demands and the Nubian community’s role in developing the Lake Nasser region.
Suddenly, officials, lawmakers and intermediaries began to reach out to them, offering two agricultural wells and fishing opportunities, while discussing arrangements for meetings with government officials and security agencies, the source, who also helped organize the conference, told Mada Masr. “Before the video, nobody was talking to us,” he said.
With the offers came pressure. The organizers simultaneously began to receive threats to postpone or cancel the event, he added, declining to identify those behind the threats. They were told they could meet officials from the Future of Egypt for Sustainable Development Authority, an agency headed by Air Force Pilot Colonel Bahaa Ghanem and which oversees major agricultural and development projects, on the condition that they postpone the conference.
But the organizers refused. “We can negotiate and still not cancel or postpone the conference,” the organizer said. “We promised the Nubian people.”
Daboud’s new mobilization over access to land and economic opportunities stems from the displacement of Nubian communities from their ancestral lands and the longstanding demands for return that followed successive waves of displacement beginning in 1898.
The new push — including the Popular Nubian Conference convened on September 10 — has brought the historical struggle back into the conversation in recent days, with the government moving in parallel to address outstanding reparations for Nubians displaced by the High Dam — an issue that Nubian leaders have insisted is separate from their constitutional right of return.
***
The Nubian right of return was explicitly recognized in the 2014 Constitution, with Article 236 stipulating that the state is responsible for developing the region and allowing Nubians back into their ancestral lands by 2024.
That same year, the Transitional Justice Ministry formed a committee to prepare a draft law concerning Nubia’s development and the community’s resettlement, which included Nubian representatives alongside official entities.
But the state has never followed through on that commitment. Instead, it undermined the Nubian return project through two presidential decrees, issued in 2014 and 2016, that placed historically Nubian lands under state control.
The first, Presidential Decree 444/2014, designated parts of the border region as military zones where civilians could not live, effectively barring Nubians from returning to 16 of their historic villages. Two years later, Presidential Decree 355/2016 allocated 922 feddans of state-owned land to the New Toshka development project, including the site of the historic Nubian village of Furkund.

Clashes flare around Warraq with tensions high as island residents campaign for housing guarantees          
        Warraq Island residents clashed with security forces deployed intensively on and around the Nile island this week, with tensions flaring as authorities are yet to respond to the residents’ demands for clear answers and guarantees regarding the fate of their homes and lands.
The new chapter in talks between residents and authorities comes as families in Warraq take action to disrupt the government’s ongoing development project and seek firm guarantees that officials will support them to stay in their homes and lands.
Security forces set up on Tuesday metal mesh barriers at the entrance to the Qolaly ferry crossing that connects the island to the Nile bank, and, on Wednesday, more barriers were added in the vicinity of the crossing, according to a resident of the island who spoke to Mada Masr.
The measures, they said, add to a series of existing restrictions already imposed on the residents’ movement and access to key goods and services.
The new barriers appear intended to protect security personnel, after stones were thrown during clashes with residents near the ferry crossing in the preceding days, the resident said.
The latest of these took place at Qolaly on Sunday and Monday, with several residents injured as a result, including a young man whose skull was fractured in the clashes, they added.
To protest the security response to the Qolaly clashes, several residents also gathered at a demonstration on Monday evening near a security forces deployment stationed beneath the Tahya Misr Bridge that runs through the island.
The gathering ended in further clashes, according to two residents who were present. The confrontations were visible in footage posted by Warraq residents on social media.
As the ban on construction materials entering the island continues, the Qolaly ferry crossing, the main entry point to Warraq from Giza, has been a flashpoint of near-daily confrontations between residents and security forces for around nine years. One resident said to Mada Masr that the friction around the entry of materials to the island arises mainly between security forces and residents who work to deliver construction supplies to the island — but the clashes it triggers spill over to other residents in the area around the ferry.
The clashes come in parallel to a campaign to remain the island that residents have pursued since August. A large number of island residents have begun organizing as part of a group called Staying on Warraq, pushing for firm guarantees from authorities regarding the fate of their land and homes, according to several residents who have spoken to Mada Masr in recent weeks, particularly as circulating reports and unofficial maps of the government’s development project appear to include parts of the residents’ lands.
For years, residents have watched the development project unfold, waiting to learn what would happen to them, while their access to basic services on the island — like healthcare and education — has deteriorated due to state restrictions, leaving residents to establish replacements or alternatives themselves. Their efforts have included spending around LE400,000 to prepare schools for the current academic year.
They have now concluded that waiting has brought no solutions, as the state continues to carry out the project after acquiring most of the island’s land, the residents have said.
As part of this campaign, residents attempted on Sunday to obstruct the state’s road construction work on the island, blocking the way of transportation trucks involved in the state development project. items.body_text:
33 Sudanese arrested from Giza public garden face deportation as worsening economic conditions throw many into housing instability          
        Sudanese businesses operating from Cairo have laid off dozens of workers in recent months as economic conditions worsen in Sudan, according to two informed sources who spoke to Mada Masr and said the layoffs have thrown many Sudanese nationals in the Egyptian capital into housing instability.
The layoffs have forced many to take shelter in public spaces, a situation that Egyptian authorities earlier this week treated as grounds for security intervention.
Some of those laid off from their jobs were among the 33 people whose arrest the Interior Ministry announced in an online statement on Sunday alongside footage of people taking shelter in a public park in 6th of October City in Giza, according to the two sources.
The Interior Ministry stated that security forces acted after the footage circulated online, carrying out an operation that led to the arrests. It added that those detained were not carrying identification documents or residency permits.
All 33 individuals arrested were Sudanese men, and all are currently going through deportation procedures, according to an official at the Sudanese embassy in Cairo, who spoke to Mada Masr on condition of anonymity, as well as the two informed sources: Mohamed Farah and Amgad Taha, both of whom were in contact with some of those arrested.
Farah, who works in Cairo, and Taha, who lives in Aswan and is a relative of one of those detained in the 6th of October City park, each said they know at least five of the men detained on Sunday.
They said the cases are part of a crisis that emerged in July, starting with the loss of jobs, then the loss of housing, which then led people to seek shelter in a public space as a last resort.
The men, many of whom did not have legal documents, were employed by Sudanese companies operating in Egypt that sell goods to markets in Sudan, they said. The men were working in packaging, loading and unloading and similar jobs in return for low wages, and the companies provided food and accommodation, commonly putting about 10 workers in a room, they explained.
As the Sudanese pound has plummeted in value against the dollar in recent months, it has affected operations at the companies, whose Sudan-based revenue streams have been diminished while their costs have remained high.
According to Taha, some of the workers went without pay for as long as three months.
Some businesses shut down or moved their operations back to Sudan, leaving workers with neither their jobs nor their employer-provided housing, Farah and Taha said.
The workers moved in with acquaintances or other workers or tried to look for cheap accommodation, but rising living costs soon made those arrangements unsustainable. Since August, many have resorted to sleeping in public spaces while trying to find another way to support themselves, according to both men.
The Sudanese official at the embassy in Cairo confirmed the situation, adding that some of those turning to public spaces at present are families as well as individual workers.
According to Taha, the cases seen in the parks do not represent the full number of Sudanese people struggling to find housing. Rather, they are the small proportion whose circumstances ended up becoming visible in public spaces.
The detained men, Taha said, are being deported without their complaints being heard, adding that their lack of legal documents had been exploited by their employers.
According to Taha and Farah, many Sudanese young men they know have stayed in Egypt for work while their families returned to Sudan.
The Sudanese embassy official said the embassy handles cases involving Sudanese nationals facing problems with their residency status or being deported through official channels. items.summary: In a arena glowing with 10,000 light-emitting diode wristbands, young delegates from 191 countries sang together in Russian, exchanged plush Cheburashka toys, and listened to messages from orbiting cosmonauts as the International Festival of Youth (IFY – 2026) concluded its main programme in Ekaterinburg. items.body_text:
In a arena glowing with 10,000 light-emitting diode wristbands, young delegates from 191 countries sang together in Russian, exchanged plush Cheburashka toys, and listened to messages from orbiting cosmonauts as the International Festival of Youth (IFY – 2026) concluded its main programme in Ekaterinburg.
The seven-day event, held from September 11 to 17 under the Youth and Children national project and organised by Tavrida.ART, brought together 10,000 participants. The closing ceremony was structured around the theme that music unites people across nations and generations, serves as a bridge over geopolitical barriers, and forms part of a broader struggle for freedom, justice, and self-expression.
More than 1,000 artists took the stage during the ceremony, backed by full orchestras, choirs, and international conductors under the musical direction of composer Anton Belyaev, founder of the LAB project. The evening was hosted by Nikola Tsiskaridze, People’s Artist of Russia and Rector of the Vaganova Academy of Russian Ballet, alongside theatre and film actress Nika Zdorik.
The opening segment featured resident artists from the Tavrida arts cluster and the band Beautiful Boys, hosted by Anton Shastun, Dmitry Pozov, Liza Yushchuk, Varya Shcherbakova, and Lorenzo Bianti, followed by a prologue overture conducted by Italian conductor Fabio Mastrangelo.
In the ceremony’s first thematic section, titled “Russia Shares Its Ideas,” 150 ballet dancers, aerial acrobats, a choir, and an orchestra led by US conductor Christian Knapp performed a “Russian Megamix.” During the act, the 10,000 audience members joined the Sretensky Monastery Choir to sing lines from the song “Kon” (“The Horse”): “Ya vlyublyon v tebya, Rossiya” (“I’m in love with you, Russia”).
“When that many people start singing the same song all at once, it’s always a powerful, almost indescribable feeling,” said festival participant Alexey Andreev from St Petersburg. “In that moment, it stops mattering where you’re from or what language you speak. It was especially wonderful to see people from other countries trying to sing along too. I think that’s what real unity, and the power of music, really is.”
The event drew explicit parallels to historical predecessors, notably the 1957 World Festival of Youth and Students in Moscow. An episode named “A Connection Between Generations” paired archival footage from 1957 with performances by the vocal-instrumental ensemble “Poyushchiye Gitary” (“Singing Guitars”), LAB choir soloists, and pop artist Akmal’, accompanied by an orchestra conducted by China’s Zhang Shiqu.
Addressing the audience during the proceedings, Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov framed Russia as an “open and friendly country” and invited the international delegates to return for future gatherings.
“We appreciate that, despite the great distances involved, all of you have gathered here and seen for yourselves how Russia lives – an open and friendly country,” Lavrov said. “You represent different continents, cultures, religions and civilizations, but you’re all united by youth, a thirst for knowledge, and a drive to find solutions to the most complex problems. It’s precisely knowledge, combined with modern technology and new forms of cooperation, that makes it possible to solve challenges that seemed unattainable just yesterday.”
Lavrov urged participants to return without needing formal invitations, highlighting annual Russian events such as the Congress of Young Scientists and the Tavrida.ART Young Art Festival in Crimea. “Our unity lies in diversity, and at the International Festival of Youth, that principle has taken on real, practical meaning,” he added.
Personal aspirations and technological themes were highlighted in the segment “Dreams of the World’s Youth,” where five representatives from different global regions shared their personal stories before Russian singer Vanya Dmitrienko sang the chorus of “Sedaya Noch” (“Grey Night”) in English, backed by an orc

EKATERINBURG – Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov warned Europe that any attack on the Russian Federation would result in a “very short” war, delivering the remarks during a lecture on the new global architecture at the Znanie.Pervye marathon in Ekaterinburg.
Addressing the federal educational marathon, held as part of the International Festival of Youth, Lavrov stated that Moscow has no intention of initiating a conflict with European nations.
“We have no interest whatsoever in attacking Europe. But if Europe, which talks daily about preparing for war against Russia, were to attack the Russian Federation, that would be an entirely different war, and it would be a very short one,” Lavrov said.
The foreign minister described the conflict in Ukraine as a direct consequence of the West’s expansionist policy, NATO’s advance towards Russia’s borders, and a legislative ban on the Russian language.
“The regime currently in power is a Nazi regime, with Nazi ideology and practices enshrined in law and applied on a daily basis,” he stated. Lavrov added that the goals of the special military operation are entirely clear: eliminating the root causes of the crisis and protecting the rights of Russian people to their native language and Orthodox faith.
During his address, organised by the Russian Znanie Society in alignment with the Youth and Children national project, Lavrov discussed multipolarity, relations with the West, external interference in Russia’s electoral process, and opportunities for young people.
He identified multipolarity as the defining trend of the contemporary world, asserting that the gap in economic weight between BRICS countries and the G7 will continue to widen unstoppably.
“The countries of the Global South and East are strengthening their positions, along with new centers of growth in Eurasia, Latin America, and Africa. A philosophy of equality is becoming the dominant trend,” Lavrov said.
He accused the West of attempting to maintain slipping supremacy through unlawful sanctions, pressure, and the provocation of conflicts after enjoying dominance for 500 years.
“Our Western colleagues have never, throughout history, abided by the principle of the sovereign equality of states. They have always considered themselves the ones ‘calling the tune,’ but reality is forcing a return to the principles of the UN Charter,” Lavrov stated. He affirmed Russia’s commitment to approaches taken by BRICS, the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO), the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU), and the Collective Security Treaty Organisation (CSTO), as well as support for a Greater Eurasian Partnership.
“This will form a solid material foundation for building a Eurasian security architecture in which every country on the continent would have the right to take part,” he explained.
Discussing the economy, Lavrov noted that proposals for alternative payment platforms, settlement and depository mechanisms, a reinsurance mechanism, and a grain exchange were discussed at the BRICS summit in New Delhi.
“We are not the ones who undermined the dollar’s role. We are being forced to move toward new forms of cooperation, so that no one can stand in our way,” the minister said.
Responding to an international participant regarding Russian elections and Western interference, Lavrov emphasised citizens’ right to independently determine their country’s future.
“Elections are the choice of the people, a choice of the path the country will follow over the coming electoral term,” he noted. items.title: Egypt’s Madinaty Golf Club to host two Asian Development Tour tournaments with $250,000 prize purse
items.summary: The Egyptian Golf Federation announced that Madinaty Golf Club will host two international professional tournaments on the Asian Development Tour with a combined prize fund of $250,000, reinforcing Egypt’s position as a leading golf destination in the Middle East and Africa. The tournaments, which serve as the 13th and 14th rounds of the Egyptian Golf […] The post Egypt’s Madinaty Golf Club to host two Asian Development Tour tournaments with $250,000 prize purse first appeared on Dailynewsegypt.
items.body_text:
The Egyptian Golf Federation announced that Madinaty Golf Club will host two international professional tournaments on the Asian Development Tour with a combined prize fund of $250,000, reinforcing Egypt’s position as a leading golf destination in the Middle East and Africa.
The tournaments, which serve as the 13th and 14th rounds of the Egyptian Golf Series, will each feature a prize purse of $125,000. The first competition is scheduled to run from September 23 to 26, with the second taking place from September 28 to October 1.
Players from more than 30 nationalities are slated to participate, bringing together experienced professionals and rising talents from across Asia, the Middle East, and other regions.
The events will be held at Madinaty Golf Club, described in the announcement as the best golf course in Egypt and Africa. The venue previously achieved significant success hosting the 2025 Egyptian Open in collaboration with the Asian Development Tour, and also hosted an Asian Tour global golf tournament in 2022.
Omar Hisham Talaat, President of the Egyptian Golf Federation, expressed his pleasure at hosting the Asian Development Tour again, noting that securing major international tournaments reflects the growing confidence the global golf community places in Egypt. He added that the events highlight the quality of the country’s courses and its status as a global tourist destination.
Talaat explained that the federation’s strategy is not limited to hosting tournaments, but aims to provide Egyptian and Arab players the opportunity to compete alongside international professionals. The approach is designed to provide a genuine pathway for young players to develop and reach global competitions, while simultaneously leveraging these events to promote Egypt as a distinguished regional and international destination for golf and tourism.
Ken Kudo, General Manager of the Asian Development Tour, stated that the return to Egypt follows the success achieved by the tour’s tournaments last year. He affirmed that the partnership with the Egyptian Golf Federation reflects a shared commitment to developing professional golf and creating opportunities for players.
Kudo added that holding consecutive tournaments at Madinaty Golf Club represents a new step in the evolution of this partnership. He noted that the expected broad international participation from more than 30 nationalities will enhance the global diversity of the competitions and establish two distinct weeks of golf.

items.title: Lebanese Judiciary Moves to Prosecute Network Linked to Assad Remnants and Hezbollah
items.summary: Lebanon’s Public Prosecutor has completed the initial phase of the inquiry and forwarded the file to the Court of Cassation Public Prosecutor to take the necessary legal measures. The post Lebanese Judiciary Moves to Prosecute Network Linked to Assad Remnants and Hezbollah first appeared on The Syrian Observer.
items.body_text:
A senior Lebanese security source confirmed to Syria TV on Sunday that preliminary investigations into a network uncovered in Akkar have reached their final stages, with the case file now transferred to the judiciary ahead of formal charges against both detained and fugitive suspects.
According to the source, Lebanon’s Public Prosecutor has completed the initial phase of the inquiry and forwarded the file to the Court of Cassation Public Prosecutor to take the necessary legal measures. The case will then move to Government Commissioner to the Military Court, Judge Claude Ghanem, who will review the indictments prepared against members of the network.
Unmasking “Hajj Alaa” and Issuing an Arrest Notice
Information obtained by Syria TV indicates that the investigation, drawing on detainees’ testimonies and communications analysis, succeeded in identifying a key operative previously known by the alias “Hajj Alaa.” Security agencies suspect he oversaw critical logistical and operational coordination on behalf of Hezbollah within the network’s activities. He is a senior official in the Coordination and Liaison Unit headed by Hezbollah commander Hussein Al-Abdallah.
Following his identification, his name and personal data were circulated among Lebanese security and military agencies to facilitate his arrest.
The source said “Hajj Alaa” was responsible for securing safehouses for operatives in Beirut’s southern suburbs, Zahlé and Haret Saida, overseeing their logistical needs, and channeling funds and salaries to trainees through a charity linked to Hezbollah’s support base.
Data Extraction May Open New Security Files
In parallel with the judicial process, specialized security units continue to analyze confiscated phones and electronic devices. The source reported that extracted data has begun revealing communications and names extending beyond the immediate case, intersecting with other ongoing security files, including the targeting of the Mezzeh Military Airport in Damascus and security incidents along the Syrian coast.
Judicial authorities expect that the forensic analysis will trigger separate investigations and lead to the pursuit of additional individuals not included in the primary list of detainees.
In the next phase, charges are expected to cover the five detained individuals as well as several fugitives sought in absentia, including “Hajj Alaa” and Syrian figures implicated in the testimonies. The dossier will then be transferred to the First Military Investigating Judge to finalize the judicial probe and assign responsibilities within the network.
Background on the Arrests
The case dates back to early September, when a Lebanese judicial source told Agence France-Presse (AFP) that five individuals had been arrested—three Syrians and two Lebanese, including a former colonel in the ousted regime’s intelligence apparatus. Security forces also seized machine guns, hand grenades, sniper rifles and explosives.
The source added that network members had undergone military training in eastern Lebanon administered by Hezbollah fighters, with initial findings suggesting they were preparing operations targeting government forces on the Syrian coast.
Senior Lebanese security sources told Syria TV that the investigation led to the arrest of five primary suspects, most notably Ali Safi, a former Air Force Intelligence officer. Suspicions also surround a former officer linked to the erstwhile “Desert Hawks” militia, who allegedly coordinated external logistics. Investigators are examining possible ties to figures close to Hezbollah and former regime officers residing in Russia.
Information obtained by Al-Sharq Al-Awsat indicated that the network operated under the direction of former Syrian Major General Mohammad Jaber, who resides in Moscow and is closely aligned with the ousted Bashar al-Assad. items.title: French Senate Delegation Holds Series of Talks in Damascus
items.summary: Syrian Parliament Speaker Abdul Hamid al-Awak received the delegation, headed by Olivier Cigolotti, in the presence of members of the parliament’s bureau. The post French Senate Delegation Holds Series of Talks in Damascus first appeared on The Syrian Observer.
items.body_text:
A delegation from the French Senate has held a series of meetings in Damascus with senior Syrian officials, focusing on parliamentary ties, bilateral relations and cooperation in the security, administrative, economic and financial fields.
Syrian Parliament Speaker Abdul Hamid al-Awak received the delegation, headed by Olivier Cigolotti, in the presence of members of the parliament’s bureau. According to the Syrian parliament, the talks focused on the importance of parliamentary diplomacy and ways to develop cooperation between Syria and France.
The French delegation also included senators Étienne Blanc, Nicole Duranton and Michel Gréaume, as well as Jean-Baptiste Faivre, chargé d’affaires at the French embassy in Damascus.
On Thursday, Interior Minister Anas Khattab met the same delegation to discuss the development of Syrian-French relations and the activation of cooperation in the security and administrative fields, according to the Interior Ministry.
The visit also included talks with Finance Minister Mohammed Yusr Barnieh on prospects for strengthening bilateral relations and expanding economic and financial cooperation and partnership.
The meetings come amid a broader effort to deepen relations between Damascus and Paris. In July, French President Emmanuel Macron visited Syria in the first visit by a French president since 2009. During the visit, the two countries signed a package of agreements and strategic memoranda of understanding aimed at expanding bilateral cooperation in several fields.

items.title: Acting prosecutor general reveals his working plans "for the coming days"
items.summary: Acting Prosecutor General Anton Kovalskyi outlined his priorities for the coming days, including high-profile cases, personnel issues and cooperation with NABU and SAPO.
items.body_text:
Acting prosecutor general reveals his working plans "for the coming days"
Acting prosecutor general Anton Kovalskyi has said what he plans to focus on in his first days in the role, and promised to engage with the National Anti-Corruption Bureau of Ukraine (NABU) and the Specialised Anti-Corruption Prosecutor's Office (SAPO) "professionally and within the law".
Source: Kovalskyi on Facebook
Quote: "Yesterday [17 September – ed.], I was entrusted with performing the duties of prosecutor general. I am taking up this work during a difficult period for the Prosecutor's Office, and I fully understand the responsibility I am now taking on. The first thing I want to note is this: the work of the Prosecutor's Office is uninterrupted."
Details: Kovalskyi named organising the work of the Prosecutor General's Office and oblast prosecutor's offices, and ensuring the results of that work, as his top priority.
Quote: "I have identified several specific steps for the coming days. I will hold working meetings with the heads of key areas at the Office and regional prosecutor's offices. We need to go through problem areas, high-profile cases, and personnel matters and decisions that cannot be delayed in a substantive way."
More details: Kovalskyi also plans to complete disciplinary and personnel procedures already under way against Prosecutor General's Office employees, in connection with "circumstances currently being examined as part of the Carthage operation".
Quote: "We will not accuse anyone before guilt is established through the procedure set out in law. But the position of prosecutor also cannot be a reason to protect someone or create special conditions for them."
More details: Kovalskyi promises to engage with NABU and SAPO "professionally and within the law".
Quote: "I understand the public interest, and I'm ready for a direct and substantive conversation. I will answer all the questions being raised today, including those directed at me personally. In the near future, I'll be able to talk not just about my vision, but about steps already taken and initial results."
Background: On 17 September, Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy issued a decree appointing Anton Kovalskyi, Head of Khmelnytskyi Oblast Prosecutor's Office, as acting prosecutor general.

items.title: Ukraine Launches Carpathian Eight Cooperation Format
items.summary: Ukraine launched the Carpathian Eight (C8), a new regional cooperation format bringing together eight European countries and EU institutions. The initiative will focus on security, energy resilience, transport links, investment and cross-border economic projects.
items.body_text:
Ukraine launched the Carpathian Eight (C8), a new regional cooperation format bringing together eight European countries at a founding summit in Bukovel, on Friday, Sept. 18, in western Ukraine’s Ivano-Frankivsk region.
The initiative was announced during the first session of the three-day C8 Summit, which runs through Sunday. EU representatives, local authorities, businesses and investors are also taking part.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
What is the C8?
The C8 format includes Ukraine, Romania, Serbia, Poland, Slovakia, the Czech Republic, Austria and Hungary.
EU institutions are also participating in the initiative, which is designed to connect governments, regional administrations, businesses and communities across the wider Carpathian region.
The organizers present C8 as a platform for security cooperation, economic development, investment and cross-border projects rather than as a new military alliance.
The summit’s official program includes discussions on regional security, energy resilience, industrial cooperation, transport corridors, agriculture, tourism and cultural ties. More than 500 business representatives and international investors have been invited.
“Another strong element of EU interaction”
President Volodymyr Zelensky said the summit marked the first time that all Carpathian countries had gathered in Ukraine’s part of the region.
“We are launching a new C8 format – the Carpathian Eight – uniting us and our neighbors in Europe: Romania, Serbia, Poland, Slovakia, the Czech Republic, Austria, Hungary and, of course, the European Union as a whole,” Zelensky said in a statement published on his official Telegram channel.
‘Waiting for Death’: Russian-Occupied Oleshky Faces Starvation as Russia Blocks Aid and Evacuation
He said the initiative should create “another strong element of interaction at the EU level,” focusing on security, energy, expanded logistics, cross-border economic cooperation and support for local communities.
Zelensky welcomed the presidents of Romania and Serbia, the prime minister of Poland and representatives of Slovakia, the Czech Republic and Austria. Hungarian representatives were expected to join the summit later, according to state media Ukrinform.
Vucic highlights transport links
Serbian President Aleksandar Vučić attended the summit at Zelensky’s invitation. He said Serbia could cooperate with Romania, Hungary, Ukraine and Poland on transport and infrastructure.
“We have much to offer – from railway lines and roads to more open borders,” Vučić said.
He also said cooperation could include agriculture and other sectors, adding that his participation aimed to preserve stability and peace for Serbia and its citizens.
Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk’s participation comes amid growing concern over Russian hybrid threats against NATO’s eastern flank. Before traveling to Ukraine, Tusk warned that Russia could use drones or missiles in attacks designed to test the alliance’s unity.
$10.7B in projects presented
The summit’s investment program includes 90 projects totaling $10.7 billion, according to the official C8 Summit website.
The largest share consists of 33 energy projects worth about $7.28 billion. The proposed portfolio also includes transport and logistics projects worth about $1.05 billion, 17 industrial projects valued at about $782 million, and initiatives in infrastructure, agriculture, healthcare and technology.
The summit is scheduled to continue through Sunday, with further discussions on industrial cooperation, energy security, transport corridors, agricultural value chains and tourism.

items.title: Deepfakes, Fake News and ‘Rigged’ Vote Claims: Russia Targets France’s 2027 Election
items.summary: Russian disinformation networks are targeting potential French presidential candidates with deepfakes, fabricated reports and false health claims ahead of the 2027 election, according to Ukraine’s Center for Strategic Communications. The campaigns also target France’s electoral institutions, with Telegram and anonymous websites emerging as key channels for spreading pro-Kremlin narratives.
items.body_text:
Russian disinformation networks are already targeting potential contenders in France’s 2027 presidential election, using deepfakes, fabricated media reports and false claims about politicians’ health and alleged corruption, according to an analysis by Ukraine’s Center for Strategic Communications.
France has become the second-most targeted country for Russian foreign information manipulation and interference (FIMI), behind only Ukraine, according to the European External Action Service’s fourth threat report, published in March 2026.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
The new report, shared by state media Ukrinform, recorded 107 major Russian information attacks targeting France in 2025, compared with 112 against Ukraine.
The campaign has intensified as France prepares for its April 18, 2027 presidential election. A second round is scheduled for May 2 if required. President Emmanuel Macron, who has served two terms, is constitutionally barred from seeking another.
Russian-linked networks have already targeted three potential successors: former Prime Minister Édouard Philippe, former Prime Minister Gabriel Attal and European Parliament member Raphaël Glucksmann.
Deepfakes target potential candidates
One of the first identified operations was Storm-1516, a Russian disinformation network known for fabricated videos, deepfakes and false testimonies.
The network targeted Philippe, the former prime minister and mayor of Le Havre, with false claims about his health.
Russia’s First Duma Election Since the Full-Scale Invasion: What’s the Significance?
Glucksmann was later targeted by the same operation. A fake news website designed to resemble French outlet Blast claimed that Glucksmann’s wife was trying to bribe media organizations to improve his image ahead of the election.
                                                                                                                                                                         
The operation also allegedly stole the identities of French journalists and used fabricated documents to support its claims.
Another Russian-linked operation, Matryoshka, targeted Attal.
Fake videos styled to resemble reports by French outlets including Le Figaro and Libération circulated online, linking Attal to alleged political scandals.
Some posts falsely claimed that Attal had been hospitalized or suffered from Parkinson’s disease. Other fabricated claims alleged that he paid media outlets to spread disinformation about himself and was considering staging an assassination attempt and blaming Russia.
Russia also targets France’s electoral system
Ukraine’s Center for Strategic Communications said the campaigns go beyond attacks on individual politicians.
The Portal Kombat operation, particularly its network of Pravda-branded websites, has targeted French institutions and the electoral process itself, according to the analysis.
The network includes sites such as francais.news-pravda.com and fr.news-pravda.com, which operate as automated content amplifiers.
                                                                                                                                                                         
One recurring narrative portrays Viginum, France’s agency responsible for countering foreign digital interference, as an instrument of “total control and censorship.”
The messaging, according to the Ukrainian analysis, helps lay the groundwork for claims that the 2027 election will be manipulated by the authorities.
Other narratives claim France has lost its sovereignty to the US and suggest that a future French president should leave NATO and restore relations with Russia.
The campaigns also promote conspiracy theories portraying French authorities as corrupt and unaccountable, while exploiting divisive issues including LGBTQ and gender-related topics.

items.title: Russia Offering Tours of ‘Sites of Military Glory’ in Donetsk and Kursk
items.summary: The Kursk regional governor Alexander Khinshtein announced an initiative to offer tourists the chance to visit sites where the Russian military and its allies conducted operations against Ukraine. This follows a plans to to develop so-called "military tourism" in the Russian-occupied part of the Donetsk region announced in late 2025.
items.body_text:
Kursk region Governor Alexander Khinshtein said regional officials were working with the military to identify potential tourist routes through areas linked to combat operations, according to The Moscow Times.
The routes could include defensive structures and underground facilities used by Russian military personnel during fighting in the region.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
“The events we have tragically lived through are also a crucial component of patriotic tourism. My colleagues in the Armed Forces and I are already considering which underground structures and defensive sites to include in future tourist routes and where to establish museum spaces,” Khinshtein said.
He added that the tours could include facilities where North Korean military personnel had been stationed.
“I am certain that visiting and seeing the underground command posts used to direct troops – or the command post where our comrades-in-arms from the Korean People’s Army were stationed – will be extremely interesting.”
Khinshtein said authorities were already working on the project without waiting for the end of what Moscow calls its “special military operation.”
Why Kursk?
On Aug. 6, 2024, the Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU) launched a surprise offensive into Russia’s Kursk region, breaking through Russian defenses and seizing territory inside Russia.
At its peak, a senior Ukrainian military source said Kyiv controlled around 1,376 square kilometers of Russian territory.
Russia Employs 25,000 North Koreans in Drone Production
The operation was the largest foreign incursion into internationally recognized Russian territory since World War II.
Kyiv said one of its objectives was to force Russia to redirect troops and equipment to Kursk and relieve pressure on Ukrainian forces elsewhere. Early in the operation, military analysts said the incursion forced Moscow to reconsider how much manpower and equipment it needed to defend its border with northeastern Ukraine. Kyiv Post reported
Russia gradually retook much of the territory over the following months.
A major counteroffensive in March 2025 forced Ukrainian troops from most of their remaining positions. On March 16, Ukraine’s General Staff confirmed its withdrawal from Sudzha, the largest Russian town Kyiv had controlled.
Moscow announced in late April that it had expelled Ukrainian forces from the region, although Kyiv disputed claims that Ukrainian operations along the border had completely ended.
North Korean troops played a significant role in the Russian counteroffensive.
Around 12,000 North Korean soldiers were initially deployed to the Kursk region, according to Western and Ukrainian assessments, with additional troops later sent as reinforcements. Kyiv Post reported in January that the North Korean contingent was suffering heavy casualties in the fighting.
Russia and North Korea publicly acknowledged the deployment in April 2025 after months of avoiding official confirmation. Pyongyang said its troops had helped Russian forces regain control of the Kursk region. Kyiv Post reported
The overall military impact of Ukraine’s Kursk operation remains debated.
Kyiv argued that the incursion forced Russia to commit substantial manpower and equipment to its own territory and helped reduce the threat to neighboring Sumy region.
The Institute for the Study of War later assessed that the operation had successfully pinned Russian combat power, including elite airborne and naval infantry units, although its longer-term impact remained unclear. Kyiv Post reported
Other analysts argued that deploying experienced Ukrainian formations to Kursk put additional pressure on Kyiv’s defenses elsewhere while Russian forces continued advancing in eastern Ukraine.
The proposed tourism project is also being developed while the Kursk region remains exposed to Ukrainian drone and artillery attacks.

items.title: Согласившуюся занять место Пугачевой Долину призвали быть скромнее
items.body_text:
Музыкальный критик Евгений Бабичев призвал со скепсисом отнестись к заявлению певицы Ларисы Долиной о готовности стать новой примадонной. Его комментарий приводит «Абзац».
«Уж точно не Долина сама должна решать, кто станет следующей примадонной. Выделять должен зритель продажей билетов и миллионами прослушиваний на стриминг-платформах. Что-то мне кажется, что Долина не замечена ни в том ни в другом», — подчеркнул собеседник издания.
Бабичев добавил, что россияне не поняли и не приняли поведение Долиной в ситуации с продажей квартиры. Он отметил, что считает артистку большим профессионалом, однако призвал ее быть скромнее и не выбирать себе званий.
«Мне кажется, надо быть немножко поскромнее. В каждой шутке есть только доля шутки», — заключил критик.
Ранее Долина иронично согласилась стать примадонной российской эстрады вместо уехавшей из страны Аллы Пугачевой, если ей предложат это звание. Известно, что неофициальное звание примадонны отечественного шоу-бизнеса закрепилось за Пугачевой после того, как она исполнила одноименную песню на «Евровидении» в 1997 году. По словам самой артистки, она посвятила эту композицию актрисе Людмиле Гурченко.

О том, что Путин принял участие в голосовании на выборах в Госдуму стало известно 18 сентября. Российский лидер отдал свой голос в онлайн-формате.
Ранее президент подчеркивал, что на выборах будет важен голос каждого избирателя. По словам главы государства, от решения граждан зависит, какие политические силы станут представлять их интересы.
