Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support.
An MP from Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk’s party, the centrist Civic Coalition (KO), has been detained by anti-corruption officers after parliament approved a request from the European Public Prosecutor’s Office to lift his legal immunity.
It is the first time in history that the EPPO, which Tusk’s government signed Poland up to in one of its first actions after taking power in 2023, has taken action against a sitting Polish member of parliament.
Poseł Wojciech Król został doprowadzony do biura Prokuratury Europejskiej w Katowicach. Śledczy zamierzają przedstawić mu zarzuty dotyczące przestępstw korupcyjnych i przesłuchać.https://t.co/AknEyHwIHL
— PolsatNews.pl (@PolsatNewsPL) September 18, 2026
The MP in question, Wojciech Król, is accused of trading in influence in relation to the EU-funded modernisation of tram infrastructure in the Upper Silesian-Zagłębie Metropolis, an agglomeration of municipalities in southern Poland that includes Katowice, a major city.
The EPPO says it has found evidence of “a system of corruption” that involved inflated costs and fictitious work on the project, for which 1.9 billion zloty (€435 million) of EU funds were designated.
Its investigation found that, as part of this system, a member of parliament – not named directly by the EPPO but who is known to be Król – had “accepted financial benefits in exchange for arranging favourable outcomes for several companies”.
Polish news website Interia reports that the EPPO suspects Król of accepting over 1.4 million zloty in bribes. The MP has publicly denied the accusation.
Eleven other people have already been charged in relation to the alleged corruption scheme, reports broadcaster TVN. They include senior executives from a municipal tram operator.
In May, the EPPO submitted a first request to Poland’s parliament to lift the immunity that Król enjoys as an MP and bring him into detention. At the time, Król was deputy head of KO’s caucus in the Sejm, the lower house of parliament, but he has since lost that position and been suspended from the caucus entirely.
In late July, a majority of MPs in the Sejm approved the lifting of Król’s immunity to face prosecution. However, at the same time, they rejected the EPPO’s request for Król to be taken into detention, after MPs from the ruling coalition voted against it.
The same week those votes took place, the EPPO issued a second request, outlining additional evidence and suspicions regarding Król’s alleged involvement in corruption.
On Thursday this week, the Sejm voted almost unanimously in favour of that second request, again lifting Król’s immunity to face further charges but this time also approving his detention. A few hours later, officers from Poland’s Central Anti-Corruption Bureau (CBA) arrested Król in Warsaw.

“This is how a state of law operates, in which parliamentary credentials and party colors offer no immunity from criminal liability,” wrote justice minister Waldemar Żurek on social media. “There are no sacred cows.”

Poland’s prime minister, Donald Tusk, has warned that, according to intelligence sources, Russia is planning drone and missile strikes on eastern NATO countries, which it would present as accidental.
Addressing parliament on Thursday, the prime minister said that “citizens absolutely have the right to know what scenario can be expected based on the information available today”. Intelligence from allies, including the United States and Ukraine, indicates that various scenarios are possible, but one is most likely, said Tusk.
Over the next few months, Russia’s recent tactic of using jet-powered drones to strike targets in Ukraine near the Polish border will likely continue, said Tusk, as well as attacks on Ukrainian economic and logistics infrastructure, such as railways.
“Russia’s plan, according to intelligence, also includes hybrid drone and missile strikes against countries supporting Ukraine, including Poland,” continued Tusk. “These possibilities have been discussed for some time. This information is now very consistent and, unfortunately, convincing.”

The aim, said Tusk, would be to “weaken NATO member states’ motivation to apply appropriate NATO regulations in the event of aggression against any member state”. Russia’s “official narrative will be that this is an accident and there’s no reason for anyone to consider any kind of NATO response”.
The prime minister said that the incidents could be similar in nature to the night one year ago when around 20 Russian drones entered Polish airspace across its eastern border.
“These ‘random’ attacks could repeat themselves, becoming an increasingly glaring illustration of NATO’s helplessness, as conceived by the Russians,” said Tusk.
In response to last year’s drone incursions, Polish and allied NATO jets shot down some of the drones. Poland then invoked article 4 of the NATO treaty and received increased air-defence support from a number of NATO allies.
Russia has recently stepped up its attacks on western Ukraine, including a number of strikes close to the Polish border. Tusk noted that, in response, Poland has begun reinforcing security at border crossings, including installing 28 new bomb shelters and expanding air-defence systems

On the night of Thursday to Friday, the latest round of Russia attacks on Ukraine prompted Poland to scramble aircraft, activate air-defence systems, and close parts of its eastern airspace – actions that have recently become increasingly common.

Warsaw has launched special joint patrols by its municipal police and roads authority to check whether electric scooters are being parked legally and in keeping with rules introduced under a recent agreement with rental firms.

An agreement reached between the city and three scooter operators – Bolt, Dott and Lime – in May expanded the number of streets where the vehicles are subject to a maximum speed of 12 km/h (7.5 mph) and increased the areas where their use is entirely prohibited.
It also introduced measures to prevent scooters from being left in places where parking is illegal. Riding and parking electric scooters was banned in several areas of Warsaw, including popular tourist attractions such as the Old Town, Krasiński Garden and Łazienki Park.
Trzaskowski added that the city has now expanded the list of areas covered by the ban, as permitted under the agreement. He did not, however, provide the new list.
The agreement requires operators to programme their scooters so they cannot enter areas where riding is prohibited or be parked in places where parking is illegal, including on bridges, in tunnels, in residential areas and on streets where the pavement is too narrow to allow legal parking.
Operators can be fined when scooters are left in violation of the rules.
The city says that, despite electric scooters accounting for just under 8% of all traffic on cycle lanes, their riders were found to be responsible for 39 of the 66 accidents recorded on cycle lanes last year. Those accidents resulted in 73 injuries.
Concerns over the safety of electric scooters have also prompted the national government to introduce stricter rules, including a nationwide requirement for children under 16 to wear a bicycle helmet when riding bicycles and electric scooters, which took effect in early June.
Poland first introduced regulations governing electric scooters in 2021, formally setting out rules for their use. Under those rules, scooters are generally required to use cycle lanes where available, with their maximum speed capped at 20 km/h.
The Polish government has moved to introduce new rules on the use of electric scooters.

items.title: Prosecutors drop case against man who arranged break‑in to retrieve his cat
items.summary: The Northern District Prosecutor's Office has closed a criminal case against a man who arranged a break‑in at a stranger's apartment to retrieve his missing cat.
items.body_text:
Prosecutors drop case against man who arranged break‑in to retrieve his cat
The Northern District Prosecutor's Office has closed a criminal case against a man who arranged a break‑in at a stranger's apartment to retrieve his missing cat.
The cat had ended up with the nonprofit Cats Help, which then placed it with a temporary caretaker who refused to return the animal and posted a misleading social‑media message claiming the cat had gone missing from her care, writes Postimees.
The owner recognized his cat and decided to retrieve the pet himself. Before acting, he called the emergency number 112 to ask what punishment he might face and explained his motives.
At the apartment, he pried open a window left ajar for ventilation but did not dare enter himself. Instead, he hired a random passerby, offering a bottle of vodka to persuade him to go inside.
Police opened a criminal investigation under the statute covering incitement and assistance in unlawfully entering a dwelling. Prosecutors later determined that continuing the case was not in the public interest and that the man's culpability was low.
Prosecutors considered the man's cooperation, his explanation of motives, and his willingness to compensate for the damage. He must pay €152.50 for the window repair and €475 for the procedural costs, both due by January 17.
Link to Postimees article (in Estonian)
--
Editor: Argo Ideon
Source: Postimees

items.title: Olympic medalists Henry Sildaru, Eileen Gu join X Games' Golden State
items.summary: Estonian freestyle skier and Olympic silver medalist Henry Sildaru was drafted to XC Golden State, where he'll team up with gold medalist Eileen Gu in the new X Games league.
items.body_text:
Olympic medalists Henry Sildaru, Eileen Gu join X Games' Golden State
Estonian freestyle skier and Olympic silver medalist Henry Sildaru was drafted to XC Golden State, where he'll team up with gold medalist Eileen Gu in the new X Games league.
The X Games will consists of three stages this season, with 40 athletes selected for the league's new team format.
Golden State, led by 1998 Olympic moguls gold medalist Jonny Moseley, selected Sildaru in the fourth round of the 2026 winter draft in Los Angeles this week.
Among others, Sildaru will team up with Chinese-American freestyle skiing star and San Francisco native Eileen Gu, who competed against his sister Kelly Sildaru in Milano Cortina. Gu also had a say in assembling the California-based team.
"Being picked 26th out of more than 200 names means a lot," Sildaru wrote on social media, noting that many strong athletes, including multiple X Games winners, were left out of the draft.
Some could still receive invitations to compete individually, he said, but only the 40 team selections will compete in the team event.
Golden State's roster also includes New Zealand's Luca Harrington, Australia's Scotty James, Japan's Mari Fukada and Hiroto Ogiwara, Finland's Anni Karava, Norway's Marcus Kleveland, American Lily Dhawornvej and fellow fourth-round pick Lainey Steen of the U.S.
'Busiest season of my life' ahead
Henry Sildaru will also compete in FIS World Cup events and the world championships this season.
"Now things are gonna get interesting," he said, describing the coming season as likely the busiest of his career. He still has several training camps and final preparations ahead before competition begins.
"Most likely the busiest season of my life and definitely one of the most challenging," he added.
--
Editor: Siim Boikov, Aili Vahtla

items.body_text:
Number of medical residents hits record high
This fall, 187 new medical residents began specialist training at the University of Tartu, bringing the total number of residents to a record 891. In recent years, interest and competition have intensified in critical specialties such as family medicine and emergency medicine, the university said.
Of the students who graduated from the basic medical program this year, 78 percent applied for specialist training at the University of Tartu. The residency admissions competition received 318 applications — significantly more than in previous years.
Family medicine received the highest number of applications, while the tightest competition was in oral and maxillofacial surgery, with nine candidates per training spot. Dermatovenerology, pediatric surgery, and otorhinolaryngology (ear‑nose‑throat) also saw high demand.
Forty‑six residents entered family medicine this year — the highest number ever.
As the number of residents grows, the university is expanding its training offerings. To support residents, the University of Tartu is launching a mentorship system and developing a digital e‑portfolio learning environment.

items.title: Turkey Arrests Fund Managers Over Stock Market Manipulation Scandal
items.summary: Authorities arrest fund managers suspected of manipulating markets and liquidate 130 troubled investment funds as turmoil roils country's financial industry.
items.body_text:
Turkey Arrests Fund Managers Over Stock Market Manipulation Scandal
Turkish authorities arrested four suspects on Friday, including investment fund board members, and imposed travel bans on 51 others, as part of an investigation into alleged manipulation of the stock market, Justice Minister Akin Gurlek announced.
Courts have also imposed precautionary measures on accounts and other assets linked to those under investigation, to prevent their transfer, Gurlek said.
“Those who exploit the sweat, labour and savings of our citizens will be held accountable before the law,” he added.
Turkey’s Capital Markets Board, SPK, has filed criminal complaints about alleged manipulative transactions in several funds and listed shares.
In a separate investigation, a court ordered access blocked to 246 social media accounts accused of publishing speculative material capable of causing fear or panic among investors.
Another investigation by prosecutors in Istanbul’s Bakirkoy District has resulted in 16 arrests over social media posts allegedly intended to manipulate capital markets, Gurlek said.
Turkish Interior Minister Mustafa Ciftci on Thursday said operations related to the stock market investigation would continue, suggesting further action is likely.
On Thursday the SPK ordered the liquidation of 130 funds managed by seven portfolio management companies after liquidity problems contributed to sharp market losses.
Trading on Istanbul Stock Exchange was temporarily suspended on Wednesday after the benchmark BIST 100 index fell by more than 6 per cent, triggering a market-wide circuit breaker.
Estimates of the combined size of the 130 funds differ.
According to Reuters, their assets are worth around 21.4 billion US dollars, involving about 353,000 investors. CNBC-e puts the total at about 19.8 billion US dollars and the number of investors at more than 514,000.
Liquidation does not mean that the investors’ money has been confiscated. Instead, banks are being tasked to deliver citizens’ money in these funds. Is Bank has been appointed to handle the liquidation of funds managed by Tera Portfoy, while state-owned Ziraat Bank will oversee funds belonging to the six other managers.
The proceeds will be distributed to investors according to their holdings. However, investors may not recover the last reported value of their holdings, as the final amount will depend on prices achieved when the assets are sold.
The crisis intensified after regulatory changes targeted risks associated with funds concentrated in thinly traded shares.
“It has been observed that some funds have caused price movements that cannot be explained by the financial realities of companies,” the SPK said on Thursday, adding that the new measures were aimed at preventing market manipulation and increasing transparency.

items.title: Expelled by Greece’s Ruling Party, Ex-PM Samaras Plots His Revenge
items.summary: Seventy-five years-old and expelled from his party, former Greek Prime Minister Antonis Samaras shows no sign of going quietly into the night. Should Kyriakos Mitsotakis be worried?
items.body_text:
At the beginning of September, former Greek prime minister Antonis Samaras seized on a newspaper report that users of the online platform of the Greek health service were allowed to specify gender options beyond ‘Male’ and ‘Female’, to include ‘Other’ and ‘Undetermined’.
Samaras was expelled from Greece’s ruling New Democracy party last year, and still bears a grudge.
He promptly took to Facebook to accuse the conservative government of promoting a “woke agenda” and echoed erroneous claims that school textbooks were depicting families with same-sex parents.
“The only thing ‘undetermined’ here is the extent of the ideological shift within the ruling party,” Samaras wrote. Greek families “need support, not redefinition”, he claimed.

items.title: EU Should Not Turn a Blind Eye to Montenegro’s Bloody Clan War
items.summary: As Montenegro gets ever closer to EU membership, Brussels’ seeming determination not to acknowledge the gang warfare still plaguing the country is puzzling – and irresponsible.
items.body_text:
When Montenegro declared independence in 2006, it identified EU and NATO integration as its strategic priorities. The country applied for EU membership in 2008, accession negotiations began in 2012, and NATO membership followed in 2017.
Yet, beneath the language of democratisation and Europeanisation lies a far less reassuring reality: a country where rival organised crime clans have waged a conflict for more than a decade, with dozens of people murdered, including innocent bystanders – and where allegations of links between criminal groups, police officers, and senior judicial figures have repeatedly surfaced
The question is not merely why Montenegro has struggled to defeat organised crime. It is why this conflict appears to have become increasingly peripheral to the European Union’s public assessment of the country.
The origins of Montenegro’s interclan war are generally traced to a dispute involving the disappearance of almost 200 kilograms of cocaine in Valencia, Spain, in 2014. What followed was a violent confrontation between two criminal groups based in the coastal town of Kotor – the Kavac and Skaljari clans. Most of the country’s organised crime groups eventually aligned themselves with one of the two rival groups.
Kotor itself became a symbol of the problem. The UNESCO World Heritage Site and historic home of both clans was described by then Interior Minister Goran Danilovic as a “hostage town.” Investigations subsequently alleged the existence of surveillance networks used by criminal gangs and the disclosure of confidential police information to members of the Kavac clan.

items.title: Bakery Giant Eyes Foreign Markets After Major Domestic Expansion
items.summary: With an investment of 11 billion forints (€30 million), Hungarian bakery giant Félegyházi Pékség Kft. officially commissioned a new production hall and logistics center on Thursday at its headquarters in the southern Hungarian city of Kiskunfélegyháza. The first greenfield project in the company’s history creates 200 new jobs in the region and lays the foundations […] The post Bakery Giant Eyes Foreign Markets After Major Domestic Expansion appeared first on Hungary Today.
items.body_text:
Central and Eastern Europe’s largest-capacity bakery is expected to produce 100 tons of bread daily.Continue reading
With an investment of 11 billion forints (€30 million), Hungarian bakery giant Félegyházi Pékség Kft. officially commissioned a new production hall and logistics center on Thursday at its headquarters in the southern Hungarian city of Kiskunfélegyháza. The first greenfield project in the company’s history creates 200 new jobs in the region and lays the foundations for expansion into European foreign markets.
Of the total investment, 4.98 billion forints (€14 million) comes from funding provided by the Hungarian government and the European Union. The company financed the remaining amount from its own resources.
The facility operates on a newly developed 9,000-square-meter site and features a high degree of automation.
The centerpiece of the facility comprises four industrial production lines for fine pastries, frozen spirals, as well as fully automated packaging and palletizing systems using robotic technology. The complex is complemented by a semi-automated frozen warehouse operated with automated guided vehicles, with capacity for 6,000 pallets.
The expansion doubles the company’s capacity in frozen baked goods:
- Hourly output: Up to 50,000 units on the new lines
- Annual capacity: More than 200 million units
- Total operating area: Increased to more than 26,000 square meters
As Gergő Gulyás, managing director and co-owner, explained, the facility is intended not only to consolidate the company’s dominant position in the domestic market but also to serve as a springboard for increased exports to Europe.
The plant, which was built in just twelve months, is currently operating at around 40 percent capacity. This is expected to reach 65 to 70 percent by the end of the year, with full-capacity operation targeted for mid-2027.
Company owner István Gulyás looked back on the development of the family business on the occasion of its 25th anniversary. When he took over the company in 2001, after it had been founded in 1999 with 20 employees, between 80 and 100 people were producing baked goods on 2,000 square meters, with monthly flour consumption of 100 to 120 tons.
Today, the company processes more than 2,000 tons of flour per month. For the full year 2026, the company expects to achieve the highest production volume in its history. More than 42 million kilograms of baked goods—over 370 million individual units—are expected to be produced and distributed.
As the new capacities are ramped up, the total workforce will gradually increase to 2,000 employees.
At the official handover ceremony, László Búza, State Secretary for Food Industry, Food Distribution and Food Culture, highlighted the project’s importance for the country. Ensuring the population’s supply of high-quality food is a key national task, he said.
The new facility demonstrates that Hungary’s food industry can catch up with the global technological forefront.
In addition to its traditional product range, the company, which accounts for more than ten percent of the Hungarian market, specifically caters to demand for vegan, allergen-free, wholegrain and diabetic-friendly products. The State Secretary also praised the use of energy-efficient refrigeration technology, the integration of employees with reduced working capacity, and cooperation with the University of Veterinary Medicine Budapest.
József Csányi, mayor of Kiskunfélegyháza, emphasized the company’s importance as a local engine of employment.
Over the past twelve years alone, the bakery has created more than 1,300 jobs at the site.
Félegyházi Pékség Kft. is 100 percent owned by a second-generation Hungarian family and relies on a two-pillar distribution network consisting of its own stores and wholesale customers. The bakery group, which holds a significant position in the domestic market, currently operates 92 of its own specialty stores and works with more than 500 partners, including retail chain

items.summary: A professional delegation from the Land Forces of the Hungarian Defense Forces Joint Operations Command and a delegation from the Turkish General Staff held discussions on opportunities for joint international training exercises. The Hungarian delegation was led by Brigadier General Zsolt Molnár, Deputy Commander for Land Forces at the Hungarian Defense Forces Joint Operations Command, […] The post Hungary and Türkiye Explore New Opportunities for Joint Military Training appeared first on Hungar
items.body_text:
The facility is suitable for the maintenance and repair of components such as running gear, auxiliary equipment, and weapon systems.Continue reading
A professional delegation from the Land Forces of the Hungarian Defense Forces Joint Operations Command and a delegation from the Turkish General Staff held discussions on opportunities for joint international training exercises. The Hungarian delegation was led by Brigadier General Zsolt Molnár, Deputy Commander for Land Forces at the Hungarian Defense Forces Joint Operations Command, while the Turkish side was represented by Brigadier General Kamil Tumba, Head of Defense Planning and Project Management at the Turkish Land Forces Command.
The visit provided an opportunity for the two nations to build on their existing cooperation and expand knowledge sharing into new areas, primarily in the fields of drone technology, technical support, and chemical defense.
The Turkish delegation learned about the Hungarian Defense Forces’ training system, with particular emphasis on the C-IED training offered by the Hungarian Defense Forces Non-Commissioned Officers’ Academy—that is, training in countering improvised explosive devices.
Another key topic of discussion was the use of these drones.
Based on the Turkish side’s experience, drones are indispensable tools in modern warfare, which is why as many soldiers as possible must learn to use them. The parties also discussed mutual training opportunities in this regard.
The Turkish delegates then visited the Central Firing and Training Range, where they were briefed on the core missions of the Hungarian Defense Forces’ 30th Kinizsi Pál Armored Infantry Brigade by Colonel István Hattyár, the brigade commander. The subsequent static and dynamic demonstrations focused on the Lynx infantry fighting vehicle.
The parties also reviewed equipment from the Turkish defense industry currently in service with the Hungarian Defense Forces (such as the Gidrán) and discussed their operational experiences with these systems. The two-day professional program concluded with a staff-level meeting, during which the two NATO member states identified areas in which they could support each other’s training efforts.
Via honvedelem.hu; Featured photo: honvedelem.hu

items.title: MOL Focuses on Solar and Energy Storage Technology at Algyő Gas Plant
items.summary: MOL’s new solar farm and electricity storage system, built with an investment of 21.575 billion forints (59.4 million euros), were officially handed over on Thursday at the group’s gas plant in Algyő, southern Hungary. György Bacsa, managing director of MOL Hungary, said at the ceremony that the group is striving to make its high-electricity-consumption plants […] The post MOL Focuses on Solar and Energy Storage Technology at Algyő Gas Plant appeared first on Hungary Today.
items.body_text:
The Ajka power plant ranks among the largest in Hungary in terms of both capacity and complexity.Continue reading
MOL’s new solar farm and electricity storage system, built with an investment of 21.575 billion forints (59.4 million euros), were officially handed over on Thursday at the group’s gas plant in Algyő, southern Hungary.
György Bacsa, managing director of MOL Hungary, said at the ceremony that the group is striving to make its high-electricity-consumption plants self-sufficient by supplementing them with generation and storage capacities, thereby making them as resilient as possible to any supply risks.
The 37.5 MWp solar power plant in Algyő is MOL Hungary’s ninth solar farm, bringing the combined capacity of its solar farms to more than 400 MWp.
The newly commissioned 40 MWh energy storage system—following the 80 MWh installation in Tiszaújváros—is the company’s second such facility,
the expert said. He added that thanks to the Algyő project, 13,000 metric tons of carbon dioxide emissions will be avoided annually.
The managing director explained that significant investments are needed in the Hungarian energy sector, and the energy infrastructure must be transformed.
In addition to the importance of security of supply, the expert emphasized that during crises, individual interests come to the fore, and everyone places an emphasis on sovereignty. We must adapt to changing circumstances and diversify our energy sources. Fossil fuels, nuclear power, renewable energy, geothermal energy, biogas, and biomass will all play essential roles, he noted.
Bacsa explained that, thanks to past and current developments,
the Algyő site—which has traditionally been a hub for fossil fuel-based energy production—is not subject to the European Union’s Emissions Trading System (ETS), as it has been able to reduce its carbon dioxide emissions to such a degree.
The MOL Group’s largest renewable energy portfolio is in Hungary, but significant investments have also been made in Slovakia and Croatia. MOL plans to build 500 MWh of storage capacity in Hungary by 2030, thereby contributing to the flexibility of the entire Hungarian energy system, the expert said.
The energy storage facility may also play a role in the market for system-level services operated by Mavir. When the system operator requests a reduction in consumption, the energy storage facility compensates for the amount of electricity withdrawn from the public grid to maintain generation; in the event of excess electricity, it switches to charging mode.

items.title: Deutsch Tamás: Nekünk az MTK szerelem. A szerelem pedig, amint azt hallhattuk, alapjog.
items.summary: Mindenkinek a szerelem ugrott be. Deutsch Tamás az MTK elnökeként reagált a tervezett összeférhetetlenségi szabályra.
items.body_text:
Deutsch Tamás: Nekünk az MTK szerelem. A szerelem pedig, amint azt hallhattuk, alapjog.
Kubatov Gábor (Fradi) és Szijjártó Péter (Budapest Honvéd) mellett az MTK sportegyesületének elnökét, Deutsch Tamást is érinteni fogja az a sportterületre szánt összeférhetetlenségi szabály, amit pénteken jelentett be a kormányszóvivői tájékoztatón Magyar Péter pénteken. A bejelentés előrevetíti, hogy a törvényjavaslat elfogadása után azok a nagyobb sportegyesületeknél, sportszövetségeknél dolgozó vezetők (elnök, alelnök, elnökség), akik az elmúlt években képviselői (EP is), miniszteri, miniszteri biztosi, államtitkári, pártelnöki vagy állami cégvezetői posztot töltöttek be, nem dolgozhatnak tovább a pozíciójukban.
Az összeférhetetlenség a politikai tisztség megszűnésétől kezdve négy évig fennáll (így vonatkozhat például Szijjártó Péterre is). A hivatalban lévő érintetteknek a törvény hatályba lépése után harminc napon belül kell nyilatkozniuk az összeférhetetlenségről.
A tervezett szabályra már reagált Kubatov Gábor, aki azt írta, hogy „a mi szerelmünk a Ferencvárossal egy életre szól. Holmi jogszabályokkal nem lehet széttépni! Küzdeni mindig, feladni soha!, és Havasi Bertalan, a Fidesz kommunikációs igazgatója is, aki azt mondta, „teljesen mindegy, hogy Magyar Péter mit jelent be. Összevissza beszél, egyik nap ezt mondja, másik nap azt”.
Deutsch Tamás, aki az MTK elnöke a Facebookon kommentálta a bejelentést, de az MTK-n keresztül küldött megkeresésünkre hosszabb reakciót küldött:
"Az MTK vezetőit az MTK választja, nem Magyar Péter. 
Nekünk az MTK szerelem. 
A szerelem pedig, amint azt hallhattuk, alapjog. Nem veheti el tőlünk senki. 
Bátorság. Buzgalom. Barátság. 
Hajrá, kékek, hajrá, MTK!
dr. Deutsch Tamás, 
az MTK Budapest elnöke" – írta.
Kerestük Szijjártó Pétert is, hogy reagáljon a tervezett összeférhetetlenségi szabályra, érdemi válaszáról beszámolunk.

items.title: Egy ENSZ-jelentés szerint háborús bűncselekménynek minősülhet az Egyesült Államok iráni iskola elleni támadása
items.summary: A támadásban a beszámolók szerint legalább 120 gyerek halt meg. Az ügyben az USA is vizsgálatot indított, ami még nem zárult le.
items.body_text:
Egy ENSZ-jelentés szerint háborús bűncselekménynek minősülhet az Egyesült Államok iráni iskola elleni támadása
Az Egyesült Államok iráni katonai műveleteit vizsgáló nyomozók két amerikai légicsapás esetében is „alapos okot találtak arra, hogy feltételezzék: az Egyesült Államok háborús bűncselekményt követett el azzal, hogy válogatás nélküli támadásokat indított, amelyek civilek halálát vagy sérülését, illetve polgári célpontok károsodását okozták” – írja a CNN. A független vizsgálat eredményét szeptember 17-én tette közzé az ENSZ.
A nyomozók két februári amerikai légitámadást vizsgáltak. A háború első napján az iráni hatóságok szerint legalább 160 ember halt meg Minab városában, ahol egy lányiskolát ért találat. Bár az áldozatok számáról több adat is megjelent, a hivatalos iráni beszámolók szerint legalább 120 gyerek, valamint 26 tanár és szülő halt meg a támadásban. Nem sokkal később Lamerd városában egy sportcentrumot és egy lakóövezetet ért légicsapás, ebben a támadásban az ENSZ beszámolója szerint 22 civil halt meg.
A minabi leányiskolát ért légicsapásról már az előzetes vizsgálatok is megállapították, hogy az Egyesült Államok indíthatta a támadást, a bizonyítékok alapján egy nagy pontosságú amerikai Tomahawk robotrepülőgép rombolhatta le az épületet. Akkor több amerikai lap forrásai is megerősítették, hogy az amerikai hadsereg elavult adatok alapján vette célba az iskola épületét, ezt erősítette meg az ENSZ friss jelentése is.
Az iráni célpontokat az amerikai Védelmi Hírszerző Ügynökség (DIA) információi alapján választották ki az iráni háborút levezénylő amerikai parancsnokságon, a Centcomon belül. A DIA katonai célpontként jelölte meg az iskolaépületet is, ami az iráni Forradalmi Gárda egy bázisából lett leválasztva, valamikor 2013 és 2016 között. Ez az elérhető műholdfelvételekből is kiderül: egy 2016-os felvételen például már látni lehetett, hogy az iskolát kerítéssel választották le a bázisról, és külön bejáratot is kapott. Egy 2025-ös műholdfelvételen pedig az látszott, hogy az iskola udvarán emberek csoportja játszik egy labdajátékra kialakított területen.
Azt egyelőre nem tudni, a DIA miért adta meg a célpontot elavult adatok alapján, amerikai sajtóbeszámolók szerint akár mesterséges intelligenciát használó rendszerek is hibázhattak.
Az ENSZ nyomozói műholdfelvételek, fényképek és videók segítségével rekonstruálták a támadásokat. Emellett megbízhatónak ítélt szervezeteket és szakembereket is meghallgattak, valamint több tucat interjút készítettek Iránban és Iránon kívül. Bár a nyomozók akadálytalan belépést kértek Iránba, az iráni kormány ezt nem engedélyezte. A jelentés szerint az ENSZ összes információkérésének csupán egynegyedére válaszolt Irán. A nyomozók találkozókat kértek az amerikai és az izraeli kormány tisztviselőivel is, de egyik helyről sem kaptak választ.
„Semmilyen információ nem utal arra, hogy az iskolát abban az időben katonai célokra használták volna. Az Egyesült Államok nem teljesítette azt a kötelezettségét, hogy minden tőle telhetőt megtegyen annak ellenőrzése érdekében, hogy az épület valóban katonai célpont volt-e” – állapította meg az ENSZ-jelentés.
A jelentést az ENSZ Emberi Jogi Tanácsának fogják benyújtani. Az ügyben korábban az amerikai és az izraeli hadsereg is vizsgálatot indított. A CNN megkereste az amerikai honvédelmi minisztériumot, amely arra hivatkozva nem kívánta kommentálni a jelentést, hogy a saját nyomozásuk még zajlik. Az amerikai külügyminisztérium egyik tisztviselője a CNN-nek azt mondta, a Trump-kormány nem tartja hitelesnek a jelentést. Hozzátette, az Egyesült Államok 2025 februárjában, Trump hivatalba lépése után alig néhány héttel kilépett az ENSZ Emberi Jogi Tanácsából.
A CNN szerint bár az amerikai vizsgálat első kettő, alapvető kérdéseket megválaszoló vizsgálata a támadás utáni hetekben lezajlott, a harmadik szakaszt – amelyben a DIA a műholdfelvételeket és hírszerzési információkat elemezné – azóta sem rendelte el a Pentagon. Ezt a lapnak júliusban három, egymástó

items.summary: Az amerikai elnök állítása szerint legjobban az építéshez ért, mégis a nyugati világ vezetője. Aranyozott diadalívet, márványos báltermet húzna fel, miközben a második elnökségének utolsó szakaszába ér.
items.body_text:
Trump a saját giccses ízlésére formálja Washingtont, mert másra már nem nagyon képes
„Azt hiszem, a szokás az, hogy egy diadalív előtt szükség lenne valamiféle diadalra” – mondta a Fast Company által megkérdezett szakértő arra a gigantikus méretű látványtervre, ami a Donald Trump által megálmodott, gigantikus washingtoni építményt ábrázolta. A szakértő mondata precízen összefoglalta azt, hogy mi határozza meg Trump építészeti városképi ambícióit az amerikai fővárosban. Legyen diadal, pompa, méret mindenekfelett, mint valami morális Potemkin-városban, amivel talán el lehet hitetni mindenkivel, hogy ennek a nemzetnek megy a legjobban széles e világon. „Egy építészeti atrocitás”, ahogy a Guardian újságírója fogalmazott.
Az, hogy Trump ízlése megkérdőjelezhető, nem újdonság – a Fehér Ház belseje lassan jobban hasonlít egy ecseri piacról összeválogatott, majd aranyba mártott régiségkereskedésre, mint egy nagyhatalom központi irodájára és az azt vezető ember lakosztályára. Az elnök belsőépítészeti megoldásai és átalakításai magasról tettek a pár száz éves tradícióra, inkább a rossz értelemben vett giccset, csicsát, aranyozott és márvánnyal bevont felületeket részesítették előnyben, ezzel a Fehér Házat gyakorlatilag a Trump-toronyban található lakosztályává változtatta, ahol előtte évtizedekig élt. Persze lehet mondani, hogy a négy fal között mindenki azt csinál, amit akar a dekorációval, de talán nincs még egy ilyen négy fal közötti tér, ami ekkora nyilvánosságot kapna a politikában.
Nem volt neki elég a belsőt átalakítani, Trump a dekorációt kiterjesztette a Fehér Ház keleti szárnyára is, amit a műemlékvédelem semmibevételével egyszerűen ledózerolt, hogy oda felépítse hírhedt báltermét. A bálterem Trump fixációja lett, interjúkban többször is hárított egyebek között az iráni háborúval kapcsolatos újságírói kérdéseket azzal, hogy az építkezésről kezdett el beszélni.
A terem maga elvileg abból a célból született, hogy nagyobb társasági eseményeket lehessen tartani az elnöki rezidencia mellett. Az első verzió szerint 650 fő befogadására tervezték, de ez idővel megnőtt ezerre. Trump a héten posztolta Truth Socialön az első beltéri látványterveket, amiken pontosan látni, hogy ez sem fog különösebben szakítani azzal a klasszicista Versailles-kinézettel, amiben eddig is létezett: kristálycsillárok, márványpadló, aranyozott plafon.
Maga a bálterem akkora lesz, hogy mellette a Fehér Ház is el fog törpülni. A sok-sok szeszélyes változtatás sok volt a projekt eredeti építészének, James MacCrerynek is, akinek helyébe az az építésziroda lépett, ami a Pentagon helyreállításáért is felelt a 9/11-es terrortámadás után.
Habár Trump büszkén vallja, hogy ez a gigantikus épülettoldás semmibe sem kerül az amerikai adófizetőknek, már hónapokkal ezelőtti közvélemény-kutatások is azt hozták, hogy a többség ellenzi az amúgy teljesen értelmetlen költést. Vagyis annyira nem értelmetlen: ugyanis lehet, hogy a hivatalos magyarázat szerint azért készül a bálterem, hogy százakat lehessen vendégül látni, a pincéjében egy atombiztos bunkerrendszert alakítanak ki. A keleti szárny alatt korábban is létezett még Roosevelt idejéből egy bunker, de ezt most amerikai sajtóértesülések szerint többszörös méretűre bővítik ki. Nemcsak a föld alatt, hanem a föld felett is lesznek hadászati tulajdonságai, a tetőre drónleszállópályát és légvédelmirakéta-rendszert is terveznek majd. Nemrég készült el a Fehér Ház kertjében egy óriási helikopter-leszállóhely is.
Trump bálterme az eddigi egyetlen a monstre építészeti projektek közül, aminek az előkészítése valóban elkezdődött, még ha jogilag egy időre akadályokba ütközött is a megvalósítása. A korábban bejelentett projektjei között szerepel egy szoborpark, ahova amerikai hősök emlékműveit állítanák, egyértelmű válaszként a Black Lives Matter mozgalom során levert, politikailag már megkérdőjelezhető figurák szobrainak. A parkból egyelőre még nem lett semmi, de negyvenmillió dollárnyi finanszírozást már elkülönítettek a projektre.

items.summary: Prague’s future Metro Line D has taken another step toward becoming a reality, with new preliminary designs released for two stations planned along the route. The Prague Public Transit Company (DPP) has presented renderings of the future Náměstí Míru interchange and Nusle station, offering an early look at how the new metro line could change the city’s underground transport network. The images do not represent the final appearance of either station. DPP plans to select the architectural solution
items.body_text:
Prague Unveils Future Metro Stations in Nusle and Náměstí Míru
Prague Morning
Prague’s future Metro Line D has taken another step toward becoming a reality, with new preliminary designs released for two stations planned along the route.
The Prague Public Transit Company (DPP) has presented renderings of the future Náměstí Míru interchange and Nusle station, offering an early look at how the new metro line could change the city’s underground transport network.
The images do not represent the final appearance of either station. DPP plans to select the architectural solutions through a two-stage competition, which will focus on the design of the interiors and the public spaces around the stations.
DPP intends to organise the competition in two stages, using a workshop format. The winning designs are expected to be selected within 18 months of signing the contract with the competition organiser. Preparations for that contract are currently underway.
Náměstí Míru station will connect Metro Lines A and D
The future Náměstí Míru station is planned beneath Sázavská Street, approximately 40 metres underground. It will be built using underground mining methods and will feature a single-vault design with an island platform.
The new station will be located above the existing Line A station, creating a new interchange between the two metro lines.
The design includes two vestibules equipped with escalators and a third access point with an elevator. The renderings show the planned exits towards Vinohradská, Francouzská, and Sázavská streets, as well as an elevator entrance on Korunní Street.
Metroprojekt has also presented a possible design for the outlet of a ventilation shaft in Riegrovy Sady. The structure will form part of the station’s technical infrastructure, although its final appearance may change following the architectural competition.
New Nusle station will serve Náměstí Bratří Synků
The second station featured in the new designs is the future Nusle station, which was previously known as Náměstí Bratří Synků.
The station will be built using cut-and-cover construction methods, with its island platform located approximately 13 metres below ground level. It is planned between Náměstí Bratří Synků and Otakarova Street.
Plans also include an underground parking garage for local residents above the station.
The new renderings show the proposed station entrances on Náměstí Bratří Synků, the northern vestibule beneath Otakarova Street, and the planned completion of the existing urban block.
When will Prague’s Metro Line D open?
Construction of Metro Line D began in 2022 with the section between Pankrác and Ryšánka. Work on the following section, extending towards Nové Dvory, began in June 2026.
The Pankrác–Nové Dvory section is planned to be the first part of the new metro line to open to passengers. DPP currently expects the section to enter service in the second half of 2032.

items.body_text:
Two New Squares and a Tower Planned Around Holešovice Station
Prague Morning
The area around Prague’s Nádraží Holešovice station is set for a major redevelopment after the international architectural competition for the site was won by Czech studio Chybík + Krištof.
The winning proposal envisions turning the current transport hub and surrounding brownfield into a new urban district, with two public squares, improved connections between public transport services and a new high-rise building designed to become a landmark.
The redevelopment covers roughly eight hectares around the station. Its aim is not only to add new buildings, but also to reorganise one of Prague’s important transport nodes and connect it more closely with the surrounding neighbourhood.
The competition jury selected the proposal by Chybík + Krištof as the winning design.
From transport hub to urban district
Nádraží Holešovice is currently one of Prague’s major transport interchanges, but much of the surrounding area has traditionally been used primarily for transport and other infrastructure.
The redevelopment is intended to change that. Alongside new construction, the project places emphasis on making transfers between different modes of public transport easier and fully accessible.
The project forms part of the wider Nové Holešovice development, which brings together the Prague Public Transit Company and private investors.
CPI Property, EP Real Estate, Penta Real Estate and AKIPIA are among the companies involved. The City of Prague and Prague 7 municipal district are also participating in the project.

items.body_text:
ČokoFest to Bring Three Days of Chocolate to Galerie Harfa
Prague Morning
Chocolate lovers will have plenty to discover in Prague this October as ČokoFest 2026 returns to Galerie Harfa for three days of tastings, workshops, competitions and sweet treats.
The festival will take place from October 16 to 18, 2026, at the shopping center in Prague 9. Admission is free.
Now in its 14th year, ČokoFest brings together Czech and international producers, including established chocolatiers and smaller makers.
Visitors will be able to sample and buy a wide selection of chocolates and confectionery, including handmade and bean-to-bar products, pralines, cakes, cookies and macarons.
The festival will also feature a range of less conventional chocolate and sweet specialties. Among the offerings will be a chocolate fountain, chocolate kebabs, chocolate-covered fruit, as well as chocolate-infused wine and beer. Other products on sale will include jams, liqueurs, syrups, dried fruits, honey products, coffee and tea.
Exhibitors from several European countries will join Czech producers, giving visitors the opportunity to discover different chocolate styles and specialties while shopping at international sales stalls.
ČokoFest will also feature a program of activities for both adults and children. Visitors can take part in tastings, competitions and creative workshops, while children can enjoy a dedicated zone and entertainment from performers dressed as popular children’s characters.
Cooking demonstrations will be another part of the program, with chefs from local restaurants sharing their experience and showing visitors how to prepare various sweet treats. Some workshops will also focus on chocolate-making techniques that can be tried at home.
The festival is designed as a family-friendly event, with activities taking place throughout the three days. In addition to tasting and shopping, visitors can watch pastry chefs at work, take part in competitions and learn more about the production and preparation of chocolate and other confectionery.
Opening hours:
Friday, October 16: 2:00–6:00 p.m.
Saturday, October 17: 10:00 a.m.–6:30 p.m.
Sunday, October 18: 10:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.

items.body_text:
Georgia Records 6.9% GDP Growth in Q2 2026
Georgia’s real gross domestic product (GDP) grew by 6.9% year-on-year in the second quarter of 2026, while nominal GDP reached GEL 28.147 billion, according to preliminary data released by the National Statistics Office (Geostat) on September 18.
Growth was primarily driven by increases in “value added” in several economic activities, including transportation and storage (19.8%), arts, entertainment and recreation (17.4%), information and communication (16.6%), health (15%), wholesale, retail trade, repair of motor vehicles and motorcycles (8%), and manufacturing (7.3%), Geostat said.
Meanwhile, construction declined by 4.8% and agriculture, forestry and fishing by 3.5%.
Wholesale and retail trade accounted for the largest share of GDP by economic activity, at 14.9%, followed by real estate activities at 9.1%, manufacturing at 8.9%, and information and communication at 7.6%.
Public administration and defense, as well as compulsory social security and construction, each accounted for 6.5% of GDP, while agriculture, forestry and fishing and education each made up 6.4%. Transportation and storage accounted for 6.3%.
Georgia’s economy is projected to grow by 6% in 2026, according to a report by the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), which forecasts growth to slow to 5% in 2027.
The International Monetary Fund (IMF) projects Georgia’s economy to grow by 6.5% in 2026, while expecting inflation to remain above the National Bank of Georgia’s target until mid-2027.
The United Nations’ World Economic Situation and Prospects 2026 projects Georgia’s economy to grow by 5.4% in 2026, while the World Bank has forecast 5.5% growth.
Geostat said the revised data will be published by November 13, 2026.

items.body_text:
Authorities Investigate as Dozens of Children at 20 Tbilisi Kindergartens ‘Show Signs of Intoxication’
Georgia’s Finance Ministry Investigation Service has launched an investigation after 55 children and one educator from 20 kindergartens in Tbilisi showed signs of intoxication, saying the cases “may be related to a bacterial infection” presumably linked to food consumed at the kindergartens.
The investigation comes amid reports that at least some of the affected children were hospitalized after developing symptoms such as fever, nausea, and vomiting, with doctors yet to establish the exact diagnosis, and that several kindergartens were temporarily closed.
The investigation is being conducted under Article 198, Part 2 of the Criminal Code, which concerns “the manufacturing and sale of products hazardous to human life or health that have endangered human life or health.” Tbilisi Kindergarten Management Agency, a body run by Tbilisi City Hall, separately said the educational process has been suspended at seven public kindergartens as a precaution against epidemiological risks
According to the Investigation Service, those affected include 55 children and 1 educator from the capital’s 20 kindergartens who sought medical assistance at six medical facilities. More than 50 legal representatives of the children, as well as employees of medical facilities, have already been interviewed.
“Based on the information available at this stage, the intoxication may be related to a bacterial infection, the source of which is presumably food products consumed at the kindergartens,” the Investigation Service said. “The exact product that caused the intoxication will be determined based on the results of the relevant examination.”
The agency added that “investigative and procedural activities, including searches, were intensively carried out throughout the night at 4 kindergartens and 3 companies supplying food products to kindergartens.” It noted that the searches were done in cooperation with relevant units of the Interior Ministry and the National Food Agency.
The agency said important items, documents, and food products will be seized from all kindergartens where cases of intoxication were recorded, and the public will be provided with additional information accordingly.
Separately, Tbilisi Kindergarten Management Agency said children at several public kindergartens had developed fever, nausea, and vomiting and had sought treatment at “various clinics.”
“Based on the recommendation of epidemiologists” and in accordance with the law, the agency said it had suspended the educational process at seven public kindergartens as “a precaution against epidemiological risks.” The remaining 183 kindergartens continue to operate normally, it said.
The agency added that it is taking “all necessary measures” in cooperation with the Tbilisi Epidemiological Surveillance Service, the National Food Agency, the Finance Ministry’s Investigation Service and the National Center for Disease Control and Public Health.
Maia Chkhaidze, Medical Director of Tsitsishvili Children’s Clinic, told journalists that 16 children from public kindergartens had been admitted to the clinic on September 17.
According to Chkhaidze, vomiting began in the evening, with some patients experiencing diarrhea while others did not. None had a fever, and all were from public kindergartens.
“None of the patients required resuscitation or intensive care,” she added. “However, to clarify the diagnosis, whether we are dealing with food intoxication or gastroenteritis caused by some other factor, the appropriate tests need to be carried out.”
According to Chkhaidze, the testing will be conducted by the National Center for Disease Control and Public Health.

Georgian Officials Hope For ‘2.5-Fold’ Growth in Power Generation by 2036
Georgian officials said they hope to increase power generation 2.5 times by 2036 through new investments, presenting a 10-year vision focused on “self-sufficiency,” expanded renewable generation, a greater role in energy transit, and an upgraded transmission grid.
The Georgian Dream officials, including Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze and Economy Minister Mariam Kvrivishvili, revealed their plans as they marked Energy Workers’ Day on September 17, stressing the goals for Georgia to become “fully self-sufficient in electricity by 2036” while linking the Caspian region, the Black Sea, and Europe in “a single energy space.”
According to Kvirishvili, the vision also envisages developing the Black Sea Submarine Cable, which received “Project of Mutual Interest” status from the European Union this year, as well as the broader “Green Corridor” project linking Georgia with Azerbaijan, Turkey, Bulgaria and Romania.
‘Ambitious’ 2036 Plan
Speaking at an event taking place near the Zemo Avchala Hydroelectric Power Plant, commonly known as Zahesi, Kobakhidze said that over the past year, the government had “carried out optimization in many directions” and laid the foundation for a “new vision” according to which Georgia’s energy system would develop over the next 10 years.
According to Kobakhidze, the government has a “very ambitious plan,” under which “power generation in Georgia must increase 2.5 times by 2036.”
“This is an ambitious plan, but its implementation is entirely realistic, and of course, our entire team will spare no effort to achieve it,” he said.
Kobakhidze said the government would make maximum efforts to use Georgia’s energy resources and potential “as wisely and rationally as possible,” attract new investment into the energy sector, strengthen infrastructure and support the development of modern technologies.
Kvrivishvili, for her part, said that energy security is a “national goal,” noting that “energy is one of those fields whose smooth operation is often invisible, but even one small disruption in it instantly becomes visible to the entire country.”
She stressed that people remember well, “what it meant to have an energy-weak Georgia,” where “electricity shortages were a standard everyday problem,” arguing that Georgia must no longer become “an energy-vulnerable country” and should instead be “an energy-strong, self-sufficient state of regional importance.”
As Kvrivishvili noted, over the past year, “the strong sides of the energy system, its weaknesses, opportunities, and the challenges that the state must address in advance became more clearly apparent.”
She then highlighted several completed, ongoing, and planned projects in the energy sector.
Kvrivishvili said that three hydropower plants and one wind project had already been constructed in 2026 and by the end of the year, the construction of another hydropower plant, two wind projects and three solar projects would be completed.
“This year, more than 300 megawatts of new renewable capacity will be added to Georgia’s energy system,” she said. “In 2027, with nearly USD 100 million in investment, 12 power plant projects totaling more than 70 megawatts will come into operation.”
Kvrivishvili said that in 2026, with the support of the Asian Development Bank, the government completed the procurement of 250 megawatts of energy storage batteries. Work will begin in 2026 and is expected to be completed by 2029, with Kvrivishvili arguing that it “will ensure the stable and secure functioning of the system, as well as expand the limits for integrating renewable energy.”
The minister also highlighted the authorities’ efforts to revive energy projects that had been stalled for years.

items.title: Pashinyan calls Baku’s portrayal of history ‘unacceptable’ as Azerbaijan doubles down
items.summary: The Azerbaijani official controversially portrayed Armenian heritage as Caucasian Albanian while giving diplomats a tour.
items.body_text:
Pashinyan calls Baku’s portrayal of history ‘unacceptable’ as Azerbaijan doubles down
Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan called Azberiaijan’s attempts to portray Armenian religious sites in Nagorno-Karabakh as not being Armenian ‘unacceptable and incomprehensible’. Meanwhile, Azerbaijani presidential aide Hikmet Hajiyev continued to make controversial comments about Armenian heritage in the region.
The battle over monuments in Nagorno-Karabakh has long been central to the conflict over the region, with Azerbaijan often labeling medieval monasteries or heritage as Caucasian Albanian, and denying their Armenian origin despite widespread recognition among international scholars. Caucasian Albania, not related to modern-day Albania in the Balkans, was an ancient Christian kingdom that existed in the South Caucasus.
The dispute escalated after a group of diplomats visited Nagorno-Karabakh earlier in September. The official tour, hosted by Azerbaijani presidential aide Hikmet Hajiyev, portrayed Armenian religious heritage as Caucasian Albanian and showed display copies of ancient Armenian manuscripts, implying their empty pages meant they were fake.
The tour was condemned in Armenia, with officials arguing the distortion of history was indicative of rhetoric that could undermine the peace process.
‘But I also consider it pointless to set the goal if we set ourselves the task of proving it, for example, to Azerbaijan, because that is a pointless and unfeasible task. We should record that this is an unfeasible task, but that does not change, has not changed, and will not change anything for us’, Pashinyan said on Wednesday.
He went on to argue that ‘established peace is a value for both Armenia and Azerbaijan’, and on both sides ‘it is necessary to treat peace with care’.
In regards to the claims about the origin of Gandzasar (Ganjasar), Pashinyan stated that Armenia responded to Azerbaijan’s claims ‘through the most competent official knowledgeable about this matter’ — the director of the Matenadaran, Ara Khzmalyan.
Critics have accused both Pashinyan and the rest of his administration for not delivering an adequate response to Azerbaijan’s claims, echoing recurring sentiments that Pashinyan is too willing to make concessions to Azerbaijan.
Amid the ongoing peace process, Armenia has taken a more cautious stance in its response towards Azerbaijan’s actions in Nagorno-Karabakh, which have included erasing Armenian religious and cultural heritage, ancient cemeteries, residential areas, and settlements, along with former government buildings.

items.title: Azerbaijan carries out parallel counterterrorism operations in 5 countries, detains 10
items.summary: Baku has accused the 10 of carrying out terrorist activities.
items.body_text:
Azerbaijan’s State Security Service (DTX) says it has detained 10 people — among them non-Azerbaijanis — in parallel counterterrorism operations carried out in five undisclosed countries over alleged terrorism-related activities, including preparations for attacks and terrorist financing.
The DTX said Azerbaijani and foreign nationals had been identified as allegedly involved in forming a secret organisation, preparing terrorist acts, and financing terrorism.
According to the DTX, the group had allegedly planned attacks on Azerbaijani public and religious figures and collected information about their movements and security arrangements.
The agency said the investigation established that Vugar Abdullayev, who had previously been convicted for crimes committed as a member of an extremist group known as the ‘Sumgayit Jamaat’, had established criminal ties with Azerbaijani citizens Jalal Hajiyev, Javid Aliyev, Nicat Ahmadov, Nazim Aliyev, Ilkin Hasan-zade, and others.
The DTX said the group had held secret meetings and telephone conversations, which were recorded and documented as part of the investigation.
According to the agency, members of the group had selected Azerbaijani citizens as potential targets, monitored their regular movements and security arrangements, and allegedly agreed to flee to conflict zones abroad after carrying out the planned attacks.
The investigation also alleged that Jalal Hajiyev organised the financing of individuals participating in armed conflicts abroad on the basis of religious radicalism, including members of internationally recognised terrorist organisations, through cryptocurrency systems.
Authorities said they had obtained evidence concerning the sources of funds collected through fake advertisements posted on social media under the guise of raising money for religious rituals, as well as the mechanisms used to transfer the funds.
The DTX said that, in cooperation with the security and intelligence agencies of other countries, a wider network of people allegedly involved in financing international terrorism had been uncovered.
Parallel counterterrorism operations were carried out in five countries, resulting in the detention of 10 members of the group, according to the agency.
One of those detained abroad, Elshan Asgarov, was extradited to Azerbaijan.
The suspects have been charged under articles of Azerbaijan’s criminal code relating to terrorist financing, establishing a criminal organisation and preparing to assassinate a state or public figure, among other offences. A court has ordered their detention as a pre-trial measure.
The investigation and operational measures in the case are ongoing, the DTX said.

Georgia’s Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze has announced the gradual closure of the grants agency, which was intended to fund state-approved NGOs after the introduction of the foreign agents law. This time, Kobakhidze attacked not only government-critical groups, but the entire concept of an NGO, calling it an ‘artificial phenomenon created for foreign intervention’.
‘The sole purpose of an NGO can be one state’s intervention in another. That is why NGOs were invented in the first place’, Kobakhidze told reporters on Thursday.
‘Therefore, it would be for us to invent NGOs [ourselves] and fund such activities’, he said, adding that the agency would be shut down by the end of the year.
Officially named the State Grants Management Agency, the body was established in April 2025 with the backing of parliament which was controlled by the ruling Georgian Dream party and a government decree signed by Kobakhidze.
The stated aim of the agency was funding groups that would be ‘in line with the priority areas of the country’s development’, as an alternative to ‘foreign actors’ who ‘arbitrarily determine the agenda of the activities of these organisations’.
The Georgian government had been awarding various types of grants, including for startups and educational projects, prior to the agency’s establishment.
The separate agency initiative came amid the government’s sweeping legislative restrictions on international funding for civil society and independent media.
On Thursday, Kobakhidze described NGOs without exception as a tool for foreign intervention.
‘When we established the agency, it became clear that this is the case’, he said, without explaining what he meant or what had happened during the agency’s brief operation to prompt the ruling Georgian Dream party to close an institution it recently created.
As of November 2025, the agency had awarded a total of ₾1.7 million ($653,000) in grants to 17 organisations, funding projects spanning social services, education, healthcare, disability inclusion, civic participation, environmental protection, research and technology. Some of the organisations had been established just months before receiving the grants.
Little is known about the agency’s recent activities, with its public presence having declined and its latest social media posts consisting of Christmas and New Year greetings. In January 2026, Tamar Zodelava, who had headed the agency, was appointed as a deputy justice minister. She was replaced by Tatia Naneishvili, her deputy at the agency.
Commenting on Kobakhidze’s latest announcement, former Georgian Young Lawyers’ Association (GYLA) chair Nona Kurdovanidze noted the agency’s establishment was ‘a performative step’ intended to soften the perception of the unprecedented scale of restrictions on foreign funding at the time.
‘Apparently, there is no longer any need for that either’, she added.
Since spring 2024, Georgian Dream has adopted a series of legislations restricting funding for civil society and media organisations, many of which had previously relied heavily on international grants.
The party first passed the highly controversial foreign agents laws, but after much of the civil sector refused to comply, it introduced further legislative changes that banned receiving foreign grants without the consent of the authorities.
Condemning Georgian Dream’s policies, the ruling party’s critics have repeatedly pointed out that several of its figures and allies previously worked with international civil society organisations.
Kobakhidze himself worked with the Open Society Foundation (founded by billionaire George Soros) in 2012–2013 and received remuneration for his work.

items.title: Government survives agricultural policy confidence vote by narrow margin
items.summary: The vote was called after the opposition Centre Party pointed out that the Finnish agricultural sector is the least profitable in the EU.
items.body_text:
Prime Minister Petteri Orpo's (NCP) government survived a confidence vote in parliament on Friday by 96 votes to 82.
Twenty MPs were absent from the vote, while opposition Social Democratic MP Timo Harakka abstained.
The vote followed an interpellation debate into the government's agricultural policies, held after the opposition Centre Party submitted an interpellation question to parliament earlier this month.
Centre Party leader Antti Kaikkonen noted at the time that the Finnish agricultural sector is the least profitable in the EU. The interpellation therefore demanded that the government provide the struggling sector with emergency funding of between 100 and 150 million euros — a move recently proposed by Sweden's outgoing government.
According to Kaikkonen, the Finnish agricultural sector has slid even further into difficulties during the current government's term in office.
The Centre Party, a historically agrarian party with firm roots in the Finnish countryside, suggested the money needed to support the sector could be obtained by the government cancelling its proposed corporate tax cut, which is set to come into effect next year.
Finland's rate of corporate tax, the duty levied on a company's profits, will be reduced from 20 percent to 18 percent from next year, according to the government's proposal. This will mean a loss of some 850 million euros for the state coffers.
Farmers protested outside of parliament in the spring over growing concerns about the future of Finnish agriculture, in particular Finland's food supplies and agricultural policies.

items.title: Citizens' initiative demanding restrictions on data centers reaches 50,000 signatures
items.summary: The petition calls for conditions on how data centres connect to Finland's electricity grid as well as for the introduction of a separate data centre fee.
items.body_text:
A citizens' initiative calling for tighter legislative control of data centres in Finland has reached the required 50,000 signatures within three days of starting, and it will now proceed to parliament to be debated by MPs.
The petition, entitled 'Datakeskukset kuriin' (roughly translated as 'Rein in the data centres') was launched on Tuesday in the wake of search engine giant Google's announcement last week that it will significantly expand its data centre operations in Finland over the coming years.
The signatories want the government to set conditions on how data centres connect to Finland's electricity grid and operate their business "taking into account the electricity grid's capacity, mandatory backup power, and the utilisation of waste heat".
In addition, the initiative calls for the introduction of a separate data centre fee, which should be calculated based on the "environmental harm caused by operations and the resources used (including electricity, water, land use)".
This would ensure that energy prices remain affordable for households and other industries, the initiative adds.
Finland has become a magnet for data centres in recent years, with companies such as Microsoft and TikTok owner ByteDance recently announcing planned investments.
Finland is an attractive destination for such investment because of the country's climate — which helps reduce the costs associated with the heat produced by data centres — as well as Finland's large supply of low-carbon electricity.

items.title: Oprah Winfrey packs out business event on first ever visit to Finland
items.summary: The daytime TV icon was the keynote speaker at the Nordic Business Forum in Helsinki on Thursday.
items.body_text:
Iconic US talk show host Oprah Winfrey made her first ever visit to Finland this week as she delivered a keynote address at the Nordic Business Forum (NBF) on Thursday.
Although the forum promotes itself as "Europe's largest business and leadership event", Winfrey dispensed with the business jargon throughout her 90-minute speech, focusing instead on a more humanistic message.
Winfrey shot to fame during the 1980s, when her ground-breaking daytime TV programme The Oprah Winfrey Show revolutionised the talk show format by focusing on self-improvement as well as other more human-centred topics.
That focus was clearly evident during her speech at NBF too.
She told her sold-out audience that her long career as a talk show host taught her that everyone — from presidents to pop superstars to everyday people — are looking for one thing in life: validation.
"At the end of every conversation, I kept hearing the same thing: did you see me? Did you hear me? Did what I say get through?"
She added that there is however an inherent danger in this "disease to please".
"When you do things with the intention to please other people, guess what: they feel pleased and keep coming back for more and your frustration, anger, and resentment don’t matter," she said.
Her message certainly seemed to resonate with her Finnish audience, with one participant interviewed by Yle calling it "inspirational".
Fee not disclosed
Oprah Winfrey follows in the footsteps of many other high-profile Americans who have taken to the NBF podium in recent years, including former President Barack Obama and former Vice President Al Gore, actors George Clooney and Will Smith, as well as Apple co-founder Steve Wozniak.
Securing Winfrey's services was still seen as a significant achievement — although organisers remained tight-lipped about the fee she was paid. Yle inquired about the amount from NBF, but no response was received.
According to various US talent agencies, Oprah's fees for private events hover around the 500,000 dollar (435,000 euro) mark, but large commercial events are believed to be significantly pricier.
NBF tried in 2018 to recruit Winfrey as a speaker, with Helsingin Sanomat reporting at the time that the star's representatives requested a fee of 1.2 million dollars.

items.title: 'I am available to form a new government': Swedish opposition leader meets speaker
items.summary: The leading candidate to be Sweden's new Prime Minister, Magdalena Andersson, has declared herself 'available' to form a new government after she held the first party leader meeting with the parliament's speaker after the election.
items.body_text:
At a press briefing following the meeting with the Speaker, Social Democratic leader Magdalena Andersson stated that she is ready to take responsibility for the election results and wishes to seek "broad cooperation."
"I am available to form a new government," she declared.
To all questions regarding how she intends to reconcile the "red lines" of the Centre Party and the Left Party, she replied:
"First, we must see who is given sonderingsuppdraget [the task of trying to form a new government]; after that, I will begin discussions and negotiations with other parties."
Andersson said she would contact six party leaders — implying that she was ready to talk to every party leader except Jimmie Åkesson, leader of the far-right Sweden Democrats.
She noted that this meant she also planned to speak to Ulf Kristersson, leader of the Moderate Party.
"Of course; if I receive sonderingsuppdraget, I will reach out to him," she said, adding that she expects a pleasant conversation.
Magdalena Andersson also said that she has already been in contact with several party leaders, without specifying which ones.
She did would not reveal whether she has already extended invitations for any meetings.
Left Party leader Nooshi Dadgostar made a brief statement on her way to meet the Speaker. She said she supports the Social Democratic leader as the next Prime Minister and defends the position that her party should be part of the government. The Left Party’s votes cannot be handed over to the Centre Party or the Social Democrats, she said.
"Our voters have rejected them. They do not want to be represented by Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist or Magdalena Andersson; instead, they need a voice of their own," she said.
Speaker Andreas Norlén is meeting with the party leaders today for initial talks. They have been summoned to the Speaker’s office in order of party size.
Magdalena Andersson was the first to meet him, at 10am, Simona Mohamsson of the Liberals will be the last, at 2pm.
A press conference with the Speaker is planned following the meetings, at approximately 3.30pm this afternoon.
The rounds of talks with the Speaker are intended to result in someone being tasked with attempting to form a government.
Christian Democrats leader Ebba Busch told the news agency TT that "trust-based conversations between the party leaders" will be necessary.
She declines to answer whether she has congratulated Magdalena Andersson yet: "I note that they do not yet have a basis for a government," she said.

items.title: OPINION: Yes, Swedish immigrants vote in their own interests – just like other voters
items.summary: Data shows that voters in Sweden with foreign backgrounds support left-wing parties in often much higher numbers than they do right-wing parties. The Local's Mandy Pipher says, 'So what?'
items.body_text:
Since the Sweden Democrats are an ethno-nationalist party with a track record of pointing to immigration as the source of all of the country’s ills, it didn’t come as a big surprise that, in the wake of their first-ever electoral decrease, top party members blamed immigrant voters.
Some blamed new citizens – those who had been granted citizenship over the past four Tidö years, against the wishes of the Sweden Democrats, who wanted a total freeze on new citizenships.
Others targeted a specific ethnic-religious minority group (guess which one!), saying that their votes had influenced, or swayed the election.
This includes Sweden Democrat party leader Jimmie Åkesson, who, in his post-election press conference this morning, said that the Social Democrats and the Left Party "mobilised Islamist voters."
Perhaps more surprising was that a Moderate MP (admittedly, one on the rightward end of the party) did something similar. In an article in the British magazine The Spectator, Fredrik Kärrholm referred the 97.6 percent vote share of the Social Democrats and Left Party in Malmö’s immigrant-heavy Rosengård neighbourhood as “Saddam Hussein numbers.”
Public broadcaster SVT and The Local’s Richard Orange did a fact check on some of these claims, finding that while the claim about who new citizens voted for was completely unfounded and, in fact, unverifiable, Swedish voters with “foreign” backgrounds did indeed heavily favour the Social Democrats and the Left Party – the two largest parties on the opposite side of the political spectrum from the Sweden Democrats.
To which I say, “So what?”
Kärrholm’s Spectator article is entitled “Did demographics decide the Swedish election?”, a headline which implies that particular demographic groups having a decisive influence on elections is somehow new or unusual.
Did demographics decide the Swedish election in 2022, when, as The Local found out, foreign-born voters with non-European backgrounds voted more to the right than in the 2026 election?
Maybe!
Did demographics change the face of Swedish politics over the last 12 years as rural working-class men threw their support in force behind the Sweden Democrats?
Yes!
That is democracy. Particular demographic groups regularly sway elections. Coming from Canada, where well-established immigrant communities from around the globe “decide” elections – i.e. participate in them as citizens, like everyone else, who is probably also an immigrant, a few generations back – and are wooed by various political parties accordingly, the “news” that immigrant Swedish voters were not particularly interested in voting for parties which either espoused or supported xenophobic and anti-immigration rhetoric wasn’t very newsworthy.
So, at risk of explaining the deeply obvious:
Yes, citizens with immigrant backgrounds get to vote, and yes, like everyone else, they are likely to vote for parties that promise to make their life better – or at least not make it worse.
Is it any surprise that voters of immigrant background would not want to vote for government coalition parties which have introduced strict new citizenship requirements with no transition period, overseen the threatened and actual deportation of their teenaged children, and increased the required salary for a work permit well beyond the reach of ordinary workers?
Is the next bit of voter demographic news going to be that moneyed families in wealthy Stockholm enclaves voted for the Moderates? That environmental activists voted for the Green Party? Or that ethno-nationalists voted for the Sweden Democrats?
The pearl-clutching in certain corners of Swedish politics on whether “immigrant voters” “influenced” this election is telling, but not about immigrants to Sweden, or their voting habits.
It reveals something worryingly anti-democratic. The message of this particular batch of pearl-clutching – a message which is more or less explicit, depending on who is delivering it – is that those voters they consider to be “fore
