items.title: Sweden Democrat leader sticks to demand for ministerial posts in future government
items.summary: Sweden Democrat leader Jimmie Åkesson has stuck fast to his party's insistence on ministerial posts in any new government and dismissed reports he plans to take a break in his first press conference since the far-right party's unexpected election setback.
items.body_text:
Asked whether there was any truth to reports in the Swedish media that the far-right party might be willing to drop its demand for its first ministerial posts if that allowed the right-wing parties to win over the Centre Party and so form a government, Åkesson insisted the party's stance was unchanged.
"I have no new position. We are not going to give up any of our demands," he said, arguing that it was up to the Centre Party – which is refusing to support a government that has Left Party ministers or Sweden Democrat influence – to shift its position.
"We have no red lines. We are not the problem; rather, it is other parties that have a bunch of red lines. And a prerequisite for anything to happen is that other parties give up their red lines."
He later argued that as the Sweden Democrats are one of the largest parties in the parliament it was "pretty unreasonable" to expect it to yield, rather than the smaller centrist parties, which he accused of causing "a great deal of parliamentary chaos in Sweden over a very long time".
'Nothing particularly dramatic'
The Sweden Democrats had an unexpectedly poor election result, dropping three percentage points on their result in 2022, but Åkesson played down his party's setback, claiming that he had been surprised throughout the last four years that his party's polling had remained stable even after winning real political power.
"I can say quite honestly that a potential drop in support after four years of taking responsibility and making compromises was part of the calculation when we entered this cooperation four years ago, so we had expected to take a hit from cooperating and compromising with the center-right parties," he said. "It's nothing particularly dramatic; I think all analysts foresaw that this could happen."
He attributed part of the party's drop in support to the so-called 'Churchill Effect', when a politician succeeds so well in their goals that voters no longer see a need to keep them in power and vote for the opposition (just as Britain's wartime leader Winston Churchill lost an election in July 1945 just two months after helping win the Second World War).
"They said we would collapse when we got power. We haven't. On the contrary, the Sweden Democrats remain a large party," he said.
No plans to resign
Åkesson also denied that he had any plans to take a temporary break from leading the party – something that the broadcaster TV4 reported on Thursday, citing anonymous sources within the party.
"And I'm not going to resign," he added quickly before public broadcaster SVT shifted away from his press conference to cover the arrival of Social Democrat leader Magdalena Andersson at the Swedish parliament to meet Speaker Andreas Norlén, adding later "I'm not going to take a 'pause' either."
He said it was impossible to know who these sources were, but suggested that they were "not particularly well-informed if they even exist".

items.title: The key advice I wish I’d known before my disastrous Oktoberfest
items.summary: Thinking about your first Oktoberfest? Readers say it's all about planning ahead, pacing yourself and looking after your friends. Unfortunately, The Local's Tom Pugh had to learn those lessons the hard way.
items.body_text:
When The Local recently asked readers to share their top tips for a successful Oktoberfest, the advice was strikingly consistent – reserve early, bring cash, avoid overdoing it and have a plan.
I wish I’d had this advice to hand on my disastrous first visit to Munich's famous beer festival.
That trip took place many years ago on a stag weekend. I wasn't the groom or the best man and had played no role in choosing Oktoberfest as the destination.
But as the only member of the group living in Germany, and one of the few who spoke any German, I somehow acquired responsibility for rescuing the situation when things went wrong.
And things went wrong almost immediately.
So here’s your advice – and a cautionary tale of what can happen when it’s disregarded.
Mistake number one: arriving without a reservation
Around two thirds of respondents to our survey described Oktoberfest as either "the best time of their life" or "brilliant fun".
While a minority said they’d had "had better times in life" or dismissed the event as "totally overhyped" the overall picture was clear. Most readers believe Oktoberfest is worth experiencing – but that this generally relies on having some kind of plan.
Reader K. Munson got to the heart of what this means in just two words: "Tent reservations."
Another respondent said that "not having a reservation for a table in a tent" is the most common mistake a first-time visitor can make.
When I first went to Oktoberfest, the decision was made for me and far too late – long after it was possible to secure a reservation. To make matters worse, we were visiting on the festival's middle weekend, traditionally one of the busiest periods of the entire event.
After spending hours trying unsuccessfully to get into a beer tent on the Saturday, our group of twelve eventually admitted defeat and retreated to Munich's Ratskeller beneath the Neues Rathaus on Marienplatz.
READ ALSO: Bag checks and safe spaces - How Munich aims to make Oktoberfest safer
It’s a wonderful place in its own right, with vaulted halls and excellent Bavarian food, but it’s not Oktoberfest. Simultaneously disappointed and overwhelmed by the sheer scale of what was happening around us, we wedged ourselves into a corner table and tried (and mostly failed) to attract the attention of the waiting staff (I wouldn’t have gone anywhere near us, either).
Eventually and sheepishly, we shuffled off to bed – determined to be up at dawn and first in the queue for the tents on the following morning.
Mistake number two: dressing as an English cricket team
Readers also had strong views on clothing.
One respondent warned visitors not to wear "cheap fake Tracht".
This is sensible advice. Bavarians generally appreciate traditional clothing, but they can spot a costume-shop imitation from a considerable distance.
Our solution was arguably worse. Rather than cheap lederhosen, we decided to dress as an amateur English cricket team. I think the organisers hoped this would mean we attracted attention wherever we went, but in a good way (hence cricket team rather than football team).
Instead, amid the sheer spectacle of Oktoberfest, we were either invisible to everyone but ourselves or seen as a mild irritant.
For first-timers, the lesson is simple. Rent authentic Tracht if you want the full experience, buy quality second-hand clothing if your budget stretches to it, or simply wear ordinary clothes. All of these options are preferable to fancy dress.
Mistake number three: treating Oktoberfest like a sprint
Many of us were new fathers enjoying our first weekend away from nappies, sleepless nights and irrevocable life decisions – and determined to make the most of it.
On Sunday morning, we were back at the Wiesn before 8am. We were shown to places in a tent at 9am and our first litres of strong German beer arrived just moments later.
One respondent to our survey advised visitors to "drink responsibly and take care of yourself and your friends".

items.title: 'Who the f*ck ever asked you?' Provocative Berlin election poster calls to extend voting rights
items.summary: A new poster campaign released ahead of the Berlin state election is aimed at those without a German passport. We spoke with Volt's Matt Bristow to discover what it's all about.
items.body_text:
It's been quite the intriguing Berlin election, at least when it comes to election posters.
And the ones that have arguably stood out the most have been from one of the smaller parties.
Volt, a progressive and pan-European party, has raised eyebrows with its 'unf*ck Berlin' poster campaign that aims to highlight that the capital can do things a lot better.
READ ALSO: What is Volt and how does it plan to 'unf*ck Berlin'?
Now, ahead of the election for Berlin's House of Representatives (also known as the state election) and local districts on Sunday, Volt has another provocative question: 'Who the f*ck ever asked you?'
The idea behind it is to draw attention to a question that is rarely asked: who actually gets to have a say in the future of this city? And who doesn't?
The poster states in English: "You work here, pay taxes, raise your kids, are part of the community. You make this city what it is. But your voice is never heard? It's time we change that."
Only people aged 16 and over with German citizenship can vote in the state election, while EU citizens can also cast ballots in the district council elections (the Bezirksverordnetenversammlungen or BVV).
Volt says this means that EU citizens "are completely excluded from one of the most important decisions for Berliners".
The party is therefore calling for full voting rights for people with EU citizenship.
READ ALSO: What political parties in Berlin say about immigration and citizenship
"Of course, the slogan immediately catches your eye," said Matt Bristow, Volt candidate in Neukölln, who came up with the idea for the campaign posters.
"But what I really find obscene is the enormous democratic deficit we have in Berlin: almost a quarter of a million EU citizens alone are not eligible to vote in elections to the House of Representatives."
For Bristow, the demand goes beyond the issue of voting rights. He referenced the recent election in the eastern German state of Saxony-Anhalt where the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD), classed by state intelligence as an extremist organisation, managed to secure nearly 40 percent of the vote.
"Saxony-Anhalt shows that we need to ‘dare more democracy’," he said. "People don’t just want to put a cross on a ballot paper every few years. They want to know that their voice actually makes a difference: in how money is spent in their neighbourhood and in decisions that affect their everyday lives.
"Too few people currently know how they can get involved in political issues in their own neighbourhoods. Even worse: the results of greater public participation processes, such as the international competition on the future of Tempelhofer Feld, are simply ignored by the Senate."
Bristow called on voters to choose Volt on election day so the party can give "power to the people".
READ ALSO: Six smaller parties running in Berlin's state elections
How has the campaign gone down in Berlin?
On the topic of edgy posters, Bristow said Volt's campaign has created a buzz.
"The unf*ck Berlin campaign is a bit like Marmite: people seem to love it or hate it," he told us. "But everyone has an opinion. In general, though, I've heard overwhelmingly more positive than negative reactions when I've been out canvassing.
"And even when people haven’t liked the sweary style, they have appreciated the substance of our manifesto."
The party says the message has sparked a conversation about the city.
Bristow says while preparing for the campaign, people stopped him in the street to ask what the message meant.
"I explained that there were lots of things in this city that simply don’t work and that we believe that not only can Berlin do better, but it deserves better too," he said. "As a message that instantly resonates with people."
But does the language go too far?

items.title: Today in Germany: A roundup of the latest news on Friday
items.summary: CDU promises fuel price relief ahead of key elections, Germany inaugurates biggest offshore wind farm to date, third death reported in Frankfurt Airport malaria outbreak and more news on Friday, September 18th.
items.body_text:
Friday's top story: CDU promises fuel price relief ahead of key elections
Germany’s governing CDU has for the first time outlined the scale of fuel price relief promised by Chancellor Friedrich Merz, with party Secretary General Franziska Hoppermann suggesting motorists could see prices fall by between 21 and 25 cents per litre from early October.
Speaking on ZDF’s Maybrit Illner, Hoppermann said discussions with Germany’s federal states would now focus on how to implement the measure. She firmly rejected calls from Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil of the SPD for a windfall tax on oil companies, arguing that such a levy would do nothing to bring down prices currently approaching €2.50 to €3 per litre.
Hoppermann also moved to quell speculation over Merz’s future, insisting the chancellor would remain in office despite ongoing political debate.
The comments come as the CDU faces a difficult electoral test. Polling ahead of elections in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania places the party on just six percent, raising the prospect of failing to cross the five per cent threshold for the first time in a federal state.
In Berlin, the CDU is polling at 20 percent, narrowly behind the opposition Left Party.
READ ALSO: Germany plans price relief for drivers amid rising fuel costs
Germany’s biggest offshore wind farm begins powering green energy push
Germany has officially inaugurated its largest offshore wind farm to date, marking a significant milestone in the country’s transition towards renewable energy and greater energy independence.
The He Dreiht wind farm, located in the North Sea around 85 kilometres north-west of Borkum, features 64 turbines with a combined capacity of 960 megawatts. According to operator EnBW, the facility will generate enough electricity to supply approximately 1.1 million households once fully operational.
Speaking at the launch ceremony in Hamburg, Environment Minister Carsten Schneider described the project as a boost for Germany’s economy and energy security.
He said that renewable energy is not only the most climate-friendly option but also the cheapest and safest form of electricity generation, reducing the country’s reliance on costly fossil fuel imports.
The €2.4 billion project was built without government subsidies, with EnBW securing long-term power purchase agreements for the electricity produced. The company said some turbines are already feeding power into the grid, while others will be connected in stages over the coming months.
READ ALSO: How do I register my balcony solar panel in Germany?
Frankfurt bomb attacks linked to organised crime as teen arrested
A series of explosions outside businesses in Frankfurt has intensified concerns over a growing wave of organised crime-related violence in Germany, with police arresting a 17-year-old Dutch suspect following the latest attacks.
Two explosive devices detonated in the early hours of Thursday outside a café in the Nordend district and a shisha bar on the Zeil shopping street.
The blasts caused extensive damage to both premises, shattered windows in nearby buildings and damaged parked vehicles, although no injuries were reported.
Investigators are examining links between the two attacks and three similar incidents in Frankfurt and neighbouring Offenbach in recent days. A separate 15-year-old suspect is already in custody in connection with an earlier explosion.
Prosecutors believe the attacks may be part of a “Violence as a Service” network, in which young people from the Netherlands are allegedly recruited to carry out bombings on behalf of criminal groups.
Hesse’s Interior Minister Roman Poseck described the incidents as evidence of a “new dimension” in organised crime, while authorities pledged close cooperation with Dutch investigators to identify those directing the attacks.

items.title: Central government spending hits Rp1,791.5 trillion by August
items.summary: The government recorded central government expenditure realization of Rp1,791.5 trillion (US$98 billion) as of August ...
items.body_text:
This realized figure represents a 29 percent increase compared to the same period in 2025, when spending stood at Rp1,388.8 trillion (US$76 billion).
Finance Minister Suahasil Nazara on Friday detailed the realization comprised of ministry/agency (K/L) expenditure of Rp912.4 trillion (US$49.9 billion) and non-K/L expenditure of Rp879.1 trillion (US$48.1 billion).
According to him, K/L expenditure realization reached 60.4 percent of the 2026 State Budget ceiling of Rp1,510.5 trillion (US$82.7 billion), a 33 percent increase compared to the realization in August 2025, which stood at Rp686 trillion (US$37.5 billion).
"Entering the final months of the year, I remind that K/L spending must remain efficient, yet priority must be given to expenditures that deliver maximum impact to the public," the minister said at the State Budget September 2026 edition press conference on Friday.
Meanwhile, non-K/L expenditure realization stood at Rp879.1 trillion (US$48 billion), or 53.6 percent of the Rp1,639.2 trillion (US$89.7 billion) ceiling. This figure represents a 25.1 percent increase from the Rp702.8 trillion (US$38.4 billion) recorded during the same period last year.
In further detail, personnel expenditure reached Rp259 trillion (US$14 billion) by the end of August 2026, or 72.3 percent of the ceiling, marking a 21.7 percent increase.
Personnel expenditure was primarily utilized for the recruitment of approximately 355,000 new civil servants (ASN) and the payment of allowances for non-civil servant educators.
Furthermore, expenditure on goods and services was recorded at Rp389 trillion (US$21.3 billion), representing 55.1 percent of the allocated budget, marking a 67.5 percent increase.
According to Nazara, this rise was primarily driven by the implementation of the Free Nutritious Meal (MBG) program with Rp131.3 trillion (US$7.1 billion), School Operational Assistance (BOS) funds for private schools of Rp10.1 trillion (US$553 million), biodiesel incentives with Rp21.4 trillion (US$1.1 billion), healthcare services provided by Technical Implementation Units/UPT with Rp11.3 trillion (US$619 million), and food stabilization measures with Rp3.3 trillion (US$180 million).
Meanwhile, capital expenditure reached Rp159.8 trillion (US$8.7 billion), or 56.3 percent of the allocation, growing by 14.3 percent; these funds were utilized to support connectivity and food security through infrastructure and irrigation network development.
Furthermore, key realizations included Rp43.1 trillion (US$2.3 billion) intended for the Ministry of Public Works, Rp44.6 trillion (US$2.4 billion) for the Ministry of Defense, Rp36.1 trillion (US$1.9 billion) for the National Police (Polri), and Rp10.4 trillion (US$569 million) for the Attorney General's Office.
Social assistance expenditure reached Rp104.5 trillion (US$5.7 billion), representing 64.3 percent of the allocation and marking a 3.4 percent increase.
This social assistance included the Family Hope Program (PKH) at Rp21 trillion (US$1.1 billion) for 10 million beneficiary families, the Basic Food Card program at Rp27.6 trillion (US$1.5 billion) for 17.6 million families, and the National Health Insurance Contribution Assistance (PBI JKN) at Rp30.9 trillion (US$1.6 billion) for 96.7 million participants.
Additionally, the government disbursed Rp10.7 trillion (US$586 million) for the Smart Indonesia Program (PIP) benefiting 15.6 million students and Rp9.7 trillion (US$531 million) for the Smart Indonesia Card (KIP) for Higher Education, benefiting 954,000 university students.
Followed by expenditure for social assistance, social rehabilitation, and disaster relief totaled Rp4.6 trillion (US$252 million).

Regional sides previously competed in the ASEAN Championship (formerly known as the AFF Cup and Tiger Cup) since 1996.
Indonesia and Hong Kong are set to co-host the 11-team tournament from Sept. 24 to Oct. 5.
All Division 1 matches will be held at Jakarta’s Gelora Bung Karno Stadium and Bandung’s Si Jalak Harupat Stadium.
Drawn in Division 1 (Group A), Indonesia will face Singapore, Malaysia, and Bangladesh sequentially in Jakarta. Meanwhile, Group B matches featuring Thailand, Vietnam, Pakistan, and the Philippines will take place in Bandung.
Hong Kong will host Division 2 matches, featuring Laos and Brunei Darussalam in Group A, alongside Cambodia, Myanmar, and Timor-Leste in Group B.

items.title: Indonesia welcomes Malaysia aid to combat Kalimantan fires
items.summary: Malaysia will deploy an aircraft, three helicopters, and 52 firefighting personnel to assist Indonesia in combating ...
items.body_text:
The assistance was finalized during a bilateral meeting with Malaysian Deputy Prime Minister Ahmad Zahid Hamidi at Prabowo's residence in Hambalang, West Java.
"Malaysia offered assistance to help us tackle forest fires in Kalimantan. I welcomed this offer with gratitude and pleasure," Prabowo said following the meeting.
The President noted that the Malaysian emergency response deployment would proceed in the near future to support local suppression teams on the ground and from the air.
"This was also done a few years ago, and I am currently formulating comprehensive preventive measures so that this issue does not keep recurring every few years," he added.
Prabowo emphasized that support from neighboring countries highlights that forest fires represent a shared environmental concern across the region.
In addition to Malaysia, Indonesia has received support from Japan alongside assistance offers from several other partner nations.
"This is an environmental issue that affects many parties; although the fires are in Indonesia, the impact is felt by our neighbors. So, they want to help us, and we gratefully accept that," the President remarked.
Beyond fire management, President Prabowo and Deputy Prime Minister Hamidi exchanged views on expanding bilateral cooperation across other sectors—including the halal industry—while emphasizing the importance of maintaining strong diplomatic ties between the neighboring nations.
"Indonesia and Malaysia are brothers; we must work together and maintain an excellent relationship," Prabowo emphasized.

items.body_text:
Gadget guide: What students must know before buying
MANILA, Philippines — Before spending their hard-earned savings on a new tool, student buyers need a reliable gadget guide to help them make informed and confident decisions on their next big purchase.
We’ve created a list of things that students should remember, know, and avoid before deciding on their next gadget purchase that will empower their studies in the coming years.
Where do I start planning?
From drafting research papers to delivering group presentations, a student’s daily routine requires a gadget that strikes the balance between performance, storage, build quality, and the right price. But with so many options on the market, knowing where to start your search can feel overwhelming.
The most common pitfall of student buyers is falling into extremes: They pay extra for high-end features that they seldom use, or they settle for cheaper and underpowered alternatives where they sacrifice the workflow needed to get the job done.
To avoid these mistakes, start by listing the specific software your courses or subjects do require. Identifying whether you primarily use productivity ecosystems or cloud suites like Google Workspace and Microsoft 365, or even heavy specialized software, is an essential first step in narrowing down your search for the next gadget purchase.
And here are some points to take care of when beginning to map out in searching for the next gadget:
- Identifying your Primary Use Case — Everyone has a different set of needs, and that’s okay. Remember that computer science and multimedia students require a different set of technical specifications and hardware compared to those in education, humanities, or business courses that typically produce essays and presentations. Thus, it is important to determine what your current technology needs are. You might also want to ask yourself: “How will my next gadget benefit my studies in the long term?”
- Mobility Check — Are you fine prioritizing raw power and screen space with desktops, or do you opt for portability in usage such as tablets, iPads, or laptops?
- Check your current ecosystem — With the current technology that you have, check how it will be compatible with syncing with the new device that you’re planning to buy. In this state, are your existing devices compatible well with the devices you aim for–-like pairing an iPad with a Mac or MacBook? Or pairing an Android tablet with a Windows laptop?
- Set a strict budget for the purchase — Allocate your financial resources wisely for your next device, and stick to what’s readily available to you. Don’t settle for less—and we recommend that if your needs require more powerful software for more powerful gear, then you would want to invest more financially.
RELATED STORY: New parental controls in iOS 27
The big four of gadget spending
When evaluating and canvassing for any gadget purchase, students usually look for these four major factors, ensuring they get the maximum value for their money before deciding on their next purchase:
- Performance
- For Laptops/Desktops: You need to focus on the processor (CPU) and memory (RAM). When using for general schoolwork, you might want to look for at least that is a mid-range processor (e.g., Intel Core i5, AMD Ryzen 5, or the Apple M-Series) that’s paired with at least 16GB of RAM for future-proofing. Enough RAM prevents your system from slowing down when you have multiple browser tabs open, a video call, and document editors open at once.
- For Phones: You may want to opt for a phone with a mid-range to flagship processor. Aim also for at least 8GB of RAM, as well as a 90Hz or 120Hz display refresh rate that gives users reading long documents and scrolling through lecture slides smoothly.
- Storage
- For Laptops/Desktops: Always go for the Solid State Drive (SSD) over a Hard Disk Drive (HDD). Aim to go for 512GB of internal storage when you can.

items.title: For Aznar Shipping, going public means growth – and dodging third-gen curse
items.summary: 'My main job is really to hand it over to the next gen,' the third-generation Aznar tells Rappler. 'Looking at the IPO process, the requirements, the standards that you are held to, it really coincided with my interest.'
items.body_text:
AT A GLANCE
- Kyle Alexander Aznar, the CEO of Aznar Shipping, is determined to break the generational curse that often affects family businesses by preparing to take the company public through an IPO.
- The IPO aims to raise up to P737 million for fleet expansion and is part of Aznar's strategy to ensure the company's success for future generations, emphasizing professional governance and mentorship.
As his family’s shipping legacy prepares to open itself up to the public, Kyle Alexander Aznar had an age-old curse on his mind.
“You know what they say, the third generation is the last generation,” the Aznar Shipping president and CEO told Rappler on Friday, September 18.
He was, of course, referring to the infamous adage that warns family fortunes rarely survives three generations. The first makes the money, second grows it, the third squanders what’s left. Gone, wasted, kaput.
The third-generation Aznar wasn’t about to let that happen. He was only 27 when he suddenly had to take over the family shipping business after his father died. Now 31 and at the helm, he sees one job as more important than simply making money.
“My main job is really to hand it over to the next gen,” Aznar told Rappler at the sidelines of his company’s H1 briefing. “We want our business to succeed — not just for my time. It’s really succeeding generations.”
His chosen way to keep the family ship afloat for another generation? Open it up to the public.
Aznar Shipping has filed for an initial public offering (IPO) that could see the Cebu-based company sell as many as one billion primary shares at an indicative price of up to P0.67 each, potentially raising P670 million in gross proceeds for the company. Another 100 million secondary shares could be sold through an overallotment option, bringing the total potential offer size to P737 million.
At this stage, everything still remains subject to book building and approval by the Securities and Exchange Commission and Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE). Aznar said the company is targeting a December listing, but stressed that he did not want to “jump the gun” on regulators.
A family business trying to grow up
Aznar is hardly the only old name sailing out of Cebu.
Cebu has long been one of the country’s biggest shipping hubs, producing generations of shipping families, from the Gothongs and Robles to the Cokaliongs and the Lims. The Aboitizes were once part of that club too, with Aboitiz Shipping eventually evolving into 2GO, now under the Sy family’s SM group. (READ: As Atlas Mining leaves by 2027, SMIC expects 2GO, renewables to fill gap)
But while many shipping businesses have remained private and closely held, Aznar sees public company governance as part of the antidote to the generational curse.
“Looking at the IPO process, the requirements, the standards that you are held to, it really coincided with my interest. That’s how I first started getting interested in it quite a few years ago,” he told Rappler.
The professionalization actually began before the IPO. Even before the company’s aspirations to go public, the shipping company already had independent directors sitting on its board. Aznar said he has been the only family member on the board for the past three years, surrounded instead by professionals whom he calls his mentors.
“I was just only 27 when I had to take over the company when my dad passed away,” he said. “I was humble enough to realize that I might not have all the answers, I might not always be right.”

items.title: FACT CHECK: No evidence Romualdez has stage 4 cancer
items.summary: The lawmaker is reportedly suffering from illnesses such as sleep apnea, hypertension, diabetes, and major depressive disorder — not cancer
items.body_text:
AT A GLANCE
- A claim that circulated on social media stating that former House speaker Martin Romualdez has stage 4 cancer is false.
- There is no credible evidence, such as court filings or public hospital records, to support the claim of Romualdez having cancer; his documented health issues are related to cardiovascular and neurologic conditions.
- Romualdez was arrested on September 7 for a plunder case and is currently in custody, having been transferred to Quezon City Jail after being assessed at the Philippine General Hospital.
Claim: Following his arrest, medical findings confirmed that former House speaker Martin Romualdez has stage 4 cancer.
Rating: FALSE
Why we fact-checked this: A YouTube channel named “News Update Files” uploaded a video on September 9 claiming that Romualdez has stage 4 cancer.
Text on its thumbnail reads, “Stage 4 cancer!? Romualdez paktay [sic] na!?” (Stage 4 cancer!? Romualdez is already dead!?). It shows Romualdez lying in a hospital bed with a detainee shirt draped over him.
The video’s title reads, “Kapapasok lang! Breaking news! Romualdez paktay na! Confirmed! Tamba merong stage 4 cancer pala!”
(Just in! Breaking news! Romualdez is already dead! Confirmed! Turns out Tamba has stage 4 cancer!)
As of writing, the video has drawn over 4,400 views, 230 likes, and 60 comments.
The facts: There is no court filing, public hospital record, or credible news report confirming that Romualdez has cancer, whether stage 4 or otherwise. The lawmaker’s medical conditions, as cited in reports, concern other health issues.
Romualdez was arrested on September 7 over a P7.44-billion plunder case linked to alleged flood control kickbacks. Authorities served the warrant while he was confined at Cardinal Santos Medical Center in San Juan City. Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla said that at the time of arrest, Romualdez was suffering from a cardiovascular event, unstable blood pressure, and an anxiety attack.
Because of his condition, authorities processed Romualdez at his hospital bedside rather than taking him to a police station. He was photographed lying down, with the detainee shirt draped over him and the booking sign positioned above him. (READ: How Martin Romualdez avoided jail by going to hospital)
His actual documented conditions are cardiovascular and neurologic in nature, not cancer. In his own manifestation asking the anti-graft court Sandiganbayan for continued hospital confinement, Romualdez cited coronary artery disease, diabetes, and primary hypothyroidism, among other ailments.
The court ordered his transfer to the Philippine General Hospital (PGH), where an independent assessment found that Romualdez has chronic coronary syndrome, hypothyroidism, sleep apnea, anxiety, and major depressive disorder.
PGH Medical Director Dr. Gerardo Legaspi, however, said that these conditions are under controlled medication and that the lawmaker is in stable condition.
Behind bars: The Sandiganbayan subsequently ordered Romualdez’s transfer to the Quezon City Jail Male Dormitory in Payatas on September 14 following the PGH doctors’ examination. Romualdez remains alive and in custody, with his official mugshots being released the following day.
Romualdez is accused of receiving kickbacks related to the flood control corruption scheme. The case also involves former Ako Bicol representative Elizaldy “Zaldy” Co and two private individuals. Co remains at large, while Romualdez has pleaded not guilty during his arraignment before the Sandiganbayan on September 16. – Cyril Bocar/Rappler.com
Efren Cyril Bocar is a journalist from Llorente, Eastern Samar who graduated with a degree in English Language Studies at the Visayas State University. Cyril is also a graduate of the Aries Rufo Journalism Fellowship of Rappler for 2024.
Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at

items.title: Ombudsman flags DICT, begins fact-finding for ‘ghost internet’ projects
items.summary: The 'ghost internet' projects deal with government contracts where hardware and related software are bought by the government, but the software installed may be either outdated or fake, leading to project overpricing
items.body_text:
MANILA, Philippines – The Office of the Ombudsman announced in a press briefing on Friday, September 18, that it was conducting a fact-finding mission on what it called “ghost internet” projects.
The “ghost internet” projects deal with government contracts where hardware and related software are bought by the government for billions of pesos, but the software installed within the devices purchased may be either outdated or fake, leading to project overpricing.
Assistant Ombudsman Mico Clavano said during the briefing, “Once the hardware — the machines, the routers — are delivered and passes inspection, everyone assumes the software that’s supposed to run on it is there as well. But nobody actually checks, and there comes the loophole.”
“A contractor can install cheaper, outdated, or even fake software while still charging the government full price for the real thing. Because nobody verifies the software after the hardware is approved, the overpricing goes undetected,” Clavano added.
It is only found out when systems break down or when somebody digs into the matter further. The investigation, Clavano said, will center around the DICT and will seek to answer four basic questions. 
- Were the contracted sites actually installed and are they working?
- Was the government billed for connectivity and services that were never delivered?
- Were the prices of hardware, software, and services reasonable or inflated?
- Who approved, certified, or released payments for projects that were not delivered?
Clavano also said the scope of the investigation will deal with entirety of contracts related to DICT initiatives, but did not specify particulars as the fact-finding process is ongoing.
The Ombudsman, in the same press briefing, confirmed that graft complaints are now pending against members of the Villar family due to allegations related to PrimeWater Infrastructure Corporation. – Rappler.com

items.title: Ombudsman probes Villars, PrimeWater execs over water district deals
items.summary: he Ombudsman is investigating members of the Villar family, PrimeWater executives and 32 local water district officials over joint venture agreements involving three water districts.
items.body_text:
Ombudsman probes Villars, PrimeWater execs over water district deals
MANILA, Philippines — The Office of the Ombudsman has opened a preliminary investigation into graft and administrative complaints against members of the Villar family, PrimeWater Infrastructure Corp. executives and 32 local water district officials over alleged water service anomalies.
At a press briefing Friday, September 18, Assistant Ombudsman Mico Clavano said the complaints involve allegedly "grossly disadvantageous" joint venture agreements between PrimeWater and several local water districts.
He also cited PrimeWater's total unpaid obligation of P65,650,708.07 for the use of materials and supplies belonging to the Quezon Metropolitan Water District, San Pedro Water District and Trece Martires City Water District.
Respondents include Sens. Mark and Camille Villar, their brother Manuel Paolo Villar and their parents, former lawmakers Manny and Cynthia Villar, whom the Ombudsman identified as beneficial owners of PrimeWater during the period under investigation.
The Ombudsman also included PrimeWater president Fe Reblancos and vice president Romeo Sabater in the complaints.
The complaints also involve the general managers of three local water districts: Enrico Pasumbal of Quezon Metropolitan Water District, Guillermo Pili of San Pedro Water District and Juliet Ocampo of Trece Martires City Water District.
Other respondents include:
- Five members of the joint venture selection committee of the Quezon Metropolitan Water District
- Five members of the Quezon Metropolitan Water District Board of Directors
- Six members of the joint venture selection committee of the San Pedro Water District
- Two members of the San Pedro Water District Board of Directors
- Five members of the joint venture selection committee of the Trece Martires City Water District
- Six members of the Trece Martires City Water District Board of Directors
The Ombudsman is looking into potential violations of Sections 3(e) and 3(g) of Republic Act No. 3019, or the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act.
"Ito 'yung nakukuha nating mga complaints galing sa ating mga kababayan na hindi malinis at may interupsyon sa tubig na nakukuha nila," Clavano said.
(These are the complaints we receive from the public about unclean water and interrupted water service.)
The Ombudsman said the case stemmed from a report it received from the Office of the Government Corporate Counsel, which showed that 75 local water districts entered into joint venture agreements with PrimeWater from 2015 to 2022.
"This is the initial list and there are still more water districts under investigation, and expectantly, more cases in the pipelines," Clavano said.
In a statement, the Villar family said they only learned about the Ombudsman’s complaints through media reports and are yet to receive copies.
“We respect the legal process and will respond to the complaints at the appropriate time and in the proper forum. We are confident that, once given the opportunity to examine the allegations and the evidence supporting them, we will be able to fully and properly defend our rights and address the matters raised against us,” they said.

items.body_text:
At least 3 dead from school shooting in South Cotabato
Content warning: School shooting
MANILA, Philippines (Updated 5:10 p.m.) — A shooting incident at Banga National High School in Banga, South Cotabato, on Friday, September 18, has resulted in at least three fatalities and six injuries.
This was confirmed by South Cotabato Governor Reynald Tamayo.
The Department of Education earlier confirmed the on-campus attack and said it was "deeply concerned" by the "reported shooting incident" at Banga National High School.
The department said it is currently coordinating with its Schools Division Office and Regional Office, local authorities, and law enforcement "to verify the circumstances and provide necessary assistance."
"Our immediate priority is the safety and well-being of our learners, teachers, and school personnel," DepEd said.
DepEd said it is ready to give psychological first aid and mental health and psychosocial support to those affected.
It urged the public to stay calm and stop sharing unverified information while authorities investigate.
In a separate statement, DepEd's Region XII office urged the public to immediately cease the distribution of videos of the "incident in Banga" to "respect the victims and their families." It said that sharing the material would cause trauma and violate the privacy of victims.
Meanwhile, the Philippine Red Cross said preliminary reports, which are subject to verification, indicated that six injured individuals were transported to Dantom Doctors Hospital and South Cotabato Provincial Hospital. It also reported one fatality and said the suspected shooter was reportedly among the injured and was a student.
The public school sits in Barangay Benitez, Banga, and offers both junior and senior high school.
This comes less than three months after two students opened fire at San Jose National High School in Tacloban City on June 22, killing at least three schoolmates and wounding about 20 others.
On August 18, a shooting broke out at the junior high school building of Ateneo de Zamboanga University. A student armed with two pistols shot dead a schoolmate.

items.title: 'Go die back home': Thai PM orders governors to speed up deportation of offending foreigners
items.summary: Thai Prime Minister and Interior Minister Anutin Charnvirakul has instructed provincial governors to use their legal authority to swiftly deport foreigners who exploit, threaten, or engage in unacceptable conduct toward Thai citizens.
items.body_text:
Speaking on Sept. 17 about the implementation of Interior Ministry policies, Anutin stated that foreigners are welcome to live and work in Thailand provided they earn a living legally and respect local society and culture.
However, he stressed that authorities must take immediate action against individuals involved in aggressive behavior, intimidation, illegal businesses, or other offenses, The Nation reported.
Anutin specifically addressed officials in Phuket and Surat Thani, urging governors across the country to resolve such cases decisively rather than handling them as isolated incidents.
He emphasized that foreigners must respect Thai customs, warning against the unauthorized establishment of places of worship, private cemeteries, or the use of commercial businesses for religious activities.
"If you come here, come and earn a living honestly. If you're going to die, go die back home. You don't need to come and die here," Anutin said, according to reports by The Nation and Khaosod.
His remarks followed recent cases of foreign nationals establishing religious sites without proper government approval.
He specifically criticized an incident involving a property registered as a restaurant but partially utilized as a religious venue, Khaosod reported.
Dismissing concerns regarding deportation costs, Anutin assured that the government would cover the expenses.
He advised provincial authorities to pay upfront and seek reimbursement later, ensuring that financial constraints do not delay deportations.
The prime minister argued that deporting offenders is preferable to keeping them in Thailand to serve prison sentences, which consumes public resources.
"If the behavior meets the criteria, take action immediately," he said, adding that officials should not hesitate over the cost of airfare, according to Khaosod.
Anutin also ordered governors to crack down on foreigners suspected of using Thai nominees to illegally own land, working without permits, or using the country as a base for criminal operations.

items.title: Vietnamese line up for Apple's first red Pro iPhone despite 11% price hike
items.summary: Thousands of Vietnamese queue to pick up their new iPhones Friday as Apple's authorized resellers in Vietnam began handing over the iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max simultaneously from 8 a.m.
items.body_text:
Young people in Hanoi try out the iPhone 18 at a store on Nguyen Trai Street. Video by Loc Chung
In Ho Chi Minh City, a line had formed outside the TopZone store on Ham Nghi Street by 6 a.m., with customers waiting to collect their phones.
TopZone, which began taking orders on Sept. 12, said it recorded more than 170,000 deposits for the new-generation iPhones within 15 hours, making it the Apple retailer with the largest order volume in Vietnam.
Vietnam is once again among the first wave of markets to sell the new iPhones, alongside more than 60 countries and territories worldwide.
The store opened at 8 a.m. sharp, and customers streamed in to collect their phones in turn.
In previous years, some retailers held midnight handover events, and customers typically lined up the evening before and stayed up all night to get their phones. This year, most retail chains scheduled pickups in the morning, with queues organized only about two to three hours in advance.
One of the first customers to collect a phone, Nguyen Viet Anh Tai, a 26-year-old office worker, chose the iPhone 18 Pro Max in Burgundy. "This year's red is really beautiful, and it's the reason I decided to upgrade from an iPhone 14 to the new device," Viet Anh said.
Le Nguyen Hoang Vu, a 32-year-old sales employee in Ho Chi Minh City, was excited to receive his new iPhone.
The iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max come in four colors this year: red, blue, silver and black. Most first-batch buyers chose red, which is also the first time the color has appeared in the Pro line.
At a TopZone store in Hanoi, the atmosphere was quieter, as there were no launch events like in previous years.
According to a representative of one retail chain, many resellers are handing over the iPhone 18 at shopping malls and stores nationwide this year instead of concentrating deliveries at a few locations. The approach spreads customers out, prevents crowding and shortens pickup times.
Nguyen Thi Hue, who manages the Viettel Store on Xa Dan Street, said the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max had drawn strong interest, especially in Burgundy and Glacier, which were also the most-ordered versions.
However, first-batch supply has fallen short of demand, so some customers will receive their phones in the second and third delivery rounds. The store expected to hand over phones to nearly 50 pre-order customers on the morning of Sept. 18.
Customers begin unboxing and setting up their new devices.
Customers upgrading from an older phone will need to sync their data, which can take hours depending on storage. What's different this year is that users will need to verify their SIM when switching to another device.
At a store on Dai Co Viet Street in Hanoi, Nguyen Quang Huy was the first customer to arrive to collect his phone.
He said he joined the line at 7 a.m. and chose a 512GB iPhone 18 Pro Max in blue. "I need the phone early, partly because of the nature of my work. I'm using an iPhone 17 Pro Max, and I get the sense the battery on the new generation is better. I also take quite a lot of photos, so I need the lens system and the ability to adjust focal length," Huy said.
A customer holds two new iPhone 18 Pro Max units, one red and one blue.
A CellphoneS representative said the chain had received about 50,000 orders for the iPhone 18, triple last year's figure, with red and blue the most popular versions. On the first day of sales, the chain expects to hand over around 10,000 units, while remaining demand will be met in subsequent shipments.
"The iPhone 18 Pro Max is still the most sought-after and most-ordered version, even though the design hasn't changed much," Huy said.
The CellphoneS representative said purchasing typically peaks in the first few days of sales before tapering off. This year, however, iPhone 18 orders have exceeded many retailers' expectations despite a slight price increase.

items.title: Queen Suthida highlights Thai craftsmanship with distinctive outfits during Vietnam visit
items.summary: Thai Queen Suthida highlighted traditional Thai culture and craftsmanship across five outfits worn during her recent state visit to Vietnam.
items.body_text:
King Maha Vajiralongkorn Phra Vajiraklaochaoyuhua and Queen Suthida visited Hanoi University on the afternoon of Sept. 16.
The event marked the final day of their state visit to Vietnam from Sept. 14, at the invitation of Party General Secretary and State President To Lam and his wife. Photo by Giang Huy
At the event, Queen Suthida wore a midi skirt and cropped jacket made of ikat silk featuring a lantern pattern. Ikat is a type of Thai fabric woven using a distinctive technique in which threads are tie-dyed before being woven into cloth. The outfit was accented with a row of black beads along the neckline, front hem, sleeves and skirt hem.
Completing the look, the queen carried an octagonal rattan handbag accented with light purple sapphires and other gemstones, paired with silver sapphire earrings and a large-faced wristwatch.
On the third day of the visit, Queen Suthida chose an olive-gray outfit as she accompanied King Maha Vajiralongkorn Phra Vajiraklaochaoyuhua to lay wreaths at the Bac Son War Martyrs Monument and the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum. Photo from her Instagram
The ensemble paired a tailored blazer with a mesh-patterned silk skirt, detailed with dense black beadwork along the sleeves.
Flower-shaped gemstone earrings accented the look, which was completed by a woven rattan handbag featuring intricately carved silver hardware. Photo by Giang Huy
At a state banquet hosted by Party General Secretary and State President To Lam and his wife on the evening of Sept. 15, Queen Suthida appeared in a royal yellow Thai Dusit gown detailed with gemstones and pearls, paired with a bow-shaped clutch.
The Thai Dusit represents one of eight formal royal dress styles created for Thai women in the 1960s through a collaboration between Queen Mother Sirikit and French couturier Pierre Balmain. The design combines traditional royal aesthetics with the silhouette of Western evening gowns from the 1960s. The ankle-length skirt is made of Yok silk, a type of Thai silk with raised patterns, or brocade woven with gold and silver threads.
The name "Dusit" comes from Dusit Maha Prasat Palace in the Grand Palace complex. In Buddhism, Dusit, or Tusita, is the fourth heavenly realm, associated with bliss, supreme happiness and purity. According to Matichon, the gown symbolizes nobility, auspiciousness and peace. Photo from her Instagram
During talks on the morning of Sept. 15, the queen wore a purple Thai dress made of silk embroidered with gold thread, paired with silver-colored high heels. Photo by Giang Huy
She carried a rectangular rattan bag decorated with the initials "ST" and a jeweled flower. The design is among Thailand's popular handicraft products. Photo from her Instagram
The Thai royal couple piloted their aircraft to Hanoi on the afternoon of Sept. 14, marking the official start of their state visit to Vietnam. To mark her arrival, the queen appeared in a gray A-line dress tailored from ikat silk woven with a delicate rice-grain texture.
The garment featured floral motifs across the lower outer skirt in tones of gray and navy, designed to transition into the pattern of the inner layer. Intricate hand-embroidery with light gray and black beads accented the floral details, creating structural depth throughout the fabric. Photo by Giang Huy
Queen Suthida completed her arrival ensemble with petal-shaped hairpins, sapphire earrings, and fine gemstone jewelry. She carried a rectangular Yaan Lipao rattan handbag featuring a tulip-shaped handle, highlighting traditional Thai basketry techniques. Photo by Giang Huy
The accessory was crafted by artisan Abdulroning Waji, a member of the Royal Handicraft Association in Narathiwat province who specializes in blending ancestral Yaan Lipao weaving methods with contemporary forms, according to Matichon.
Preserving royal artisanal knowledge transmitted across generations, the heritage craft serves as an international showcase of refined Thai handicraft culture.

items.title: Fitch upgrades Thailand outlook to ‘stable’
items.summary: Fitch Ratings has revised Thailand’s outlook to “stable” ​from “negative”, ‌citing increased confidence that government debt will broadly stabilise over the medium term and that political conditions will improve following the general elections ​held ⁠earlier this year.
items.body_text:
Fitch Ratings has revised Thailand’s outlook to “stable” from “negative”, citing increased confidence that government debt will broadly stabilise over the medium term and that political conditions will improve following the general elections held earlier this year.
The outlook revision reverses a downgrade warning issued last year, when concerns over rising debt and weak growth weighed on the country’s credit profile.
The Thai economy has remained resilient despite higher energy costs and softer tourism demand following tensions in the Middle East, with technology and data-centre investment helping support growth.
The rating action also follows a smooth political transition after the February general election, with Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul’s coalition securing a working majority and easing concerns over policy uncertainty.
In a statement on Friday, Fitch said Thailand’s strong external finances and its ability to fund most government debt domestically continue to underpin the investment-grade rating, despite elevated debt levels and modest long-term growth prospects.
Fitch said the government debt-to-GDP ratio stood at 59.3% in the 2025 fiscal year and is projected to remain below 63% by fiscal 2028, well below the statutory maximum of 70%. This represents an improvement over a previous forecast of 65%.
The agency projects that the current account balance will return to a surplus of 1.5% of GDP in 2027, following a temporary deficit of 0.5% of GDP in 2026, driven by high oil prices and capital goods imports for data centre construction.
The move by Fitch follows a similar action by Moody’s in April, when it revised Thailand’s outlook to stable, citing reduced downside risks from US tariffs.
The ratings agency also affirmed country’s BBB+ sovereign credit rating.
Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Ekniti Nitithanprapas said the move by Fitch “demonstrates growing confidence in the government’s policy direction”.
“The government will accelerate the concrete implementation of policies aimed at promoting investment in new industries, expediting the transition to green energy … and prioritising the maintenance of fiscal discipline to enhance potential and lay the foundation for the country’s sustainable growth,” he said.

items.title: Australian suspect in Pattaya teen's murder denied bail
items.summary: The Australian suspect in the killing of a Thai girl was denied bail on Friday after denying the allegation and other charges at the Pattaya Provincial Court.
items.body_text:
The Australian suspect in the killing of a Thai girl was denied bail on Friday after denying the allegation and other charges at the Pattaya Provincial Court.
Simon Peter Carman pleaded not guilty to four charges, maintaining that what he did was in self-defence, according to ABC of Australia.
Mr Carman, 46, was before the court for his hearing after prosecutors on Thursday indicted him for intentionally murdering Thanchanok Donhomlah, 17, from Kalasin.
Along with murder, he was accused of three other charges: hiding and destroying the corpse, taking a minor away from their parents or guardian for indecent activity, and engaging in indecent behaviour with a minor.
Thanchanok's murdered corpse was placed in a suitcase and dropped by a railway track in Pattaya on June 26, one day after she was reportedly seen with Mr Carman. She had been reported missing the day earlier.
The Australian was later arrested at Suvarnabhumi airport attempting to return to his home country. Australian media said his destination was Perth in the country's west.
His statement to the court on Friday reiterated the position he made with police after the arrest in June. He told authorities at the time that he acted in self-defence with no intention to kill.
Mr Carman applied for bail and prosecutors moved to opposte the request, ABC said. The prosecution argued that he had been arrested while preparing to flee the country.
After deliberating on the request, the court denied the bail motion and has scheduled Oct 12 for an examination of evidence.

items.title: Salvage mission begins as navy battles to raise capsized Java Sea ferry
items.summary: BANJARMASIN (Indonesia), Sept 18 — Indonesian authorities were preparing on Friday to right a capsized passenger f...
items.body_text:
BANJARMASIN (Indonesia), Sept 18 — Indonesian authorities were preparing on Friday to right a capsized passenger ferry that went down in the Java Sea last week, a navy official said, with dozens of people still missing.
The Virgo Transport 8 carried 213 passengers and 30 crew when it lost contact with its shipping company after departing from Indonesia’s second city of Surabaya on Java island on Sunday, headed for Banjarmasin on Borneo island.
At least six people have died and 129 are missing, according to the national search and rescue agency, Basarnas. Some of the victims are feared trapped inside the vessel, which is now submerged.
An expert team has been brought in to assist the operation to right the ferry, local navy commander Galih Nurna Putra told reporters on Friday.
“The salvage operation is underway,” Galih said, adding that “there was an observation yesterday”.
The head of the Banjarmasin search and rescue agency, I Putu Sudayana, said teams would be able to resume the recovery of bodies once the vessel is righted.
Before that process is completed, divers face risks if they try to enter the capsized ship, he said.
“We understand the psychological condition of the victims’ families, but please also understand the situation faced by the joint search and rescue team, because they must also pay attention to (operational) safety.”
The capsized vessel has drifted from its original position and sunk farther into the sea, from an initial depth of 21 metres (69 feet) to 29 metres, Basarnas operation director Yudhi Bramantyo said on Thursday.
Marine accidents are a regular occurrence in Indonesia, an archipelago of more than 17,000 islands that relies heavily on boat connections for daily transport and tourism.
Lax safety standards and unpredictable weather are the main reasons for the disasters.
On Thursday, rescuers formally called off a search for eight people, including five journalists sent to cover a volcanic eruption, nearly two weeks after their speedboat went missing in waters between Java and Sumatra islands. — AFP

items.title: Philippine Coast Guard seizes 12.5 tonnes ammonium nitrate, dynamite aboard Palawan ferry
items.summary: MANILA, Sept 18 — The Philippine Coast Guard said on Friday it confiscated 12.5 tonnes of ammonium nitrate and 130...
items.body_text:
MANILA, Sept 18 — The Philippine Coast Guard said on Friday it confiscated 12.5 tonnes of ammonium nitrate and 130 cases of dynamite aboard a vessel sitting at port in Palawan province.
The explosive substances were found on Sunday alongside materials used in detonations inside two trucks on a ferry that carried both cargo and passengers, the coast guard said in a statement.
Ammonium nitrate, a chemical used in fertilisers, is safe if stored properly, but there can be catastrophic consequences when mishandled or mixed with explosives.
A stash of 2,750 tonnes of ammonium nitrate left to degrade in a Beirut warehouse killed more than 220 people and laid waste to swathes of the Lebanese capital when it exploded in 2020.
“The explosives and components were discovered inside (two trucks) aboard the RoRo (roll-on, roll-off) passenger vessel,” the coast guard said in a Friday statement, adding the cargo had been “improperly declared”.
“The confiscated explosives and components are currently under the custody of the Philippine National Police,” they said.
“The (coast guard) will work closely with the PNP to determine the role of the accompanying personnel in the shipment of said cargo.”
It was unclear if any arrests had been made as of Friday afternoon, and the name of the involved company has not been disclosed.
A coast guard officer tasked with port safety had been “relieved from his post to ensure impartial investigation”, the statement said.
The discovery comes in the wake of a series of deadly ferry accidents.
On September 9, a fire ripped after an explosion in the cargo hold of the M/V June Aster near the resort area of Coron, Palawan, burning dozens of passengers to death.
In January, a triple-decker ferry carrying more than 340 people sank off the southern Philippines, killing at least 52 people. — AFP

items.title: Witness says attack was ‘like a scene off Jaws’ as shark kills swimmer in Western Australia
items.summary: SYDNEY, Sept 18 — A shark killed a man as he swam off a popular beach near Perth in Western Australia today, polic...
items.body_text:
SYDNEY, Sept 18 — A shark killed a man as he swam off a popular beach near Perth in Western Australia today, police said.
It was the fourth death from a shark attack in Australia this year.
“It was reported a male swimmer had been bitten by a shark while swimming along the coast,” a Western Australia state police spokeswoman said in a statement.
“The swimmer died as a result of the attack.”
Police helicopters and boats scoured waters off Sorrento Beach after emergency services were called to the beach in the morning, officials said.
Authorities closed beaches in the area until further notice.
Local media reported that witnesses had seen blood in the water.
“It was like a scene off Jaws where a body is flicked around like a rag doll,” an unidentified male witness on the beach told local broadcaster Seven.
Surf Life Saving WA said in a social media post that an unidentified species of shark was involved in the incident about 50 metres offshore.
It was the second shark attack in Western Australia this week, after a man lost part of his leg when he was bitten at Glenfield Beach, north of Perth.
There have been multiple shark attack fatalities around the country this year.
A 12-year-old boy died after he was bitten by a shark while swimming in Sydney Harbour in January.
Three divers were fatally mauled in separate incidents between May and June — two in Western Australia and the third in Queensland.
Also in June, a woman had to have part of her left arm amputated after she was mauled by a shark at one of Australia’s most popular beaches, Coogee, in Sydney.
There have been around 1,300 shark incidents around Australia since 1791, of which more than 260 resulted in death, according to a database of their encounters with humans. — AFP

items.title: Van Bommel delight as son is named in Netherlands squad
items.body_text:
Van Bommel delight as son is named in Netherlands squad
Sept 18 : New Belgium coach Mark van Bommel was told his son Ruben had earned a first Netherlands call-up while holding a press conference on Friday to announce his own maiden squad.
On a busy day for the Van Bommel household, PSV Eindhoven winger Ruben van Bommel was included in new Netherlands coach Xavi Hernandez’s first squad for Nations League matches later this month.
The Dutch announcement was issued at noon, just as the elder Van Bommel began unveiling his Belgium squad in Tubize. After explaining his selections, he was asked by reporters about his son's call-up.
"Is the squad already known?" Van Bommel replied.
"Do you think I already knew?" he added with a laugh.
"I’m very proud of him, just as every father would be very proud of his son when he is called up for the Dutch national team. I played for the national team myself. That is the highest level you can achieve."
Van Bommel said the call-up was particularly significant after his son's recovery from a cruciate ligament injury.
"It has been a difficult year for him," he said.
"To come back in that way is a great achievement by him."
The 22-year-old has made a strong start to the season at Dutch champions PSV Eindhoven and becomes the third generation of his family to be involved with the Dutch team.
His grandfather Bert van Marwijk, 74, coached the Netherlands to the 2010 World Cup final and his father Mark, 49, won 79 caps and captained the national team. Mark also played in the 2010 final, which the Netherlands lost to Spain in Johannesburg.
Van Bommel's first game in charge of Belgium is away against Italy in Rome on September 25, a day after the Dutch play their first game of the new Nations League campaign against Germany in Amsterdam.
(Writing by Mark Gleeson in Cape Town; Editing by Toby Davis)

items.title: Van Dijk stays on but Depay omitted from Xavi’s first Netherlands squad
items.body_text:
Van Dijk stays on but Depay omitted from Xavi’s first Netherlands squad
Sept 18 : Netherlands' record scorer Memphis Depay was left out, but captain Virgil van Dijk continues his international career as new coach Xavi Hernandez named his first squad on Friday for the upcoming Nations League matches.
• Depay played only as a substitute at the World Cup earlier this year and remained on a national-record 55 goals. His omission was widely expected and could signal the end of the 32-year-old striker’s international career after 112 appearances.
• Van Dijk said last month that he would consider his international future after speaking to the new coach but has decided to continue. The Netherlands face Germany, Greece and Serbia twice in four Nations League matches during the extended three-week international window.
• Xavi handed a first call-up to Ruben van Bommel and Gjivai Zechiel and brought back midfielder Joey Veerman but must do without talisman Frenkie de Jong, who is still suffering from a knee injury sustained at the World Cup.
• Marten de Roon and Wout Weghorst are also not included in the 26-man squad, along with Guus Til and injured Brighton & Hove Albion midfielder Mats Wieffer.
• Jeremie Frimpong, Kenneth Taylor and Jurrien Timber, who missed the World Cup, return to the squad.
Squad:
Goalkeepers: Mark Flekken (Bayer Leverkusen), Robin Roefs (Sunderland), Bart Verbruggen (Brighton & Hove Albion)
Defenders: Nathan Ake (Fenerbahçe), Denzel Dumfries (Real Madrid), Jeremie Frimpong (Liverpool), Lutsharel Geertruida (PSV Eindhoven), Jorrel Hato (Chelsea), Jurrien Timber (Arsenal), Micky van de Ven (Tottenham Hotspur), Virgil van Dijk (Liverpool), Jan Paul van Hecke (Tottenham Hotspur)
Midfielders: Ryan Gravenberch (Liverpool), Teun Koopmeiners (Juventus), Tijjani Reijnders (Al-Qadsiah), Kenneth Taylor (Lazio), Quinten Timber (Crystal Palace), Joey Veerman (Borussia Dortmund), Gjivai Zechiel (Feyenoord).
Forwards: Justin Kluivert (Bournemouth), Ruben van Bommel (PSV Eindhoven), Brian Brobbey (Sunderland), Cody Gakpo (Liverpool), Noa Lang (Napoli), Donyell Malen (AS Roma), Crysencio Summerville (Al Hilal).
(Writing by Mark Gleeson in Cape Town; Editing by Toby Davis)

items.title: WHO flags growing health workforce gap as workers and patients age
items.body_text:
WHO flags growing health workforce gap as workers and patients age
GENEVA: The World Health Organization warned on Friday (Sep 18) of a gap in the medical workforce around the world in the 2030s, with a quarter of doctors set to retire in the next decade.
"In many countries, both our populations and health workers are ageing at the same time. This can intensify the projected global shortage of 11.1 million health workers by 2030," the WHO said in a statement accompanying a major report on workforce trends based on data from over 100 countries.
By 2030, 67 countries are projected to lack sufficient staffing to maintain the standards of medical treatment they currently enjoy, it said.
To maintain the current density of medical staff to the population, an additional 832,000 health workers are needed, and this could increase reliance on foreign health care workers in poorer countries, the report said, potentially impacting healthcare standards there.
Higher income countries, including many in Europe, are set to be the hardest hit since they have a higher share of older healthcare workers, the report said. In these countries, one in three doctors will retire in the next ten years, it said.

items.title: Barefoot and terrified, Yemenis flee the Houthi advance
items.summary: AL-BIREEN CAMP, Yemen, Sept 18 - When a terrifying bombardment erupted around their camp in Yemen this week as a long-paused civil war reignited, Rawya Hassan and her family fled for their lives, barefoot and leaving their animals and other belongings behind.
items.body_text:
Barefoot and terrified, Yemenis flee the Houthi advance
AL-BIREEN CAMP, Yemen, Sept 18 - When a terrifying bombardment erupted around their camp in Yemen this week as a long-paused civil war reignited, Rawya Hassan and her family fled for their lives, barefoot and leaving their animals and other belongings behind.
The family had already been forced from their village by war years earlier and now had to escape the fighting again, joining 115,000 people who aid agencies say are on the move after a rapid advance by the Houthi group.
"We are under terror, under the rockets, under the missiles," she said, making bread in a makeshift clay oven among the shacks and acacia trees of the small al-Bireen camp, where the family has now sought shelter.
The conflict between the Iran-backed Houthis and forces aligned with the Saudi-backed government mostly stopped after a 2022 truce, but fighting has broken out again in a spillover from the wider war between Iran and the United States.
As the Houthis seized the port city of Mocha and the southern stretch of Yemen's Red Sea coast last week, a wave of displaced people fled into areas held by the government and across the sea to Djibouti.
Among them were Hassan, 48, and her family of seven children, in a remote district of Taiz province, an area of steep, dry foothills between the coast and Yemen's central highlands.
The family were originally from the village of al-Tuweir, but fled fighting in the area eight years ago for a camp in al-Kadha district nearby. Now even that place of shelter has gone and they must start afresh.
"We escaped barefoot. We didn't even know where our children were. We had nothing with us, no covers, no mattresses, no food, no drink, nothing,” she said, describing shells falling and warplanes or drones circling overhead.
Her older sister, Rawda, was with the children and after a long walk they reunited the next day at al-Bireen camp where they are entirely dependent on aid.
Rawda, an orange scarf wrapped round her head, said the family does not now know where to go. From the camp, a dirt path leads up into the hills, and a road runs nearby between the Houthi-held coastline and another frontline at the city of Taiz.
SUDDEN RETURN TO WAR HAS PUSHED MANY TO FLEE
Larger numbers of people fled along the Indian Ocean coastline from the Bab el-Mandeb Strait at the mouth of the Red Sea towards Aden, arriving at camps pitched before the city in windswept sand with white tents standing in rows.
Um Mohammed said her family had escaped from Mocha when the Houthis advanced last week. It was the latest blow the family had suffered after her son was killed earlier in the war. When they reached al-Firdaws camp the family were given only thin mattresses and old blankets for the tent where they now shelter, she said.
Small children played nearby and women hauled large buckets of water from tanks brought by pick-up truck as aid workers distributed food rations.
"They put us in the middle of the sand. We have suffered a lot," she said, boiling water in a kettle over a small twig fire, adding that they had lost their livestock, clothes and blankets as they left.
The fighting in Yemen has exploded back into full-blown war along several fronts, with the Houthis using drones and ballistic missiles and Saudi Arabia pounding districts held by the Iran-backed group with warplanes. There is no sign the violence will let up soon.
The UN migration agency IOM said on Friday that at least 112,000 people had been displaced inside Yemen over the last two weeks and that nearly 3,000 more had fled to Djibouti, crossing the Gulf of Aden in overcrowded boats. REUTERS

items.title: Egyptian deported by US to Equatorial Guinea held incommunicado for a week, lawyer says
items.summary: Sept 18 - An Egyptian man deported from the US to Equatorial Guinea who criticized the conduct of security forces there has been held for a week at a gendarmerie station, one of his lawyers said.
items.body_text:
Egyptian deported by US to Equatorial Guinea held incommunicado for a week, lawyer says
Sept 18 - An Egyptian man deported from the US to Equatorial Guinea who criticized the conduct of security forces there has been held for a week at a gendarmerie station, one of his lawyers said.
Ahmed Soliman was arrested on Friday last week and has not been able to see his attorneys, the lawyer, who spoke on condition of anonymity, told Reuters.
The spokesman for the central African nation's government and its embassy in Washington did not respond to requests for comment.
VIDEO SHOWS ALTERCATION IN HOTEL
Earlier this month, Soliman said police officers pulled guns on him and other migrants during an altercation at a hotel in Malabo, the former capital, where he and other migrants deported by the US have been held.
Video of the incident and news of Soliman's subsequent arrest spurred fresh criticism from rights groups of the so-called third-country deportation deals that the Trump administration has struck with several African countries.
The deals enable Washington to deport migrants who cannot legally be sent to their home countries because they obtained protection from US immigration judges.
Washington has defended the third-country deals as lawful and said deportations are carried out in accordance with US immigration law.
Soliman was in custody at La Luna gendarmerie station in Malabo, his lawyer said.
The facility has been used in the past to hold human rights activists, according to rights groups including Amnesty International.
DETAINEES ACCUSED OF BREAKING MIRROR, AMNESTY SAYS
Soliman had been accused of breaking a mirror in an elevator in the hotel, though that was a pretext for his arrest, the lawyer said.
"We are certain that it was a retaliation for Ahmed speaking out and the videos leaked," said the lawyer, referring to footage of security forces pulling guns on deportees.
Amnesty International said in a statement on Friday that Soliman was being held with another deportee, Samson Birhane, and that they were both accused of breaking the mirror.
"Police officers covered the two men’s heads with a bag and beat them in their heads, backs and ribs," Amnesty said, describing how they were allegedly taken into custody.
"The authorities must immediately release them, inform them of any charges against them and allow them unimpeded access to counsel."
Equatorial Guinea's government spokesman and its US embassy have not released any statements on Soliman's case.
In a statement on Wednesday, US Representative Adelita Grijalva, a Democrat from Arizona, where Soliman has spent much of his life, criticized the third-country deportations.
"Our country is responsible for sending people out this way, period," she told Reuters.
"And so we should make sure that where they're going is somewhere safe. Just because a country accepts somebody does not mean that that's a good placement." REUTERS

items.title: Malawi police rescue kidnapped British woman after exchange of gunfire

items.body_text:
Malawi police rescue kidnapped British woman after exchange of gunfire
BLANTYRE, Sept 18 - Malawi police said they had rescued a British woman who was kidnapped last week, in an intelligence-led operation in which the kidnappers were shot and later died.
• Police said 47-year-old British national Nusrat Osman was abducted by four unidentified men in the city of Blantyre's Mount Pleasant suburb on September 11.
• She was rescued on Thursday and reunited with her family, the Malawi Police Service said in a statement dated September 17.
• The motive of the kidnapping is not clear.
• The operation to rescue Osman involved an exchange of fire between police and the kidnappers, who were armed with an AK-47 rifle and a pistol.
• The kidnappers were shot during the operation and later died in hospital from their injuries.
• The senior police officer who was wounded is in hospital in a stable condition.
• Investigations into the kidnapping are continuing. REUTERS
