items.title: CGA plans a historic 2027 visit to Philippines
items.body_text:
- 
            CGA plans a historic 2027 visit to PhilippinesGEOPOLITICAL SIGNIFICANCE: The CGA’s nonmilitary role makes it a tool to avert diplomatic issues, an official said, while confirming the donation of a ship to Manila
  - By Lo Tien-pin and Jake Chung / Staff reporter, with staff writer and CNA
 Coast Guard Administration (CGA) ships are scheduled to sail to the Philippines bearing the words “Taiwan Coast Guard” in a high-profile visit in October next year, the first such visit by a Taiwanese maritime law enforcement vessel to the Southeast Asian nation, the agency said yesterday. The CGA also confirmed that it had donated one of its decommissioned patrol vessels to the Philippines in a rare transfer of a retired ship to a nondiplomatic ally. The Republic of China (ROC) Navy last made such a visit in 1974, shortly before the Philippines switched diplomatic recognition to the People’s Republic of China in 1975. The Lienchiang Coast Guard Administration vessel sails in an undated photograph.Photo courtesy of the Coast Guard Administration Official naval visits between Taiwan and the Philippines have effectively halted for half a century, a senior government official said on condition of anonymity. Unlike the navy’s goodwill missions, which involve an annual deployment of three ships intended to project force and conduct more sensitive operations, the CGA’s nonmilitary functions make it a more effective tool for overcoming Taiwan’s diplomatic difficulties, the official said. In September last year, the CGA’s 4,000-tonne Chiayi-class vessel Taipei (台北) visited Palau on a goodwill mission. The CGA’s planned visit to the Philippines next year would carry considerable geopolitical significance, the official said. Taiwan and the Philippines are both targets of China’s “gray zone” tactics, prompting the two sides to strengthen cooperation in maritime law enforcement and regional security, the official said. The efforts include the attendance of a senior Philippine Coast Guard official at Central Police University’s graduation ceremony last year and Taiwan’s donation of a retrofitted 500-tonne disaster relief and rescue vessel to the Philippines on Wednesday. According to media reports citing information from VesselFinder, a Philippine law enforcement vessel named Bling No. 1 sailed from the Port of Kaohsiung for sea trials before returning. Although stripped of its armaments and CGA markings, the vessel resembled the Lienchiang (連江), which was decommissioned on Oct. 27, 2023, or the Kinmen (金門). The CGA said in a statement that the transfer was “handled according to usual practice.” The Ministry of Foreign Affairs declined to comment on whether it was the first time Taiwan had donated a vessel to the Philippines. Su Tzu-yu (蘇紫雲), a research fellow at the Institute for National Defense and Security Research, said the donation was part of an international trend to counter China’s “expansionist behavior” at sea. Japan is to transfer decommissioned Abukuma-class destroyer escorts to the Philippines, while the US has transferred many patrol boats to the country, Su said. “China’s gray zone threats have prompted collaboration between the ‘white fleets,’” Su said. “This shows that Beijing’s actions have backfired.” Next year’s eight-day goodwill mission is to reportedly involve celestial navigation training using sextants, maritime operations and law enforcement instruction for 100 CGA personnel and students in Central Police University’s Department of Maritime Police. The trip is to facilitate exchanges with the Philippines on non-traditional security issues, including maritime humanitarian assistance and combating crime at sea. The approach would not only help reduce political sensitivities among neighboring countries, but also demonstrate Taiwan’s flexibility and adaptability as a maritime nation, the official said.

items.title: Central bank keeps key rates unchanged
items.body_text:
- 
            Central bank keeps key rates unchangedFED UP: The governor of Taiwan’s central bank said that there is still time to observe, while stock markets around the world mostly rose after the US Fed hiked interest rates
  - By Crystal Hsu / Staff reporter
 The central bank yesterday kept its key interest rates unchanged for a 10th straight quarter while easing housing credit controls, signaling confidence that property lending has cooled enough to allow a targeted relaxation without undermining financial stability. The central bank left its discount rate at 2 percent, the collateralized lending rate at 2.375 and the short-term lending rate at 4.25 percent. However, it increased the maximum loan-to-value ratio for people buying a second home to 70 percent from 60 percent and ended a restriction on loans for land purchases. Central bank Governor Yang Chin-long speaks at a news conference at the bank in Taipei yesterday.Photo: CNA Central bank Governor Yang Chin-long (楊金龍) said that monetary policy has remained relatively tight since 2024, helping stabilize domestic prices and anchor inflation expectations. “We still have time to observe,” Yang said, adding that two central bank board members dissented, while the majority backed maintaining the current policy stance. Some members nevertheless warned that inflation still requires close monitoring, he said. The cautious approach reflects uncertainty over the global economic outlook and the potential effect of conflict in the Middle East on Taiwan’s prices and economy, Yang said. Domestic inflation is manageable this year and is expected to fall below 2 percent next year, while economic growth is expected to remain solid, he said. The central bank lifted its forecast for full-year economic growth to 11.48 percent and said it expects the pace to slow to 5.82 percent next year. It also raised its growth forecasts for this year’s consumer price index (CPI) and core CPI to 2.03 percent and 2.16 percent respectively, putting both above its 2 percent inflation watch level. The easing in housing comes as property lending has continued to moderate. Real-estate loans accounted for 34.44 percent of total bank lending at the end of July, down from 35.56 percent in March and 37.61 percent in June 2024. Credit flows into property have dropped, while first-home buyers account for a growing share of residential mortgage borrowers, Yang said. Lending for urban renewal and reconstruction of aging or unsafe buildings has also taken up a larger share of construction loans, he said. Housing transactions have cooled, with speculative activity declining and expectations of further home-price gains moderating, Yang said. The central bank also removed a requirement introduced in December 2021 that land loans be accompanied by a commitment to begin construction within a specified period. Yang cited labor shortages and difficulties disposing of excavated soil as factors that can delay projects. Commercial banks have gained more experience managing property-related credit risks after several years of tighter controls, giving the central bank room for a targeted relaxation of land-financing restrictions, Yang said. The bank also expects growth in broad money supply to exceed its 2.5-to-6.5 percent reference range this year and raised the upper end to 6.75 percent, citing robust artificial intelligence-related exports and investment, buoyant stock-market activity and a low comparison base. Global stock markets mostly rose yesterday after the US Federal Reserve delivered a widely expected interest rate hike, while falling oil prices and easing bond yields also helped calm inflation fears. items.title: Takaichi retains key ministers in reshuffle
items.body_text:
- 
            Takaichi retains key ministers in reshuffle
  - AFP, TOKYO
 Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi yesterday retained her key ministers in a Cabinet reshuffle and made two appointments of Taiwan-friendly politicians. Takaichi — who has high approval ratings nearly a year into office — kept core members of her team, according to a Cabinet list announced by government spokesman Minoru Kihara. They include Kihara, Minister of Finance Satsuki Katayama, Minister of Foreign Affairs Toshimitsu Motegi and Minister of Defense Shinjiro Koizumi. Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi speaks at a news conference at her office in Tokyo yesterday.Photo: AP The prime minister also made new appointments, with Hisayuki Fujii named minister for internal affairs and communications, and Takashi Yamashita returning as minister of justice. Fujii and Yamashita have represented the ruling Liberal Democratic Party in the “two-plus-two” policy dialogues with Taiwan. At the talks between the Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) and the LDP, the two have engaged in face-to-face discussions on issues such as Taiwan Strait security. Fujii participated in the dialogue in 2024, while Yamashita engaged in the seventh, expanded edition of the dialogue on Monday with DPP representatives, including Legislator Puma Shen (沈伯洋), the party’s candidate for Taipei mayor. During the meeting, the LDP’s Taiwan policy project team identified enhancing deterrence, civil defense, “gray zone” contingencies and economic cooperation as areas for further discussion. While Fujii has engaged in Taiwan-Japan exchanges through the lens of diplomatic and security policies, Yamashita has been more involved in the internal deliberation of Taiwan policy within the LDP. The small-scale reshuffle comes as Takaichi navigates rising inflation and a weak yen while pursuing a consumption tax cut on food starting next year. While Takaichi’s tax cut pledge is popular among voters, economists have criticized the plan, warning that she has failed to identify about ￥5 trillion (US$32 billion) needed annually to fund it. Takaichi’s policy of expansive government spending has also rattled markets, pushing Japan’s benchmark bond yield to about 3 percent, its highest in three decades. With Katayama in the finance role, Japan has repeatedly intervened in the foreign exchange market to prop up the falling yen. On defense, Koizumi remains tasked with updating Japan’s foundational national defense strategy. “Revising our strategy is something that has a major impact on Japan’s security and on the entire region,” Koizumi told reporters after he was reappointed. The defense ministry “must marshal all our resources and move forward with a greater speed” with the review with “a strong sense of urgency,” he added. Additional reporting by Lin Tsuei-yi

items.title: US lawmakers hold hearing on plight of jailed media tycoon Jimmy Lai, as Hong Kong slams ‘hypocrisy’
items.summary: Hong Kong authorities have condemned US lawmakers for holding a hearing on jailed pro-democracy media tycoon Jimmy Lai and colluding with “anti-China and destabilising elements” to demand his release ahead of a planned summit between Chinese leader Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump. The government said in a statement on Thursday that it “firmly […]
items.body_text:
Hong Kong authorities have condemned US lawmakers for holding a hearing on jailed pro-democracy media tycoon Jimmy Lai and colluding with “anti-China and destabilising elements” to demand his release ahead of a planned summit between Chinese leader Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump.
The government said in a statement on Thursday that it “firmly rejected” members of the Congressional-Executive Commission on China (CECC), a US government agency that monitors human rights in China.
After a hearing with Lai’s son Sebastien on Wednesday, CECC leaders introduced a bill aimed at securing the release of Lai and other “democracy advocates, journalists, former legislators, and civil society leaders” imprisoned in Hong Kong. Claire Lai was also scheduled to testify alongside her brother but pulled out due to a recent cancer diagnosis.
“Jimmy Lai was sentenced to an appalling 20-year prison sentence simply for exercising his God-given rights and standing up for the people of Hong Kong,” CECC chair Senator Dan Sullivan said. “He should be released immediately.”
Co-chair Representative Chris Smith called Lai’s sentence “unjust, politically motivated [and] an affront to free speech and human dignity.”
‘Nothing to do with freedom of the press’
Lai was sentenced in February to 20 years in jail, following his conviction on foreign collusion and sedition charges under the Beijing-imposed national security law. The 78-year-old was accused of using his newspaper, Apple Daily, to lobby foreign nations to impose sanctions, blockades, or other hostile activities upon China and Hong Kong. He was also accused of inciting hatred against the authorities with op-eds published in the now-shuttered tabloid.
“The [Jimmy] Lai Chee-ying case has nothing to do with freedom of the press at all,” the Hong Kong government statement read, adding that “defendants have used journalism as a guise to wantonly create social conflicts, incite social antagonism, incite hatred and glorify violence, bringing harm to our country and Hong Kong.”
“These countries and their politicians, including the so-called CECC, display their hypocrisy and double standards by pointing fingers at the HKSAR for our work in safeguarding national security,” it said.
In a separate statement, Hong Kong’s Legislative Council also condemned what a spokesperson called “maliciously provocative political maneuvering and alarmist talk by some politicians.”
‘Humanitarian grounds’
Lai’s son and daughter, Sebastien and Claire Lai, have lobbied Western governments to press for their father’s release, alleging that he is being held in solitary confinement without air conditioning and his health is deteriorating.
The CECC and the United Nations have called for Lai’s release on humanitarian grounds, citing his age, health, and the impact of the years he has already spent in detention.
The Hong Kong government statement also hit back at these claims, stating that “medical services received by Lai Chee-ying in custody are undoubtedly adequate and comprehensive,” and the Correctional Services Department “has been providing adequate medical attention.”
Xi Jinping is due to meet US President Donald Trump at the White House on Thursday next week, four months after Trump’s state visit to Beijing in May.
Trump said he mentioned Lai’s case during their summit in May, but Xi signalled that Lai’s release was “unlikely.”
Freeing Lai is a “tough one for him to do,” the US president said.

items.title: Advocates call for stronger consent laws as Hong Kong to criminalise persistent child sexual abuse and ‘cyberflashing’
items.summary: A campaign group has continued to urge the government to impose limits on a defence allowing a sexual assault suspect to claim they mistakenly believed they had been given consent, after authorities announced stronger protections under upcoming sexual offences reforms. The group, which calls itself We Are X, after the placeholder name assigned to sexual […]
items.body_text:
A campaign group has continued to urge the government to impose limits on a defence allowing a sexual assault suspect to claim they mistakenly believed they had been given consent, after authorities announced stronger protections under upcoming sexual offences reforms.
The group, which calls itself We Are X, after the placeholder name assigned to sexual assault survivors in court, said that it welcomed the Security Bureau’s move to propose the criminalisation of persistent child sexual abuse and sending digital pictures of one’s genitals without consent, known as “cyberflashing.”
Hong Kong authorities are seeking to introduce dozens of new offences to Hong Kong’s archaic sex laws, including provisions to protect mentally impaired people, expand the scope of rape, and redefine consent during sexual activity.
We Are X’s Friday statement read: “We would like to remind the public that the purpose of creating this offence is to provide children who endure persistent sexual abuse with an avenue to seek legal recourse and receive comprehensive protection.”
The campaign group called on the government to make meaningful changes regarding what they called the stringent and unreasonable burden of proof placed on survivors.
Loopholes
The group had previously expressed concerns that defendants could still be acquitted by arguing that they had an “honest but mistaken belief” that consent was provided.
It “remains concerned” that the government has maintained it is up to the courts to decide whether a defendant’s “mistaken belief” is reasonable, the statement said.
That approach fails to address situations where a defendant relies on the “mistaken belief” defence even in cases where “vitiating factors” — such as force, fear, unconsciousness, or deception — are involved, the group said.
“We earnestly hope the Government will… ensure the law accurately reflects the reality of sexual violence and establishes an objective and effective legal framework for assessing ‘sexual consent’ within the judicial system,” the statement read.
The Association Concerning Sexual Violence Against Women (ACSVAW) had a similar response, saying in a statement that the current approach contains “severe legal loopholes,” adding that defendants have been acquitted after claiming they believed consent was given based on “absurd or unreasonable grounds.”
The association said that the defendant must be barred from raising the “mistaken belief” defence if they failed to take steps to ascertain the victim’s consent.
A limit must also be imposed if the defendant was reckless as to whether there was consent, and if the defendant was in a state of self-induced intoxication.
We Are X also called on the government to step up publicity and education efforts addressing misconceptions about false accusations or a lowered conviction threshold. The government itself has said that prosecution and conviction thresholds will remain unchanged.
It also continued to suggest that the government change the word “rape” in its sex crime laws to “sexual assault by penetration.” The clearer terminology would help the public understand that the offence covers all types of non-consensual penetrative sexual assault, regardless of gender, it said.

items.title: Australian judge William Gummow dies aged 83 after decade on Hong Kong’s top court
items.summary: Non-Permanent Judge of the Hong Kong Court of Final Appeal (CFA) William Gummow has died aged 83. The Australian judge had served on the city’s apex court since 2013. Born in 1942, Gummow practised for ten years as a solicitor before being called to the New South Wales Bar in 1976. In 1986, he was […]
items.body_text:
Non-Permanent Judge of the Hong Kong Court of Final Appeal (CFA) William Gummow has died aged 83. The Australian judge had served on the city’s apex court since 2013.
Born in 1942, Gummow practised for ten years as a solicitor before being called to the New South Wales Bar in 1976. In 1986, he was appointed to the Federal Court of Australia.
Gummow served on the High Court of Australia from 1995 to 2012, and earned the honour of Companion of the Order of Australia in 1997.
He last sat on Hong Kong’s top court in May.
See also: Explainer: Why do foreign judges sit on Hong Kong’s top court?
Last year, he had committed to continuing in the role until July 2028.
Since its establishment in 1997, the CFA has periodically invited judges from other common law jurisdictions to serve on its panel.
The practice has long been seen as a vote of confidence from the international community in Hong Kong’s judicial system, bolstering the city’s reputation as a global financial and business hub.
However, in recent years, the presence of overseas judges has come under scrutiny amid a wave of resignations following the introduction of the national security law in June 2020. The UK has also considered pulling its judges from Hong Kong’s top court.
Condolences
The Judiciary said in a Thursday statement that he had “authored important judgments that have greatly enriched our jurisprudence,” as it expressed sympathies to his family.
In a Thursday statement, the Hong Kong Bar Association (HKBA) also expressed its condolences: “The HKBA and the wider community in Hong Kong strongly support and appreciate the contribution made by Overseas NPJs to the administration of justice in Hong Kong which includes all areas of the law including commercial law, human rights and criminal law.”
The High Court of Australia said it would hold a ceremonial sitting to honour him: “Justice Gummow was a deeply learned, rigorously analytical and highly collegiate member of the High Court who contributed greatly in that capacity and throughout his professional life to the content and trajectory of Australian law.”
Spate of resignations
Last April, Australian judge Robert French resigned from Hong Kong’s top court, saying the role of overseas non-permanent judges on the CFA had become “increasingly anachronistic and arguably cosmetic.”
He was the sixth foreign judge to depart Hong Kong’s highest court since the start of 2024.
Anthony Murray Gleeson from Australia did not renew his term when it ended in February 2024, citing old age; UK judges Jonathan Sumption and Lawrence Collins quit in June 2024 before their terms ended; while Canada’s Beverley McLachlin and the UK’s Nicholas Phillips did not extend their terms.
Sumption wrote an opinion piece for the Financial Times just days after his resignation, saying Hong Kong was “slowly becoming a totalitarian state.” Judges operate in an “almost impossible political environment created by China,” he said.
Before the most recent string of departures, two British judges, Robert Reed and Patrick Hodge, quit the CFA in 2022, citing the erosion of political freedoms.
Last June, a judge from New Zealand, William Young, joined the CFA.
Hong Kong’s justice chief has downplayed the departure of foreign judges in recent years, saying it is not about their numbers but whether the judges have “a good international reputation.”

items.body_text:
第7屆唐獎表彰6位國際學者 永續獎得主：守護環境如「登月」艱困盼達成
第七屆唐獎頒獎典禮，永續發展獎得獎人蘇珊、索羅門（左）領獎。（記者田裕華攝）
第七屆唐獎今頒獎，學術巨擘齊聚台北。此屆永續發展獎得主是揭開臭氧層破洞原因、成功推動全球環境治理的美國大氣化學家蘇珊．索羅門，在如今臭氧洞正逐步復原之時，她指出，今日的環境挑戰或許同樣看似難以解決，但科學、公共參與、產業合作與明智政策曾讓人類克服臭氧層耗損危機，期盼人類能再次完成這項如登月般艱鉅的「守護環境」任務。
唐獎每2年舉辦1次，今年包括蘇珊．索羅門、生技醫藥獎得主米歇爾．薩德蘭、卡爾．瓊、漢學獎得主葛兆光及法治獎得主布魯斯．艾克曼等5位得主都親自出席領獎，生技醫藥獎得主史蒂文．羅森伯格則透過線上參與。
艾克曼回憶，父母家族為逃離歐洲反猶迫害來到美國，自己成長於1950年代紐約的貧困社區。儘管父母曾勸他不要抱持進入哈佛的夢想，但他在學校鼓勵下決定挑戰原本看似遙不可及的目標，進而走出貧困社區、展開具有意義的學術人生，未來他將持續探索威脅法治未來的全球性危機及其深層根源。
以免疫細胞療法開創血癌與實質固態瘤革命性料療法獲獎的卡爾．瓊表示，患者及其家人才是此獎的核心，在充滿不確定的時候，他們選擇相信研究團隊，「我們欠他們的，不是任何一個獎項所能償還」。而一項治療若無法真正到達需要它的人手中，就無法改變生命；讓患者能夠獲得治療，也必須成為衡量成功的一部分。
唐獎評選委員會總召集人、中研院士翁啟惠表示，4個獎項評選委員會始終秉持客觀、公正與專業標準遴選得主；得主的卓越成就，持續對人類健康、環境永續、學術研究及社會正義產生深遠影響。
第七屆唐獎頒獎典禮，包括蘇珊．索羅門、生技醫藥獎得主米歇爾．薩德蘭、卡爾．瓊、漢學獎得主葛兆光及法治獎得主布魯斯．艾克曼等5位得主都親自出席領獎。（記者田裕華攝）

民進黨台北市長參選人沈伯洋今晚（18日）到景美集應廟與支持者見面掃街，有網友6點半左右抵達就發現景美夜市人潮洶湧，擠得水洩不通，反用藍營抹黑的「蟑螂老鼠」戲稱，「景美夜市～現在滿街的蟑螂老鼠！一起送我們的市長進台北市政府」。更實況轉播現場的大家都很歡樂，根本韓國巨星等級。
國民黨部分政客和側翼對「洋流」不以為然，質疑「造神」、「請工讀生」，甚至侮辱這些支持者都是「蟑螂老鼠」，引發爭議。然而每次活動都是滿滿的人潮，無疑次次打臉所謂的「請工讀生」、「蟑螂老鼠」。
網友看到摩肩擦踵的「洋流」笑說，「景美夜市已經多久沒有這種盛況了」、「這麼多工讀生，便當要怎麼發？（反串註明）」、「一堆老人。 真是不敢相信！」、「台北市政府要求攤商要行政中立耶！你們這些蟑蟑鼠鼠請千萬不要為難攤商哥姐們呦」、「這裡還是景美夜市唯一的大空地，外面是馬路，夜市裡面很窄，沒想到滿成這樣」、「我這輩子沒看過景美夜市有這麼多人過……」、「我的天啊！景美人不服輸喔」。

items.body_text:
◎ 廖明輝
五月川普訪問北京時，美中宣布一個頗有雄心的新名詞：「建設性戰略穩定」。習近平甚至說，這將為未來三年乃至更長時間的美中關係提供指引。四個月後，川習準備再度於華盛頓碰面，問題卻來了。從稀土供應仍受干擾，AI競爭愈打愈烈，美國擴大對伊朗制裁，台灣軍售依然敏感。美中如果連這些核心矛盾都在升高，所謂「戰略穩定」到底穩定了什麼？
5月川習會，美中宣布一個新名詞：「建設性戰略穩定」。4個月後，川習準備再度於華盛頓碰面。（路透檔案照）
有趣的是這個詞並沒有消失。北京九月仍公開重申「建設性戰略穩定」；美國在台協會谷立言處長日前也說即將舉行的美中峰會是在公平互惠基礎上推進「戰略穩定」、避免誤判的機會。問題不在美中還提不提，而在兩國說的是不是同一件事。北京五月給的定義是以合作為主、競爭有度、分歧可控、和平可期；但華府關心的卻是稀土不能斷、農產品能賣、AI風險不能失控，同時不能放棄科技與軍事優勢。相同的四個字，美中在背後其實是各自解讀成兩套不同的盤算。
美國在台協會處長谷立言表示，即將舉行的美中峰會是在公平互惠基礎上推進「戰略穩定」。（資料照）
九月的川習二會正好成為檢驗所謂「戰略穩定」壓力測試。中國近期採購約一百萬噸美國黃豆，像是先替峰會鋪紅毯；另一方面，部分中國稀土供應商卻停止對美出貨。美中又準備討論AI安全，但幾乎同一時間，華府指控中國AI企業「工業規模」蒸餾美國模型。這才是今日美中關係真貌，一手成交、一手防堵；一邊談安全護欄，一邊搶技術制高點。所謂穩定並不是結束競爭，而是雙方都還不想讓競爭提前失控。
地處美中之間的台灣，必須看懂「穩定」可能具有的兩面性。五月川習會，習近平已明講台灣是中美關係最重要問題，處理不好可能走向碰撞甚至衝突；美國卻同時強調維持印太有利的力量平衡並協助台灣提升自我防衛。這兩條路線並不容易同時滿足。北京若把「戰略穩定」理解成美國降低對台軍售、約束台灣，甚至修改對台政策語言；華府若為了稀土、貿易或中東合作而接受這種邏輯，那麼穩定的就不是台海，而是北京施壓台灣的空間。
因此，川習二會是否再次高舉「建設性戰略穩定」並不是最重要的。真正的試金石就是能不能約束強者片面改變現狀，而不是要求台灣承擔大國和解成本。台灣當然樂見美中避免誤判，但不能把大國關係氣氛緩和誤認為台海安全改善。軍售是否照常推進、美國對台政策文字有沒有後退、中國軍事壓力是否下降，才是判斷的尺度。
川習二會真正的試金石，是能不能約束強者片面改變現狀，而不是要求台灣承擔大國和解成本，例如軍售是否照常推進、中國軍事壓力是否下降等。圖為中國海警船。（路透檔案照）
我們可以說五月的「戰略穩定」只是宣言，九月才開始驗收。若它只是讓美中在黃豆、稀土與晶片之間找到交易空間，卻讓北京取得更多介入台灣安全的槓桿，就不是建設性穩定，只是把美中的衝突時間點往後遞延。若從台灣視角來看川習二會，真正可靠的穩定從來就不是川普與習近平握手，而是要讓任何一方都知道，片面改變台海現狀就必須要付出不可承受的代價。
（作者為中華經濟研究院輔佐研究員）

About the Author
Stephen Mercado
Stephen Mercado is a retired officer of the CIA’s Open Source Enterprise (originally the Foreign Broadcast Information Service). A researcher primarily interested in Japanese intelligence history and Asian open-source intelligence, he earned a master’s degree in international affairs at Columbia University’s School of International and Public Affairs. He is the author of "Japanese Spy Gear and Special Weapons: How Noborito's Scientists and Technicians Served in the Second World War and the Cold War" (Pen & Sword Military, 2025), "The Shadow Warriors of Nakano: A History of the Imperial Japanese Army’s Elite Intelligence School" (Brassey’s, 2002), a dozen articles and several dozen book reviews.

items.title: North Korean county officials fail to sway parents of bullied disabled student
items.summary: County education officials in Musan county in North Korea’s North Hamgyong province visited the home of a disabled student’s family this month, joining teachers who had already made repeated visits, in an effort to persuade the parents to send their child back to school. The parents are refusing, citing years of bullying that began in […]
items.body_text:
County education officials in Musan county in North Korea’s North Hamgyong province visited the home of a disabled student’s family this month, joining teachers who had already made repeated visits, in an effort to persuade the parents to send their child back to school. The parents are refusing, citing years of bullying that began in elementary school.
A source in North Hamgyong province told Daily NK on Friday that teachers at a middle school in Musan county’s town center had visited the student’s home multiple times after the child stopped attending classes, but the visits produced no results. On Sept. 2, officials from the county party’s education department joined the effort, visiting the family directly to press the parents to reconsider.
The student was born with a congenital spinal disability, the source said. In North Korea, people with spinal disabilities are sometimes described with a derogatory term meaning “hunchback,” and classmates reportedly used this kind of language to mock the student throughout elementary school, subjecting the child to persistent bullying and social exclusion.
Aware of this reality, the parents had originally planned to keep their child in school only long enough to learn basic reading and writing, the source said. While overt teasing eased somewhat as the child moved up in grade level, the student had few classmates willing to spend time together or grow close, according to the source.
Tutoring instead of the classroom
“The parents don’t want their child to go through that kind of school experience again,” the source said. “Both the school and the county party are trying to persuade them to send the child back, but since neither side can offer a concrete plan to protect a disabled student from bullying, the parents aren’t backing down.”
The source added that people with disabilities in North Korea are frequently assigned to jobs at convenience facilities or in light manual labor, such as watch or shoe repair. “The parents figure their child will end up in simple repair work after graduating anyway, so they’re asking why the child should have to endure bullying at school in the meantime,” the source said.
Instead, the parents have hired a private tutor to teach the child computer skills at home, the source said. The family can afford the tutoring fees, and they believe that strong computer skills could open the door to better job prospects for their child despite the physical disability.
When county party education officials visited the family, they argued that attending school alongside peers is necessary for a child to grow into a productive member of society and urged the parents to reconsider. The parents pushed back firmly, telling officials, “We’ll take care of our child’s future ourselves, so please stop putting more pressure on a child who already has physical difficulties,” according to the source.
The standoff has placed the school in a difficult position. Because the student falls under North Korea’s compulsory education requirements, prolonged absence leaves the school responsible for managing the case.
“The school is trying every way it can to get the student back into the classroom to avoid responsibility for a long-term absence, while the parents are holding firm, saying they won’t let their child be hurt again,” the source said. “Even with county party education officials getting involved, the parents are showing no sign of budging, and the issue remains unresolved.”

items.title: South Korea’s unification education is asking the wrong question about peace
items.summary: South Korea’s Ministry of Unification will hold its first Peace Wind Week starting Sept. 11, 2026, an 11-day series of public events, including a DMZ peace walk and academic forums, organized under the slogan “The peace I want, toward a peace wind for the Korean Peninsula.” The ministry has said it wants to gather peace-related […]
items.body_text:
South Korea’s Ministry of Unification will hold its first Peace Wind Week starting Sept. 11, 2026, an 11-day series of public events, including a DMZ peace walk and academic forums, organized under the slogan “The peace I want, toward a peace wind for the Korean Peninsula.” The ministry has said it wants to gather peace-related events that individual agencies and regions previously held separately into a single period, raising public interest and spreading a shared sense of support for peace on the Korean Peninsula.
Peace is a good word. No one prefers war to peace, and coexistence is better than confrontation, dialogue better than military tension. Creating space for the public, especially young people, to talk about the future of inter-Korean relations has real value. That is exactly why more caution is needed. A pleasant-sounding word can become the most convenient way to paper over an uncomfortable reality.
This year’s government roadmap, the 2026 Basic Direction for Peace, Unification and Democratic Citizenship Education, shifted the paradigm of unification education toward “peace, unification and democratic citizenship.” It named cultivating peace awareness and democratic citizenship as core goals, declared that “the starting point of unification is peace,” and pledged to build an environment that draws out students’ critical thinking and reasoned debate. The direction itself has merit, moving away from one-directional lessons on the necessity of unification and toward students thinking and arguing for themselves.
But that shift raises a question that cannot be avoided: can critical thinking be taught without accurately showing today’s North Korea?
North Korea is already rewriting the language it uses to describe its relationship with the South. This year’s revised constitution deleted long-standing phrases such as “the northern half,” “unification of the fatherland” and “independent, peaceful unification and great national unity.” A new territorial clause describes South Korea as a separate state sharing a border with the North. The constitution stops short of the blunter language Kim Jong Un has used elsewhere, such as calling the South the “principal hostile state,” but North Korea has clearly moved a considerable distance from the ethnic-nation, unification-centered framing it once used to describe inter-Korean relations.
If North Korea is erasing the language of unification while South Korea’s unification education simply repeats the word peace more loudly, students will naturally ask why they are still being taught to pursue unification with a North Korea that no longer talks about it. Unification education should not fear that question. It should start there. The moment education avoids a question, it loses its persuasive power. Teaching peace without acknowledging North Korea’s changes, and teaching unification while dwelling only on North Korea’s threat, both show just half the picture. If a peace wind is going to blow, it needs to blow over reality, not around it.
Unification education must follow reality’s hardest questions
Teach the North Korea that exists, not the one people wish for
The danger in unification education is not limited to teaching false facts. Selectively presenting only the reality one prefers is equally risky. The emphasis of South Korean unification education has swung considerably depending on the administration and the moment: security and threat at some points, reconciliation and cooperation at others, exchange and community when inter-Korean relations improved, and North Korea’s threat again when relations soured.
North Korea, however, does not change according to South Korea’s election cycle. What students need to learn is not a North Korea edited to fit one political lens, but the North Korea that exists right now. items.title: North Korea’s meth prices surge as drug trafficking crackdown intensifies
items.summary: North Korea’s crackdown on drug trafficking has intensified sharply this year. The tightened enforcement has shrunk methamphetamine distribution networks, and it has driven prices for the drug sharply higher, according to a source with knowledge of the country’s northern border region. A source in North Pyongan province told Daily NK on Tuesday that police have […]
items.body_text:
North Korea’s crackdown on drug trafficking has intensified sharply this year. The tightened enforcement has shrunk methamphetamine distribution networks, and it has driven prices for the drug sharply higher, according to a source with knowledge of the country’s northern border region.
A source in North Pyongan province told Daily NK on Tuesday that police have recently launched a sweeping crackdown on drug-related crimes. The effort is concentrated in areas along the North Korea-China border, and it has made methamphetamine, known locally as “bingdu,” far harder to obtain than before.
Methamphetamine use became widespread in North Korea in the 1990s, when the drug was manufactured domestically and traded informally as the state-run economy collapsed during a devastating famine. It remains one of the most commonly abused substances in the country today.
Until just a year or two ago, people in the region could obtain the drug fairly easily through merchants who specialized in handling and distributing it, the source said. Under the current crackdown, though, those merchants have largely disappeared from view, and the drug trade itself has contracted sharply.
In the past, most people caught distributing or selling the drug could bribe the police officer who caught them and avoid serious consequences. Officers who accept bribes now face harsher scrutiny themselves, the source said, and that method of avoiding punishment no longer works.
Meth prices climb sharply as supply networks shrink
As the crackdown has squeezed distribution networks, prices for methamphetamine have climbed sharply. A single dose once sold for 100 to 200 Chinese yuan, or roughly $15 to $30, the source said, and it now regularly tops 500 yuan, or about $75.
Demand for the drug remains steady, the source explained, but supply has fallen sharply as the risk of arrest and the severity of punishment have both increased, and that imbalance has driven prices upward across the board.
The source added that instances of drug misuse among North Korean people have noticeably declined as a result. Methamphetamine has long been used informally in the country as a stimulant or as a substitute for painkillers.
That pattern now appears to be fading as the drug grows scarcer and far more expensive. “In the past, plenty of people would reach for bingdu instead of medicine when they felt sick or run down,” the source said.
“But now, with prices this high and the fear of getting caught, people don’t seek it out the way they used to.” Prices have climbed so high that even a single dose is hard to afford, the source said.
As a result, people who had used the drug habitually are cutting back or quitting altogether. Authorities appear to be tightening drug enforcement for two overlapping reasons.
One is to curb the spread of drug misuse among North Korean people. The other is to dismantle the informal distribution networks that have taken root in the country’s border regions.
North Pyongan, Ryanggang and North Hamgyong provinces all border China, and they have long served as key conduits for drug trafficking and other informal trade. Authorities appear to be concentrating enforcement resources there in an effort to root out distribution networks entirely.
“Border areas along the river have always been a hub for the drug trade, so enforcement there has always been far more intense than inland,” the source said. “Now, the closer you get to the border, the harsher the crackdown, to the point where people are afraid to even say the word ‘bingdu’ out loud.”

items.title: North Melbourne's 32-game winning streak over after shock loss to Hawthorn
items.summary: North Melbourne has lost for the first time in almost three years, with the two-time defending AFLW premier falling to a shock 7-point defeat to Hawthorn in Cairns.
items.body_text:
North Melbourne's record AFLW winning streak is over, with the Kangaroos falling to a shock 7-point defeat to Hawthorn in Cairns.
The defeat ended a run of 32 consecutive wins for North, an V/AFL and AFLW record.
Hawks midfielder Jasmine Fleming starred with 25 disposals in the absence of injured captain Emily Bates.
North Melbourne's record 32-matchwinning streak is over after Hawthorn pulled off a massive AFLW upset.
The Hawks' 4.8 (32) to 3.7 (25) win on Friday night in Cairns is their greatest win since they joined the women's league in 2022.
The Kangaroos' sequence of straight wins is the longest in AFL, VFL and AFLW history. They had not been beaten since 2023, going undefeated in their 2024 and 2025 premiership runs.
Hawthorn's Jacqueline Dupuy said the feeling was "unreal".
"In my head, I was just panicking, thinking, 'How long have we got?' I reckon I looked at the bench three or four times in the last 90 seconds, just praying for the siren," Dupuy told ABC Sport.
"It was pretty unreal when it finally went. And to be able to look around at these girls I love so much and just see the sheer joy and feel that myself was amazing."
Loading Twitter content
Hawthorn's win was made even more impressive given the absence of captain Emily Bates, who went down with an ACL rupture last weekend.
The triumph came off the back of relentless pressure.
North led by 10 points at the main break in blustery and humid Cairns conditions, but Hawthorn's Mikayla Williamson kicked the only goal of the third term, pulling the match to within three points.
Four straight behinds gave Hawthorn the lead in the last term for the first time since the first quarter. Cairns native Jacqueline Dupuy then kicked a goal to give Hawthorn a seven-point buffer at nine minutes.
But North was not done, with Blaithin Bogue kicking a goal against the run of play.
Inside the last two minutes, Hawks ruck Lucy Wales snapped the sealing goal.
"It's just a credit to the kind of player Lucy is. She's clutch. She is one of the most consistent players for us and I just feel like it was very fitting that she was able to kick that winning goal," Dupuy said.
North's last loss was the 2023 grand final against Brisbane. The Kangaroos then started the 2024 season with a win and a draw, before starting their historic streak.
Friday night's tally was also their lowest score since 2023.
It is a great start to the weekend for the Hawks, ahead of Saturday's AFL preliminary final against Brisbane, when they will also start as underdogs against the two-time defending premiers.
The AFLW victory puts the team just outside the top four.
"It's always tough to go to sleep after a game, and certainly feeling pretty jacked right now," Dupuy said.
"But I'm sure we'll get a rest and go up again in six days, which would be exciting to head down to Geelong."

items.title: New ‘world’s best airline’ crowned as Qantas fails to crack top 10
items.summary: Qatar Airways has lost the title of world’s best airline at the 2026 World Airline Awards, in a year when the highly regarded Middle East carrier has been disrupted by conflict in its region.
items.body_text:
New ‘world’s best airline’ crowned as Qantas fails to crack top 10
Qatar Airways has lost the title of world’s best airline at the 2026 World Airline Awards, in a year when the highly regarded Middle East carrier has been disrupted by conflict in its region.
Qatar was pipped by Singapore Airlines for the Airline of the Year, which took out the No.1 spot after the Gulf carrier won the previous two years.
Qatar Airways took second place – the position held by Singapore Airlines last year. It’s the sixth time Singapore Airlines has taken out the top award, a feat surpassed only by Qatar, which has won nine times.
Qantas, meanwhile, climbed two places from 14th to 12th this year, still far below its historical results where it consistently ranked in the top five, including as recently as 2022. However, the airline has continued to climb back from its nadir in 2024, where it fell to 24th amid a series of scandals including illegally sacking staff, selling fares for flights that had already been cancelled and criticisms over the availability of rewards seats for Frequent Flyer members.
Among Australia’s other airlines, Virgin Australian dropped three places to 37th, while Jetstar stayed in 88th place.
Sign up for the Traveller newsletter
The latest travel news, tips and inspiration delivered to your inbox. Sign up now.
As usual, Asian and Middle Eastern airlines dominated the top 10, with Hong Kong’s Cathay Pacific in third and Japan’s All Nippon Airways (ANA) in fourth. Rounding the top five was Turkish Airlines, which started flights between Australia and Istanbul via Asia in 2024 and plans non-stop flights between Australia and Turkey next year.
Singapore Airlines also won the award for world’s best economy class and best economy class catering, and was runner-up business class (behind Qatar Airways) and first class (behind Air France).
The airline reported record revenue of $6.28 billion for the first quarter of this financial year, even as it slumped to an $83 million net loss due to conflict in the Middle East causing fuel prices to surge.
This year a new award, for best onboard Wi-Fi, went to Qatar Airways. It was the only category in which US airlines dominated, taking all other slots in the top five behind Qatar (Delta Air Lines, United, Alaska Airlines and JetBlue).
The World Airline Awards are based on online customer-satisfaction surveys conducted by consultancy firm Skytrax, with passengers from 100 countries taking part and more than 350 airlines featuring in the final results. Skytrax claims the awards are based on the world’s largest airline satisfaction survey.
Some aviation experts have questioned Skytrax’s methodology and the lack of transparency in its awards process. According to some reports, Skytrax has refused to answer questions related to how its survey system works or even what the business actually does.
Airlines, however, are quick to trumpet the results when favourable.

items.summary: Simon Peter Carman appeared in a Pattaya court on Friday charged with killing Tunchanok Donhomla An Australian man accused of murdering a Thai teenager and putting her body in a suitcase pleaded not guilty on Friday in a hearing in the seaside resort city of Pattaya, a court official said.Simon Peter Carman, 45, was arrested in June after 17-year-old Tunchanok Donhomla was reported missing in Pattaya City, about 150km south-east of Bangkok. items.body_text:
An Australian man accused of murdering a Thai teenager and putting her body in a suitcase pleaded not guilty on Friday in a hearing in the seaside resort city of Pattaya, a court official said.
Simon Peter Carman, 45, was arrested in June after 17-year-old Tunchanok Donhomla was reported missing in Pattaya City, about 150km south-east of Bangkok. A suitcase containing her body was found shortly after.
Police said she died of suffocation.
Carman appeared on Friday at Pattaya provincial court, where he pleaded not guilty to all charges, a court spokesperson said.
He had been charged with murder, concealing a body and taking a minor for indecent purposes. The next court date was set for 12 October.
Police previously said CCTV footage showed him entering a condominium in Pattaya with the girl in the early hours of 25 June, and leaving that evening carrying a large black suitcase.
In a police interrogation video shared online by Thai media, Carman has said he was acting in self-defence because the girl was threatening him with a knife.
The case put the spotlight on Pattaya, which is popular with foreign tourists for its beaches and nightlife, but also has a reputation for sex tourism.

items.title: Swimmer dies after being bitten by shark off popular Perth beach
items.summary: Locals describe their shock at witnessing the incident at Sorrento Beach on Friday morningFollow our Australia news live blog for latest updatesGet our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcastA man has died after being bitten by a shark off Sorrento Beach in Perth’s north.Emergency services were called to the popular beach at about 10.30am on Friday after reports of a shark-related incident. Continue reading...
items.body_text:
A man has died after being bitten by a shark off Sorrento Beach in Perth’s north.
Emergency services were called to the popular beach at about 10.30am on Friday after reports of a shark-related incident.
Western Australia police said a man had been bitten by a shark while swimming along the coast. He died as a result of his injuries, police said.
Emergency services, including water and air personnel, conducted an extensive search of the area. The swimmer’s body has not been found.
The Alkimos Surf Life Saving Club said Sorrento Beach will remain closed until 12pm on Saturday. Locals have been urged to stay out of the water until the beach was declared safe for swimming.
The City of Wanneroo has closed all other beaches along its coastline until 12pm on Saturday.
The local state MP, Liam Staltari, extended his condolences to the man’s family, friends and loved ones.
“Like all locals and people from across WA, I’m deeply saddened by the tragic death of a man following today’s shark attack at Sorrento Beach,” he said.
“Our entire community is thinking of you at this incredibly difficult time.”
A witness, Darrel Haythornthwaite, told 7News that he could not believe the incident had occurred, “especially in a place like this”. He said the man’s friend, who was swimming with him, made it back to shore but was inconsolable.
“He felt bad because he didn’t go back to save his mate and I said, ‘Nah you couldn’t have done that’,” he told the outlet. “There’s nothing that anyone could have done.”
Another witness, Ingrid Mitchell, told 9News she swam at the beach every day and did not expect sharks to attack outside of dawn and dusk.
“There was other swimmers in there … just near the seaweed, and there was one poor girl there who was sun-baking, and she saw the whole lot as well,” she said.
A third witness, Jacqui Rapaic, told the ABC she was walking along the beach with a friend when the incident occurred.
“My friend said, ‘Jac, I think there’s been a shark attack’ and I looked out to the ocean and I could see a pool of blood,” she said.
“I hugged onto my friend … [we] felt rather traumatised at that point. It happened so quickly.”
The fatality follows a shark attack on Monday at the remote Glenfield Beach, north of Geraldton on WA’s mid-west coast, which left a surfer with serious injuries.
He was taken to the nearby Geraldton health campus and is in a stable condition.
- with AAP

items.title: Andrew Hastie says AI advised him to reply ‘congratulations!’ to man who planned to end life with assisted dying
items.summary: Liberal MP speaks of AI’s shortcomings as cyber chief tells inquiry the tech is needed to fend off ‘highly capable malicious cyber actors’Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcastWhen a man with a terminal illness wrote to his local MP Andrew Hastie, telling him he planned on ending his own life with voluntary assisted dying, Microsoft Copilot suggested Hastie reply with “congratulations!”, “great to hear from you” or “that is wonderful news!”.Hastie shared the episode at a par
items.body_text:
When a man with a terminal illness wrote to his local MP Andrew Hastie, telling him he planned on ending his own life with voluntary assisted dying, Microsoft Copilot suggested Hastie reply with “congratulations!”, “great to hear from you” or “that is wonderful news!”.
Hastie shared the episode at a parliamentary inquiry on Friday to underline the shortcomings of the American-run software as he called for AI run by Australians.
The hearing offered the some of the most detailed explanations of the Albanese government’s desire to bring Anthropic and OpenAI to Australia, in the face of calls to slow them down or shut them out.
The defence establishment told the inquiry that cutting the companies out could be catastrophic.
Abigail Bradshaw, the director general of the Australian Signals Directorate, said her agents needed advanced AI every day to fend off “highly capable malicious cyber actors”.
“If a digital adversary has access to newer, more capable models than we do, they may be able to identify and exploit vulnerabilities in systems and networks before we can identify them,” Bradshaw said.
But Australia’s top cyber-intelligence agency is “entirely reliant” on US-housed processing and would “dramatically” lose capability if cut off in a conflict, Bradshaw said.
The defence department’s chief AI officer, Chris Crozier, said the government was already trying to keep its tech needs local, contracting Google to build a series of interlinked datacentres spread across the country and disconnected from the US.
“Somebody can’t wake up and have a bad day and decide they’re going to turn it off,” Crozier said.
“We do not want to be using AI tool sets that are located offshore … we want the compute, we want the application, we want the data, we want the decision making, all based in Australia.”
Bringing big tech into the country would make the job much easier, he said, and not just by allowing the army to protect and maintain its datacentres.
The Office of AI, set up in the prime minister’s department, said bringing firms under Australian law would make it easier for local law enforcement to combat threats on the platforms.
Tight conditions on access could also materially improve Australia’s chances of using and defending itself with the best AI tools in the world, the inquiry heard.
“We will get more assured access, earlier access, more detailed technical access, and better integration with technical experts at the frontier,” Bradshaw said.
These would be assured by strict requirements on any top developers looking to train models in Australia, such as demanding government oversight and early access to advanced models, she suggested.
The government is already planning to set the rules for companies that come here. It is consulting on standards that would force AI companies to report issues and breaches and potentially reserve some computational power for local research.
Large datacentres will have to engage with communities, build away from schools and homes, and underwrite new renewables in most states.
Another pillar of the standards – copyright law – is yet to be settled, with AI developers refusing to train models here without law reform.
A proposal to give the companies access to everything Australians create online by default sparked a wave of backlash from creatives, who say the companies could pay for local licensing deals to access Australian content.
But Jenna Priestly, the assistant secretary at the attorney general’s department, on Friday confirmed looser copyright laws would also affect AI access to foreign-made content distributed in Australia.
She said the companies wanted to train models on “maybe billions” of pieces of information and claimed it was practically “impossible” to make deals with every rights holder.
“As Australia’s copyright framework protects not only copyright material that’s Australian in origin, but worldwide, I think it is a fairly large number that [companies] would need to go and strike deals with,”

items.title: Canada's top general is up for a senior NATO post. Will Trump get in her way?
items.summary: Canada's Gen. Jennie Carignan faces Germany's Gen. Carsten Breuer on Saturday in a secret-ballot contest to chair NATO's Military Committee. A victory would make Carignan the first woman to hold the post and return Canada to the chair after nearly two decades, amid Ottawa's push for deeper ties with Europe.
items.body_text:
Canada's top general is up for a senior NATO post. Will Trump get in her way?
Alliance holding secret ballot on Saturday to choose Military Committee chair
Top military commanders from 32 Western nations will vote Saturday on whether they prefer Canada's chief of the defence staff or her German counterpart to lead a significant NATO committee.
Gen. Jennie Carignan and Gen. Carsten Breuer are vying for the top job at the NATO Military Committee, a post not held by a Canadian in almost two decades.
The Liberal government of Prime Minister Mark Carney has thrown its weight behind her candidacy. The election at a meeting of alliance chiefs of defence staff comes as Canada and Europe explore closer political, economic and defence co-operation.
If elected, Carignan will be the first woman to lead the military committee in the 77-year history of the alliance.
- Canada wants into Britain's rapid-response defence club
- EU chief says she wants Canada to become the bloc's 1st associate member
In an interview with CBC News, Carignan said it's "a privilege to be considered," especially at a time when the alliance faces heightened tensions with Russia, hybrid attacks and the war in Ukraine.
"Don't get me wrong. I absolutely know what I'm getting myself into, but such an important time to work with NATO as partners," Carignan said. "And I think I can make a difference in that way."
Carignan said she was encouraged to put her name forward by some of her fellow defence chiefs.
The chair of NATO's Military Committee is the alliance's senior military officer and, in practical terms, the bridge between NATO's political leadership and its military commanders.
The committee assesses threats, capabilities and operational requirements and provides military advice to the North Atlantic Council. The current chair is Italian Admiral Giuseppe Cavo Dragone, who took office in January 2025.
The position of chair is different from the more high-profile Supreme Allied Commander Europe (SACEUR) which is responsible for operations and potential warfighting.
The vote comes following Carney's visit to Strasbourg, France, this week where European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen proposed the idea of Canada becoming the EU's first "associate member." It's unclear precisely what that kind of status could mean but it has the potential to substantially deepen economic and political integration.
- Carney wants Canada to join Europe's Erasmus+ program. What is it?
- Far-right German politician heckles Carney with 'U.S.A.' chant before EU address
Carney welcomed the proposal. Donald Trump did not.
The U.S. president, on the one hand, called it "laughable" but then also described it as a potentially "hostile act" that would prompt more tariffs.
Steve Saideman, a defence expert at Carleton University who has written extensively on NATO, said Carignan "absolutely has a shot" at the committee chair's position.
"I think that Carney probably did his homework and wouldn't put the name forward if she didn't have a chance," said Saideman, who added the geopolitical timing is extraordinary.
"I also think that Canada, right now, is being highly sought after by the Europeans to be anchored in all kinds of European structures. So, I think it's a possibility."
There is, however, also the possibility the Trump administration could attempt to block consensus, said Saideman.
"Trump is not going to let a Canadian or a woman be the head of the military committee, if anybody around him has paid attention to it," he said.
"He's very upset at Canada for daring to actually have agency. His reaction yesterday to the news about associate membership suggests that he'll find any opportunity, particularly one that is as relatively cost-free as this, to block Canada from whatever aspirations it has."
The election of chair is decided by majority vote in a secret ballot among the defence chiefs. The vote takes place during a closed, private session of the committee.

items.title: Germany's far-right AfD party copied Trump's playbook and won. It now hopes to use it to govern
items.summary: From creating a deportation task force to revising history lessons in schools, the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party, which won a resounding victory in the state of Saxony-Anhlat last week and could soon hold power, wants to implement policies that echo some of those enacted by U.S. President Donald Trump.
items.body_text:
Germany's far-right AfD party copied Trump's playbook and won. It now hopes to use it to govern
After strong showing in state election, AfD has 1st chance to govern and is looking to U.S. for inspiration
Christian Machek is at a rally for the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party in Berlin. Despite backing a nationalist party thousands of kilometres from the United States, he considers himself both an AfD and "Trump supporter."
The AfD secured a resounding victory in a recent regional election in the eastern German state of Saxony-Anhalt, where the party is designated as right-wing extremist by the local domestic intelligence agency.
U.S. President Donald Trump celebrated the win on social media.
"I was happy [Trump] congratulated the AfD for a good campaign," said Machek, an Austrian Belgian citizen who lives in Berlin and says he works with the party in Germany’s parliament, the Bundestag, as an assistant to its spokesperson on religious affairs.
Ahead of Sunday's Berlin state election, the AfD party is polling just three points behind first place, according to a Sept. 10 survey conducted by German election research company Infratest-Dimap.
Machek, who also works for Europa Aeterna, which describes itself as a conservative political philosophy association rooted in Christianity, said the AfD is instilling a sense of patriotism and hope for the future. He sees Trump as a strong leader who also inspires national pride.
"I'm a Trump supporter from the beginning," said Machek. "It's a good sign. Just gives us hope that we're not alone."
The AfD fell just short of securing an absolute majority in Saxony-Anhalt, but it still has a chance of becoming the first far-right party to hold state power since the Second World War. In Germany, governments are usually run by a coalition of parties, meaning the AfD will need co-operation from other political parties or individual elected representatives to govern.
- Far-right victory in German state expected to send shockwaves throughout the world
- AnalysisGermany's AFD could become 1st far-right party to hold state power since WWII. What could that mean?
AfD politicians cite Trump as the inspiration for some of their cultural policies, an area the party will control if it successfully forms government. They've even used the catchphrase "Make Saxony-Anhalt Great Again" on the campaign trail, an echo of Trump's MAGA slogan.
Although many AfD talking points pre-date Trump, the populist party is one of several around the world for which the U.S. president has provided a blueprint for how to gain mainstream support.
"Trump represents a model … of how you can whip up the base, how you can make electoral gains, and maybe even how you can seize power," said Eric Langenbacher, a political scientist with the American-German Institute in Washington, D.C.
"The fact that he's shown that what people thought were fantastical policies can actually be implemented, I think that is the biggest impact that he's had on the AfD, on Germany, and on many other countries as well."
Hard line on immigration
Langenbacher said some of the AfD's strict immigration policies echo those implemented by the Trump administration.
In Saxony-Anhalt, the AfD has said it wants to strip citizenship from immigrants who commit crimes, expand detention centres for deportees and create a "deportation task force," a term Trump started using during his 2016 presidential campaign.
"Sometimes, I feel like in Saxony-Anhalt, they just cut and paste from Project 2025," said Langenbacher, referring to the policy blueprint from the Heritage Foundation, a conservative think-tank, that has inspired some of Trump's efforts to reshape government and immigration enforcement.
The similarities between Trump and the AfD are evident to Anne-Christin Richter, 43, who lived and worked for a commercial vehicle manufacturer in Detroit for 10 years. She recently moved back to her hometown of Magdeburg, Saxony-Anhalt's capital.

items.title: Philippines school shooting leaves 2 students, gunman dead
items.summary: Three students were killed in a school shooting in the southern Philippines on Friday, including a 16-year-old suspected gunman who turned the gun on himself, provincial officials said.
items.body_text:
Philippines school shooting leaves 2 students, gunman dead
8 others injured in incident in Banga, South Cotabato
Three students were killed in a school shooting in the southern Philippines on Friday, including a 16-year-old suspected gunman who turned the gun on himself, provincial officials said.
Eight others were injured, with four in critical condition, and all the victims were students aged 14 to 17, said Albert Palencia, mayor of Banga town in South Cotabato, where the shooting took place.
"The suspect supposedly sat beside his friends and told them to go home 'because after lunch, I will be executing my plan.' His friends laughed because the shooter was a known joker," Palencia told Reuters.
"After lunch, he started shooting students. He hit 10 students before killing himself," Palencia added.
In a separate interview with DZBB radio, Palencia said the suspected gunman appeared to have fired indiscriminately at students in a classroom next to his own after leaving his Grade 9 classroom.
Palencia said the suspect used a 9-mm pistol belonging to his father, a Department of Education employee, after breaking into a vault where the firearm had been stored and bringing it to school.
Cluster of school shootings
South Cotabato Gov. Reynaldo Tamayo urged parents to ensure guns were kept out of reach of minors.
"We need to be responsible in storing firearms. Gun owners, in particular, must make sure that minors do not have access to them," Tamayo told Reuters by phone.
"We cannot expect a handful of security personnel to monitor thousands of students. We need to work together because otherwise this will be very difficult for us to address."
The incident follows two fatal gun incidents since June at schools in the Philippines, where school shootings were previously rare.
Last month, a student livestreamed himself shooting and killing another student in a classroom in Zamboanga, in the country's south, before taking his own life.
In June, at least three students were killed and about 20 others injured in an attack at a public high school in Tacloban, where two classmates opened fire on campus.
The Philippines has relatively strict gun ownership regulations, including background checks and psychological evaluation requirements, although illegal firearms remain in circulation.

items.title: In a U.S. and Mexican war on screwworm, horse smugglers expose cracks in the front
items.summary: Flies that prey on cattle are making a comeback, and the illicit animal trade can help them hitch a ride north
items.body_text:
When sheriff’s deputies intercepted a trailer carrying six horses near the border town of Redford, Texas, they uncovered more than a livestock violation. The animals had crossed the Rio Grande illegally from Mexico through a shadowy smuggling network, bypassing the veterinary inspections, health certifications and quarantine measures that the U.S. requires for livestock.
Smuggled animals are coming into focus as possible hosts for New World screwworm. The flesh-eating parasite began infesting U.S. cattle in June despite efforts to halt the spread, such as a U.S. ban of more than a year on Mexican livestock, a team of government inspectors on horseback and a swarm of sterile flies.
The horses caught near Redford in late May were not infested, but the case highlights a little-enforced part of the U.S. response to the threat. As U.S. authorities restricted cattle imports and disrupted billions of dollars in trade to contain the fly, a cartel-linked trade in horses and other animals continued moving through remote stretches of the border.
Redford, Texas, was one of several border communities where Reuters learned about illicit animal smuggling, and the risk that horses could carry screwworm north.
Reuters
For more than a year, U.S. officials have argued that illegal livestock trafficking from Central America helped carry screwworm north. But Reuters found illicit animal movements have also persisted along parts of the U.S.-Mexico border, often taking the same routes used to smuggle drugs and people.
The stakes are enormous. A previous screwworm outbreak killed thousands of animals in the U.S. before the pest was declared eradicated in the 1960s.
In Texas, where authorities confirmed the first new U.S. animal cases this year, experts estimate a widespread outbreak could cost the economy up to US$1.8-billion.
The Trump administration has partially reopened the border to Mexican livestock to bring relief to U.S. consumers, with beef prices at record highs after the ban, despite rising infestations in Mexico.
U.S. Department of Agriculture officials, law enforcement and animal-industry experts said smuggled animals range from high-value horses bought for racing and rodeos to dogs used in illegal fighting rings and cattle. Authorities have also intercepted exotic animals, including primates, bears and tigers in recent years.
Mexico’s animal health agency Senasica has confirmed over 2,000 equine cases of screwworm since the outbreak started in 2024.
“These kinds of movements represent a risk because they allow the fly to travel much faster than it could move naturally,” said Oscar Rico, a researcher at Universidad Nacional Autonoma de Mexico, who co-authored a study predicting how animals could spread screwworm.
During a week in August, Reuters visited three remote communities along the Texas-Mexico border, joined patrols with local officers and interviewed sheriffs, veterinarians and former Border Patrol agents.
They described the challenge of policing hundreds of miles of rugged terrain where animals, drugs and people can cross undetected.
Presidio County Sergeant Deputy Sheriff Jaime Sanchez, who investigated the Redford case, said trafficked horses can fetch at least $30,000 on the black market, with smugglers able to undercut legal sellers by avoiding import paperwork, taxes and veterinary requirements.
Smugglers often take the horses to Houston and Dallas, where they sell them for farm work, racing or charrería, Mexico’s traditional equestrian sport.
Mr. Sanchez’s department has intercepted more than 50 smuggled horses in the past two years by pulling over horse trailers, an unusual sight in the dry, border community of Presidio, Texas.

items.title: Hundreds of thousands of Iranians participate in government-organized rally
items.summary: Government stresses national unity as economy worsens under U.S. naval blockade and sanctions
items.body_text:
Hundreds of thousands of Iranians rallied Friday in a government-organized show of defiance after months of war, pledging their readiness to take up arms in the biggest such demonstration since the United States and Israel attacked in February.
Iran’s government has sought to rally the people and stress national unity, even as the economy worsens under a U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports and new U.S. sanctions meant to increase Tehran’s economic pain.
Estimates varied of the number of people volunteering to receive limited military training and defend the country in an effort described as “Janfaday-e Iran,” or the “ones who sacrifice their lives for Iran.” They marched through downtown Tehran in combat uniform, carrying flags, as onlookers cheered.
UN mission finds U.S. may have committed war crimes in Iran, and Tehran crimes against humanity
For days, state media have encouraged Iranians to join the campaign, saying training with assault rifles would begin soon. The volunteers would be an additional layer of security to the powerful Revolutionary Guard paramilitary and its all-volunteer arm, the Basij.
Tehran’s Guard chief, Gen. Hassan Hassanzadeh, told the state broadcaster that over 600,000 people had registered to participate, with over 1 million expected to take part in the training. On Friday morning, the broadcaster estimated over 300,000 people were on the streets.
The new head of the Basij, Hossein Taeb, declared in a speech as the rally began that the volunteers will be ready for “full-fledged defence” and similar rallies will take place in other cities soon.
The new trainees will make a “nightmare” for Iran’s enemies, Taeb added, as President Masoud Pezeshkian, military commanders and other senior officials watched the march.
Some participants trampled flags of the U.S. and Israel. Others chanted “Death to America” and “Death to Israel.”
“I am here to tell [U.S. President Donald] Trump that we Iranians have no fear about his threats against our homeland,” said Marzieh Afaghi, 24, who attended the rally with her toddler and husband. “No one in history could invade Iran and remain there.”
The rally was also a chance for Iran to show off military hardware. Anti-aircraft batteries were on display, while female Guard members in black head scarves sat with truck-mounted machine guns.
The Guard displayed drones that have been widely used against ships in the Strait of Hormuz, where Iran has asserted control since the war began, severely affecting the Gulf region’s shipments of oil and natural gas to the rest of the world.
Volunteers could help suppress future dissent
Friday’s events also suggested that hard-liners like Taeb among Iran’s leadership will be more prepared to suppress any future demonstration against the theocracy.
In January, shortly before the war, Iran saw some of its largest nationwide protests in history, which began over the struggling economy and turned to wider grievances. Activists have said a crackdown killed over 7,000 people and saw tens of thousands detained.
In May, government officials said more than 30 million people in Iran – home to a population of some 90 million – had volunteered via an online form or at public gatherings to lay down their lives for the theocracy. The Associated Press could not independently confirm that.

items.title: More than 100,000 Yemenis displaced as conflict escalates, thousands flee to Djibouti
items.summary: UN International Organization for Migration says people are fleeing on overcrowded boats and arriving with very limited food and water
items.body_text:
At least 112,000 people have been displaced inside Yemen within the last two weeks as fighting continues along the country’s west coast amid a renewed conflict, while nearly 3,000 have fled by sea to Djibouti, the United Nations migration agency said on Friday.
Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis have stepped up attacks on Saudi cities and energy infrastructure while advancing along Yemen’s Red Sea coast towards the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a key shipping route. Responding to the Houthi offensive, the Saudi and Yemeni air forces have bombarded Houthi targets.
Nearly 3,000 people have crossed the Gulf of Aden to Djibouti in the Horn of Africa in less than a week as escalating violence have forced more families to flee, Sandrine Desamours, the representative for the UN’s refugee agency, UNHCR, told reporters in Geneva via video link from Djibouti.
The government of Djibouti is preparing for the arrival of up to 10,000 refugees – which will add acute pressure on the country’s health care and education services, she said.
Saudis and Houthis trade strikes as Yemenis take to boats to flee fighting as war spreads
The UN International Organization for Migration said people are fleeing on overcrowded boats and arriving with very limited food and water. Most fleeing are Yemeni families seeking refuge in Djibouti, but IOM is also beginning to see a small number of migrants, mainly from Ethiopia, heading in the same direction.
Additionally, authorities in Somaliland and Puntland have also reported increased arrivals from Yemen, including Yemeni refugees and Somali refugee returnees, though numbers remain in the hundreds for now, UNHCR said.
UN agencies described the latest fighting as being a crisis on top of multiple crises as the country’s health services and economy have been shattered amid a long civil war between forces of the internationally recognized, Saudi-backed administration and the Houthis created one of the world’s biggest humanitarian crises.
The Houthi advance along Yemen’s Red Sea coast is bolstering Tehran’s hand in its conflict with the US, as the group tightens its control of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a strategic chokepoint for global oil and commodities shipping, more than six months after U.S. and Israeli attacks on Iran.

Cook This: 3 recipes from Mexican Soul, including cheesy, melty choriqueso
Santiago Lastra takes a creative approach to Mexican cooking — using ingredients available at any grocery store
Our cookbook of the week is Mexican Soul by Santiago Lastra, written with support from his brother, Eduardo Lastra.
Jump to the recipes:choriqueso, albóndigas (meatballs) and butternut squash aguachile.
Recommended Videos
Chef Santiago Lastra takes his native cuisine to unexpected places in his cookbook debut, Mexican Soul (Quadrille, 2026). Using pistachios to make guacamole and mashed potatoes to make tortillas, he shows that Mexican cooking isn’t bound to a set of ingredients. It’s a state of mind.
“My dream is to be able to showcase the quality of Mexican cooking, but also just the diversity of it,” says Lastra. “There’s an opportunity for people to make their food a little bit more Mexican, but more than just using very traditional recipes.”
The first part of the book focuses on the foundations of Mexican food, with traditional recipes that illustrate its core elements. In the second part, Lastra features “Mexican Soul Recipes,” all of which use ingredients available in supermarkets year-round.
“I realized that I don’t cook as much Mexican food at home myself, and it’s always been this limitation of being outside Mexico that I believed was the problem,” says Lastra, who was born in Mexico City, raised in Cuernavaca and lives in London, England. “But actually, it’s a combination of that, and just the way that we’re introduced to Mexican cooking that can sometimes be very complicated.”
Lastra saw an opportunity to tell a story about the ease and accessibility of Mexican food — one that he says has already been established with other cuisines, such as Italian. If you have pasta, tomatoes, olive oil and garlic, you can make Italian food. “My question was, ‘Can Mexican food be like that?’ Can Mexican food be done with three or four ingredients — and quick?”

-   Cook This: 3 recipes from Chocolate Baking, including a lazy baked Alaska

Take the potato, for instance. Lastra considers sourcing fresh masa (made from ground nixtamalized corn) and its preparations, such as sopas, tamales and tortillas, the greatest obstacle to cooking Mexican food outside of Mexico. “And the biggest challenge is being solved by the ingredient that everyone has — that is potatoes,” he says. After years of research, Lastra landed on masa made with mashed potato and potato starch as a readily available alternative.
“The tortillas puff, and they’re delicious, and they taste like mashed potatoes, but they have the texture of the tortillas.”
In the first part of the book, Lastra “untangles” Mexican food by explaining what it is, how it tastes and sharing the “unwritten rules” that are common knowledge among Mexican cooks, along with traditional recipes.
“It couldn’t be a Mexican cookbook without a guacamole made with avocados or a quesadilla made with corn masa or carnitas,” says Lastra. With Mexican Soul, he wanted to give people a foundation to build on, and then an invitation to play. “It’s hard to have innovative or different recipes if you don’t understand the source of what the tradition looks like.”
In restaurants, the more you strive to create something unique, the more complicated things become, says Lastra. Writing the book reconnected him to what it means to cook at home — to nourish and bring people together with limitations that don’t exist in fine dining.
“It feels very nice because you can cook with less. And you can make things that are quick, delicious, beautiful and Mexican, but without having to overcomplicate (things),” says Lastra. “This book is helping me understand food on such a different level, and now I do all these recipes all the time.”
